Trilium limits each IP address to 10 failed sign-in attempts in 15 minutes. Once an address reaches the limit, Trilium rejects every further attempt from it, including correct ones, until the 15 minutes have passed. The sign-in page then shows __TRILIUM_PH_0__Too many login attempts__TRILIUM_PH_1__; other clients receive HTTP status 429.
The limit applies to every way of signing in with the password:
Setting up __TRILIUM_PH_0__Synchronization__TRILIUM_PH_1__ from a desktop or mobile app.
Connecting the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Web Clipper__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or the Android sender app.
All of these count toward the same limit, and a wrong password, a wrong one-time password and a wrong recovery code each count as one failed attempt. Successful sign-ins are not counted.
The limit is per IP address, not per account, so an attacker cannot lock you out by failing to sign in from their own address. The count is kept in memory: restarting the server clears it.

Behind a reverse proxy, Trilium sees every request as coming from the proxy unless it is configured as a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Trusted proxy__TRILIUM_PH_1__. All clients then share a single limit, so a few wrong attempts from anyone block everyone.

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is a security process that requires users to provide two or more verification factors to gain access to a system, application, or account. This adds an extra layer of protection beyond just using a password.

By requiring more than one verification method, MFA helps reduce the risk of unauthorized access, even if someone has obtained your password. It’s highly recommended for securing sensitive information stored in your notes.

units.context: Multi-factor authentication with TOTP > Relationship to OpenID Connect (OIDC)

units.source: Multi-factor authentication makes your Trilium login safer by requiring an additional proof of identity apart from your password. __TRILIUM_PH_0__Signing in with OpenID Connect__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is a different concept which delegates your authentication to an external provider (e.g. your Google provider, or a self-hosted one such as Authelia). These authentication providers might provide their own security features such as TOTP or passkeys.
units.context: Multi-factor authentication with TOTP > Relationship to OpenID Connect (OIDC)
Multi-factor authentication with TOTP > Time-based one-time password (TOTP)

units.source: TOTP (Time-Based One-Time Password) is a security feature that generates a unique, temporary code on your device, like a smartphone, which changes every 30 seconds. You use this code, along with your password, to log into your account, making it much harder for anyone else to access them.

OpenID is a standardized way to let you log into websites using an account from another service, like Google or Authelia, to verify your identity.

When OpenID is activated, the password-based authentication in Trilium is replaced with a button that connects using your provider. This means that the configuration of __TRILIUM_PH_0__Multi-factor authentication with TOTP__TRILIUM_PH_1__ no longer takes effect, since your provider has to handle any multi-factor authentication.

create short text note from popup
Clicking the extension's button in the browser toolbar opens its popup:

The popup shows what will be saved from the current page: the note's title, which can be edited before saving, the website, and below them a preview, which starts with a box for your own note and the page's description. A switch above the preview chooses what to save, among what the page offers:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Selection__TRILIUM_PH_1__, when text is selected on the page: __TRILIUM_PH_2__Save selection__TRILIUM_PH_3__ saves it into the note of that page's clippings, as the context menu does.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Page__TRILIUM_PH_1__: __TRILIUM_PH_2__Save page to Trilium__TRILIUM_PH_3__ saves the page's text and images. A smaller switch at the top of the preview chooses how much of the page to keep: __TRILIUM_PH_4__Article__TRILIUM_PH_5__ keeps only the page's main text, without its menus, sidebars and footers, and __TRILIUM_PH_6__Whole page__TRILIUM_PH_7__ keeps everything the page shows. __TRILIUM_PH_8__Whole page__TRILIUM_PH_9__ is for pages that are not an article (such as a gallery or a page of cards), where __TRILIUM_PH_10__Article__TRILIUM_PH_11__ can leave out part of the content; the preview shows what each one keeps. __TRILIUM_PH_12__Article__TRILIUM_PH_13__ is unavailable on a page where Trilium finds no article. The author the page names shows under the description, marked by the __TRILIUM_PH_14__ icon. It can be edited or cleared before saving, or written in when the page names none, and is saved in the __TRILIUM_PH_15__ label of the note. When the page states when it was published, that date shows under the author, marked by the __TRILIUM_PH_16__ icon, and is saved in the __TRILIUM_PH_17__ label of the note. When it states when it was last modified, that date shows below, marked by the __TRILIUM_PH_18__ icon, and is saved in the __TRILIUM_PH_19__ label.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__PDF__TRILIUM_PH_1__, when the tab shows a PDF in the browser's viewer: __TRILIUM_PH_2__Save PDF to Trilium__TRILIUM_PH_3__ downloads the PDF and saves it as a file note, which Trilium opens in its __TRILIUM_PH_4__PDFs__TRILIUM_PH_5__ viewer. Only the title and the description can be edited, since a file note has no text of its own for your note. The page's address is saved in the note's __TRILIUM_PH_6__ label and the PDF's file name in __TRILIUM_PH_7__. Saving a PDF needs Trilium v0.107.0 or later.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Bookmark__TRILIUM_PH_1__, always: there is no preview, and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Save bookmark__TRILIUM_PH_3__ saves a link to the page with your note as the content of the note. Left empty, the title stays the page's title.

The box for your note, marked by the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ icon, has the cursor when the popup opens, so a note (such as why the page is worth keeping) can be typed right away. It grows with its text, and keeps it when switching between __TRILIUM_PH_1__Selection__TRILIUM_PH_2__, __TRILIUM_PH_3__Page__TRILIUM_PH_4__ and __TRILIUM_PH_5__Bookmark__TRILIUM_PH_6__. A note on a selection or a page is saved above the clipped content, in a __TRILIUM_PH_7__Note__TRILIUM_PH_8__ admonition. Left empty, nothing is added. __TRILIUM_PH_9__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_10__+__TRILIUM_PH_11__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_12__ in any of the popup's fields saves, whichever is chosen.

The description, marked by the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ icon, comes from the page's __TRILIUM_PH_1__ meta tag, or the one it gives social sites. It can be edited or cleared before saving, or written in when the page has none, and is saved in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ label of the note. Clippings saved with the keyboard shortcuts or the context menu, screenshots and images included, get the description as the page gives it. Each clipping that brings a description updates the label. The description, the author and the dates are shown by clicking the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Web clip__TRILIUM_PH_4__ badge next to the title of the note (see __TRILIUM_PH_5__Note badges__TRILIUM_PH_6__).

The popup opens on the selection if there is one, otherwise on __TRILIUM_PH_0__Page__TRILIUM_PH_1__, showing the article, or the whole page when the page has no article. On a PDF, it opens on __TRILIUM_PH_2__PDF__TRILIUM_PH_3__. On a page that shows nothing to save, it opens on __TRILIUM_PH_4__Bookmark__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and says so. The keyboard shortcuts and the context menu still save right away, without a preview: saving the whole page that way saves the article, the whole page when the page has no article, or the PDF when the tab shows one.

Pages the extension cannot access (the browser's own pages, the extension stores, and pages that were open before the extension was installed until they are reloaded) cannot be saved or captured, so the popup says so in place of the preview, and only __TRILIUM_PH_0__All tabs__TRILIUM_PH_1__ remains available there.

Below the preview, a row of buttons offers the other actions: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Area__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (a screenshot of an area you select), __TRILIUM_PH_2__Visible__TRILIUM_PH_3__ (a screenshot of the visible part of the page), __TRILIUM_PH_4__Full page__TRILIUM_PH_5__ (a screenshot of the whole page) and __TRILIUM_PH_6__All tabs__TRILIUM_PH_7__ (saves the links of every tab in the current window as a list of __TRILIUM_PH_8__Link Previews__TRILIUM_PH_9__, or of text links when __TRILIUM_PH_10__Autogenerate link previews__TRILIUM_PH_11__ is turned off). Hovering over a button shows its full name and, if it has one, its keyboard shortcut.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Full page__TRILIUM_PH_1__ scrolls through the page, takes a screenshot of each part and joins them into one image, then scrolls back to where the page was. The scrollbars are hidden while it does, so they do not appear in the image. Stay on the tab until it is saved: switching to another tab stops the screenshot. A header that stays at the top of the window appears once, at the top of the image, and headings that stick while scrolling appear where they are in the page. Other elements that stay in place while scrolling (such as cookie banners and chat buttons) are left out, while a background that fills the whole window repeats on every screen. In Firefox, the page is captured without scrolling through it, which is faster: such a background then appears only at the top, and images that the page loads only once they are scrolled into view can be missing. A long page is saved as several images, one below the other in the note. A page longer than 100 screens is cut off there, and the message after saving says so. Screenshots keep their full height in Trilium: __TRILIUM_PH_2__Resize image__TRILIUM_PH_3__ (under __TRILIUM_PH_4__Automatically compress images__TRILIUM_PH_5__ in Options → Media) limits only their width.

The popup stays open while Trilium saves, which can take a few seconds for a long page or a large PDF, and the other actions wait until it is done. The bar at the top of the popup then says, in green, that the clipping was saved (in place of the notice that the page was already clipped), with __TRILIUM_PH_0__Open note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to open it in Trilium (and, after __TRILIUM_PH_2__All tabs__TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__Close saved tabs__TRILIUM_PH_5__), or, in red, why it could not be saved. The same clipping cannot be saved twice by accident: the save button stays disabled until another mode is chosen. __TRILIUM_PH_6__Crop__TRILIUM_PH_7__ is the exception: the popup closes so that an area of the page can be selected, and the notification on the page reports the outcome.
If the current page was already clipped, a notice at the top offers to open the note in Trilium.
Trilium was not found: start the desktop application, or check the server address and token in the extension's options.

Downloaded resources are large files that some features need but that do not ship with Trilium, such as the speech recognition models used to transcribe meetings. Trilium downloads them the first time a feature needs them, and keeps them on the device for later use.
Currently, only __TRILIUM_PH_0__Meeting transcription__TRILIUM_PH_1__ on the desktop application uses downloaded resources:
Recognizing speech, with the __TRILIUM_PH_0__High accuracy__TRILIUM_PH_1__ model.
Telling speakers apart, while __TRILIUM_PH_0__Identify speakers__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is on.

When a feature needs resources that are not on the device yet, Trilium asks before downloading them. The dialog lists each resource with what it is used for, where it is downloaded from, its license and its size, followed by the total download size and the free space on the disk.
To start the download, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Download__TRILIUM_PH_1__. Each resource shows its progress, and the feature continues once all of them are downloaded.

To stop the download, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Cancel__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or close the dialog. The files already downloaded are kept, and the next download continues where this one stopped, even within a large file.
If the disk does not have enough free space, the dialog says so and the download cannot be started.
Every file is checked against a checksum built into Trilium before it is used, so a file that was damaged or altered during the download is discarded.

Downloaded resources are not synchronized. Each device that uses a feature downloads its resources separately, even when the notes are kept in sync through __TRILIUM_PH_0__Synchronization__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

To see the downloaded resources, go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Downloaded resources__TRILIUM_PH_3__. Each resource that was downloaded, or partly downloaded by an interrupted download, is listed with the space it takes on the disk and its status. Below the list, __TRILIUM_PH_4__Space used__TRILIUM_PH_5__ shows the space they take in total, and how much free space is left on the disk.
To open the folder of a resource, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button (desktop only).
To delete a resource, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button. If a feature needs it again, it is downloaded again.
The list also shows, faded out, anything else in the resources folder:

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Older version__TRILIUM_PH_1__: the files of an earlier version of a resource. When a resource is updated, the new version is downloaded into a new folder, and the old one is left behind.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Not used__TRILIUM_PH_1__: a resource that no feature of this installation uses, for example one downloaded by a feature that was removed.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Unknown__TRILIUM_PH_1__: any other file or folder, for example one copied there by hand.
These can be deleted in the same way.

If a server and a desktop application share the same data directory, a resource used by only one of them shows as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Not used__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in the other. Deleting it there removes it for both.

The resources are stored in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ folder of the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Data directory__TRILIUM_PH_2__, one folder per resource. To store them elsewhere, set the __TRILIUM_PH_3__ environment variable to another folder before starting Trilium.

An example of a collection with a relatively large number of children that are hidden from the tree.

The tree works well when the notes are structured in a hierarchy so that the number of items stays small. When a note has a large number of notes (in the order of thousands or tens of thousands), two problems arise:
Navigating between notes becomes cumbersome and the tree itself gets cluttered with a large amount of notes.
The large amount of notes can slow down the application considerably.
Since v0.102.0, Trilium allows the tree to hide the child notes of particular notes. This works for both __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and normal notes.
When the subtree of a note is hidden, there are a few subtle changes:
To indicate that the subtree is hidden, the note will not have an expand button and it will display the number of children to the right.
It's not possible to add a new note directly from the tree.
For __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_1__, it's best to use the built-in mechanism to create notes (for example by creating a new point on a geo-map, or by adding a new row in a table).
For normal notes, it's still possible to create children via other means such as using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Internal (reference) links__TRILIUM_PH_1__ system.
Notes can be dragged from outside the note, case in which they will be cloned into it.
Instead of switching to the child notes that were copied, the parent note is highlighted instead.
A notification will indicate this behavior.
Similarly, features such as cut/copy and then paste into the note will also work.
Even if the subtree of a note is hidden, if a child note manages to become active, it will still appear inside the tree in a special state called __TRILIUM_PH_0__spotlighted__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
During this state, the note remains under its normal hierarchy, so that its easy to tell its location. In addition, this means that:
The note position is clearly visible when using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
The note can still be operated on from the tree, such as adding a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Branch prefix__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or moving it outside the collection.
The note appears in italics to indicate its temporary display. When switching to another note, the spotlighted note will disappear.

Only one note can be highlighted at the time. When working with multiple notes such as dragging them into the collection, no note will be spotlighted. This is intentional to avoid displaying a partial state of the subtree.

units.source: This page explains how to manipulate the note tree in TriliumNext, focusing on moving notes.
You can easily rearrange the note tree by dragging and dropping notes, as demonstrated in the example above.

units.context: Note Tree > Drag and Drop > Importing files

units.source: A file or archive can easily be imported into Trilium just by dragging it inside the note tree.
units.context: Note Tree > Drag and Drop > Importing files

units.source: Note that a drag & drop always imports with __TRILIUM_PH_0__safe import__TRILIUM_PH_1__ on, meaning that some features such as scripts are disabled in the upcoming notes. To bypass that, use the dedicated __TRILIUM_PH_2__import__TRILIUM_PH_3__ feature (right click → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Import into note__TRILIUM_PH_5__).
units.context: Note Tree > Drag and Drop > Importing files

units.source: Unlike the import dialog, the drag & drop also has some basic auto-detection of the import. For example, dragging a .zip file with a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ folder in it will automatically trigger a dedicated __TRILIUM_PH_1__Obsidian__TRILIUM_PH_2__ import.

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Trilium offers efficient keyboard-based manipulation using the following __TRILIUM_PH_1__shortcuts__TRILIUM_PH_2__:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ + __TRILIUM_PH_2__↑__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_5__ +__TRILIUM_PH_6__↓__TRILIUM_PH_7__: Move the note up or down in the order.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__←__TRILIUM_PH_3__: Move the note up in the hierarchy by changing its parent to the note's grandparent.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__→__TRILIUM_PH_3__: Move the note down in the hierarchy by setting its parent to the note currently above it (this action is best understood through a demo or hands-on experience).
__TRILIUM_PH_0__←__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__→__TRILIUM_PH_3__: Expand and collapse a sub-tree.

You can also move notes using the familiar cut and paste functions available in the context menu, or with the associated keyboard __TRILIUM_PH_0__shortcuts__TRILIUM_PH_1__: __TRILIUM_PH_2__ ( __TRILIUM_PH_3__copy__TRILIUM_PH_4__), __TRILIUM_PH_5__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_6__ + __TRILIUM_PH_7__X__TRILIUM_PH_8__ (cut) and __TRILIUM_PH_9__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_10__ + __TRILIUM_PH_11__V__TRILIUM_PH_12__ (paste).
See __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note tree contextual menu__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for more information.
Click the tree icon in the tree toolbar to open the tree settings popup. Each option takes effect as soon as it is changed:

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Display density__TRILIUM_PH_1__: __TRILIUM_PH_2__Relaxed__TRILIUM_PH_3__ (default) or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Dense__TRILIUM_PH_5__. Dense rows are shorter, so more notes fit on the screen. This setting is not synchronized, so each device keeps its own.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Hide archived notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__: When enabled, archived notes are not shown in the tree.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Automatically collapse notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__: When enabled, notes are collapsed after a period of inactivity to keep the tree tidy.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Follow active note__TRILIUM_PH_1__: When enabled (default), the tree automatically scrolls and expands parent nodes to keep the currently active note visible. When disabled, the tree is fully detached from navigation — only the background highlight of the active note is updated, but the tree viewport and its expanded/collapsed state are never changed by navigation. Use the crosshair button to manually jump the tree to the active note at any time.

units.source: To hide or show the note tree, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button to the left of the first tab in the horizontal layout, or the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ button at the bottom of the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_3__ in the vertical layout. The __TRILIUM_PH_4__Toggle Left Pane__TRILIUM_PH_5__ __TRILIUM_PH_6__keyboard shortcut__TRILIUM_PH_7__, which is not assigned by default, does the same. See __TRILIUM_PH_8__Vertical and horizontal layout__TRILIUM_PH_9__.

units.source: A small strip with an arrow icon runs along the left edge of the app in the horizontal layout. In the vertical layout, it runs along the right side of the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_1__, and only shows while the tree is hidden.

units.source: When the tree is hidden, pressing the strip will __TRILIUM_PH_0__peek__TRILIUM_PH_1__ the tree.
units.context: Note Tree > Hiding and peeking the tree

units.source: In this mode the tree is shown temporarily above the content, without shifting the content of your notes.

units.source: Clicking outside the tree, pressing __TRILIUM_PH_0__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or pressing the strip again will hide the tree.

Only one panel is peeked at a time: peeking the tree hides a peeked __TRILIUM_PH_8__Right Sidebar__TRILIUM_PH_9__, and the other way around.

units.source: The note tree comes with multiple keyboard shortcuts to make editing faster, consult the dedicated __TRILIUM_PH_0__Keyboard shortcuts__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section.
Example of using keyboard keys to move a note
In Trilium, tabs allow easy switching between notes.
Depending on the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Vertical and horizontal layout__TRILIUM_PH_1__:
For the vertical layout, the tabs will be placed at the top but to the right of the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
For the horizontal layout, the tabs will be placed at the top in full-width, above the __TRILIUM_PH_0__note tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__, allowing for more tabs to be comfortably displayed.
To create a new tab, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button that is to the right of the last tab.
Right-clicking or pressing and holding the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button shows a menu with:
If there are any __TRILIUM_PH_0__Workspaces__TRILIUM_PH_1__, one entry per workspace, which opens the workspace in a new tab, hoisted into it.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Recently changed notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__: up to 15 notes, the most recently changed first, with the path of each note on the right. Notes that are already open in a tab are not listed, and in a __TRILIUM_PH_2__hoisted note__TRILIUM_PH_3__ only its descendants are. Selecting a note opens it in a new tab.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__All recent changes__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which opens the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Recent Changes__TRILIUM_PH_3__ dialog.
To close a tab, press the corresponding __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button.
For multitasking, tabs can be used alongside __TRILIUM_PH_0__Split View__TRILIUM_PH_1__. Each tab can have one or more notes, displayed horizontally.
Tabs can be reordered by drag-and-dropping it into a new position.
An existing tab can be displayed in a new window by dragging the tab upwards or downwards. It is not possible to combine tabs back into another window.
Since tabs are a commonly used feature, there are multiple keyboard shortcuts that can be used:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_3__+__TRILIUM_PH_4__T__TRILIUM_PH_5__ to reopen the last closed tab.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Tab__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_5__+__TRILIUM_PH_6__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_7__+__TRILIUM_PH_8__Tab__TRILIUM_PH_9__ to go to the next or previous tab.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__1__TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_5__+__TRILIUM_PH_6__2__TRILIUM_PH_7__, up to __TRILIUM_PH_8__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_9__+__TRILIUM_PH_10__9__TRILIUM_PH_11__ to activate the first, second and up to ninth tab.
There is also a shortcut to go to the last tab, but it is not assigned a key by default.

To show Trilium in full screen, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__F11__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ __TRILIUM_PH_3__Fullscreen__TRILIUM_PH_4__ button in the __TRILIUM_PH_5__Global menu__TRILIUM_PH_6__. While in full screen, the tab bar shows a __TRILIUM_PH_7__ __TRILIUM_PH_8__Leave full screen__TRILIUM_PH_9__ button before the __TRILIUM_PH_10__Right Sidebar__TRILIUM_PH_11__ toggle; press it to return to the normal window.

When Trilium starts, it reopens the tabs from the previous session. Only the active tab loads its note right away; every other tab loads its note the first time you switch to it. This keeps startup fast when many tabs are open, especially tabs that show collections.
The same applies to a tab opened in the background, for example with a middle click or __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+click on a link.
Tabs are also supported on the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Mobile Frontend__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

Since v0.102.0, the tabs are displayed by pressing the dedicated tab switcher button in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_1__. In this view the tabs are laid out on a grid with a preview of the note content. On a phone, a tab left on the note tree shows the folder it was on instead, with the tab's note highlighted. Swiping left or right on the launch bar goes to the next or previous tab directly, as long as all of its buttons fit on the screen, with the page following the finger until it lets go.
The context menu button at the top-right of the popup allows creating a new tab, reopening the last closed tab and closing all the tabs.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Split View__TRILIUM_PH_1__s are also indicated in the tab switcher, with two titles displayed in a tab.

Versions prior to v0.102.0 also supported tabs, but they were displayed directly above the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_1__. The decision to use a more mobile-like tab switcher was taken because the original tab bar could not support many tabs at once and the new design better aligns with how mobile applications handle tabs.

units.source: The note menu contains various actions and configurations for the current note. It can be found in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note buttons__TRILIUM_PH_1__ area (to the right of the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Title__TRILIUM_PH_3__).

Every split has a note menu of its own, which acts on the note displayed in that split. Entries that don't apply to the current note are still listed but grayed out, while entries that only exist for some notes (described in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note-specific entries__TRILIUM_PH_1__) appear only on those notes.

These entries are the row of icons at the top of the menu, each with a short title. Hovering one shows its full name and its keyboard shortcut. In Quick edit on a phone, where only __TRILIUM_PH_0__Find__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is left, it is listed as an ordinary entry instead.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Find__TRILIUM_PH_2__ opens the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Search in note__TRILIUM_PH_4__ bar, to find and replace text inside the current note. On the desktop application, the same bar opens with __TRILIUM_PH_5__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_6__+__TRILIUM_PH_7__F__TRILIUM_PH_8__.

It is available on __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Code__TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__Mind Map__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and __TRILIUM_PH_6__Spreadsheets__TRILIUM_PH_7__ notes, __TRILIUM_PH_8__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_9__, PDF files, and any note displayed as __TRILIUM_PH_10__Note source__TRILIUM_PH_11__.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Attachments__TRILIUM_PH_2__ switches the note to the list of its __TRILIUM_PH_3__Attachments__TRILIUM_PH_4__, where they can be uploaded, opened, downloaded, renamed or deleted.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Note map__TRILIUM_PH_2__ opens the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Connections tab__TRILIUM_PH_4__ of the __TRILIUM_PH_5__Right Sidebar__TRILIUM_PH_6__, which shows the __TRILIUM_PH_7__Note Map (Link map, Tree map)__TRILIUM_PH_8__ centered on the current note.
The toggles in this section take effect immediately:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Shared__TRILIUM_PH_2__ publishes the note via __TRILIUM_PH_3__Sharing__TRILIUM_PH_4__, by cloning it into the __TRILIUM_PH_5__Shared Notes__TRILIUM_PH_6__ tree.
Turning it off removes the clone from that tree. If the note exists only as a shared note, Trilium asks for confirmation, since unsharing it deletes it.
The toggle is unavailable on the root note, on the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Shared Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note itself, and on system notes.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Protect the note__TRILIUM_PH_2__ encrypts the note, turning it into one of the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Protected Notes__TRILIUM_PH_4__. If no protected session is active, Trilium asks for the password first. Only the current note is affected, not its children.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Bookmark__TRILIUM_PH_2__ adds the note to the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Bookmarks__TRILIUM_PH_4__ that are displayed in the __TRILIUM_PH_5__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_6__, or removes it from them.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Template__TRILIUM_PH_2__ marks the note as one of the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Templates__TRILIUM_PH_4__ (by adding the __TRILIUM_PH_5__ label), which makes it available when creating a new note.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Full width__TRILIUM_PH_2__ lets the note use the whole width of the window instead of the limit set in __TRILIUM_PH_3__Content width__TRILIUM_PH_4__ by adding the __TRILIUM_PH_5__ label. It is not listed for note types that are always displayed at full width.
The two submenus in this section:

__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Note type__TRILIUM_PH_2__ changes the type of the note to any of the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Note Types__TRILIUM_PH_4__; the current one is checked. If the note already has content, Trilium asks for confirmation first, since the content generally doesn't carry over. __TRILIUM_PH_5__Converting between note types__TRILIUM_PH_6__.
For a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note, the language is chosen in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Status bar__TRILIUM_PH_3__ instead.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Editable__TRILIUM_PH_2__ controls when the note opens as read-only (see __TRILIUM_PH_3__Read-Only Notes__TRILIUM_PH_4__):
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Auto__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (the default): the note is editable, unless it is long enough to be opened as read-only automatically.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Read-only__TRILIUM_PH_1__: the note always opens as read-only, but can still be edited after pressing __TRILIUM_PH_2__Edit note__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Always editable__TRILIUM_PH_1__: the note is always editable, regardless of its length.

units.source: These entries manage the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Revisions__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of the note:

__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Note revisions…__TRILIUM_PH_2__ opens the revisions dialog, where previous versions can be previewed, compared with the current one, downloaded or restored. The arrow beside it opens the entries that save a revision right away. On mobile, tapping it opens those entries, with __TRILIUM_PH_3__Note revisions…__TRILIUM_PH_4__ as the first one.
__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Save revision__TRILIUM_PH_2__ saves a revision of the note right away, instead of waiting for the next automatic snapshot.
__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Save named revision…__TRILIUM_PH_2__ also saves a revision right away, but first asks for a short description of the changes, which is shown in the revisions dialog.
The following entries only appear on some notes:
__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Edit note__TRILIUM_PH_2__ appears at the top of the menu when the note is currently read-only. It enables editing until the note is closed.
__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Word wrap__TRILIUM_PH_2__ appears at the top of the menu on __TRILIUM_PH_3__Code__TRILIUM_PH_4__ notes, and sets whether long lines wrap in this note:

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Auto__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (the default) follows __TRILIUM_PH_2__Options__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Code Notes__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Wrap lines in code notes__TRILIUM_PH_7__.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__On__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Off__TRILIUM_PH_3__ override it for this note only, by setting the __TRILIUM_PH_4__ label.

__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Convert into attachment__TRILIUM_PH_2__ appears on an image note that has no children and a single parent which is a __TRILIUM_PH_3__Text__TRILIUM_PH_4__ note. After a confirmation, it turns the image into an attachment of its parent note and opens it there. See __TRILIUM_PH_5__Attachments__TRILIUM_PH_6__.
__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Re-render note__TRILIUM_PH_2__ appears on a __TRILIUM_PH_3__Render Note__TRILIUM_PH_4__, and runs its script again to refresh the output.
__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Board properties__TRILIUM_PH_2__ appears on a __TRILIUM_PH_3__Kanban Board__TRILIUM_PH_4__, and configures its columns, card attributes and card templates.
__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Calendar properties__TRILIUM_PH_2__ appears on a __TRILIUM_PH_3__Calendar__TRILIUM_PH_4__ that creates events, and configures its event templates.

__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Geo map properties__TRILIUM_PH_2__ appears on a __TRILIUM_PH_3__Geo Map__TRILIUM_PH_4__, and configures its map settings and the image of an __TRILIUM_PH_5__image map__TRILIUM_PH_6__.
__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Table properties__TRILIUM_PH_2__ appears on a __TRILIUM_PH_3__Table__TRILIUM_PH_4__, and configures which notes it shows.
The __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Advanced__TRILIUM_PH_2__ submenu groups the actions that are needed less often:

__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Open externally__TRILIUM_PH_2__ (desktop application only) saves the note to a temporary file and opens it in the application that the operating system associates with it. Trilium watches the file: each time it is saved, a notification in the window it was opened from offers to upload the modified version back into the note, keeping the current content as a revision. A file that the operating system would run as a program, such as a __TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__, __TRILIUM_PH_5__ or __TRILIUM_PH_6__ file, is not opened; __TRILIUM_PH_7__Open with...__TRILIUM_PH_8__ can still open it in an application you pick. It is unavailable on __TRILIUM_PH_9__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_10__ and __TRILIUM_PH_11__Saved Search__TRILIUM_PH_12__ notes.

__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Open with...__TRILIUM_PH_2__ (desktop application only) works like __TRILIUM_PH_3__Open externally__TRILIUM_PH_4__, but lets you pick the application to open the file with. See __TRILIUM_PH_5__Open with__TRILIUM_PH_6__ below.
__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Note source__TRILIUM_PH_2__ shows the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Note source__TRILIUM_PH_4__, the content of the note exactly as it is stored.

__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Convert to Markdown note__TRILIUM_PH_2__ (on text notes) and __TRILIUM_PH_3__Convert to text note__TRILIUM_PH_4__ (on Markdown notes) switch the note between rich text and Markdown. After a confirmation, Trilium saves a revision and converts the content; the revision allows going back if some formatting was lost. See __TRILIUM_PH_5__Converting between note types__TRILIUM_PH_6__.
__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Compress images__TRILIUM_PH_2__ opens a dialog that reduces the size of the images in the note. It lists the images found and how much space they take, and offers to:
Resize the images larger than a chosen size.
Keep, optimize, or convert to JPEG the PNG images.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Process child notes as well__TRILIUM_PH_1__, to include the images of the notes beneath this one.
Compressing cannot be undone. Images can also be compressed automatically on upload, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Images__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__View OCR text__TRILIUM_PH_2__ (on image and file notes) shows the text extracted from the note via __TRILIUM_PH_3__Text Extraction (OCR)__TRILIUM_PH_4__. If the note has not been processed yet, the dialog offers to __TRILIUM_PH_5__Process OCR__TRILIUM_PH_6__.

__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Open note on server__TRILIUM_PH_2__ (desktop application only, listed when __TRILIUM_PH_3__Synchronization__TRILIUM_PH_4__ is configured) opens the same note on the sync server, in the web browser.

__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Open with...__TRILIUM_PH_2__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Advanced__TRILIUM_PH_4__ submenu opens the note in an application you choose, instead of the one the operating system associates with its type. As with __TRILIUM_PH_5__Open externally__TRILIUM_PH_6__, Trilium saves the note to a temporary file, watches it, and offers to upload the modified version back into the note. The entry is available only in the desktop application; attachments offer the same action.
On Windows, the system's __TRILIUM_PH_0__Open with__TRILIUM_PH_1__ dialog lists the installed applications.
On Linux, the application chooser comes from the desktop portal (__TRILIUM_PH_0__), so it works in the Flatpak as well.

In the Flathub version, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Open externally__TRILIUM_PH_1__ also goes through the desktop portal, which can show the application chooser the first few times a file type is opened, as the system's policy decides; __TRILIUM_PH_2__Open with...__TRILIUM_PH_3__ always shows it.

On macOS, a file picker opens in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Applications__TRILIUM_PH_1__ folder; the note opens in the application you select there, as with __TRILIUM_PH_2__Open With__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Other…__TRILIUM_PH_5__ in Finder.

If the application chooser cannot be shown (such as when no desktop portal is running on Linux), Trilium reports an error instead of opening the file. __TRILIUM_PH_0__Open externally__TRILIUM_PH_1__ still opens it in the default application.

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Delete note__TRILIUM_PH_2__ opens the deletion dialog for the current note and its subtree. The dialog lists the notes that will be deleted and the relations that will be broken, and offers to:

Also delete the other clones of the note, if it is cloned elsewhere. Otherwise, only the current placement is removed and the note stays in its other locations. See __TRILIUM_PH_0__Cloning Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Erase permanently__TRILIUM_PH_1__ instead of the usual soft deletion. This cannot be undone.
Notes deleted without erasing can be brought back, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Restoring Deleted Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
The note menu is not available on launchers.

On the notes of __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and of the in-app help, most entries are grayed out, since these notes cannot be imported into, deleted or have revisions. Of the two, only the in-app help can be exported, see __TRILIUM_PH_2__Import & Export__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note properties__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section is only listed when the note itself is displayed, not its __TRILIUM_PH_2__Attachments__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or its __TRILIUM_PH_4__Note source__TRILIUM_PH_5__.

In __TRILIUM_PH_0__Quick edit__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note map__TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__Full width__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and __TRILIUM_PH_6__Convert into attachment__TRILIUM_PH_7__ are not listed.

On the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Mobile Frontend__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the note menu opens as a sheet from the bottom of the screen. Besides the entries above, it contains the items that the desktop layout places elsewhere:

Two more icons in the row of icons at the very top of the sheet, which reads __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__New split__TRILIUM_PH_2__, __TRILIUM_PH_3__Note map__TRILIUM_PH_4__, __TRILIUM_PH_5__Find__TRILIUM_PH_6__ and __TRILIUM_PH_7__ __TRILIUM_PH_8__Child note__TRILIUM_PH_9__ from left to right: __TRILIUM_PH_10__New split__TRILIUM_PH_11__ opens a __TRILIUM_PH_12__Split View__TRILIUM_PH_13__ while there is none in the tab, and __TRILIUM_PH_14__Child note__TRILIUM_PH_15__ creates a note under the current one.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Backlinks__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note paths__TRILIUM_PH_3__, below the row of icons, which open the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Backlinks__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and the other locations of the note.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Attachments__TRILIUM_PH_2__ and __TRILIUM_PH_3__ __TRILIUM_PH_4__Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_5__, under them, which open the attachments and the attributes of the note, each with the number the note has. Links made by the content of the note are not counted as attributes. __TRILIUM_PH_6__Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_7__ is unavailable where the note cannot be edited. On mobile, __TRILIUM_PH_8__Attachments__TRILIUM_PH_9__ is listed here instead of in the row of icons.
The custom buttons of the note type (such as __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Download__TRILIUM_PH_2__ on a __TRILIUM_PH_3__File__TRILIUM_PH_4__).
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Close this pane__TRILIUM_PH_1__, on the second note of a __TRILIUM_PH_2__Split View__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Note settings__TRILIUM_PH_2__, below __TRILIUM_PH_3__Protect the note__TRILIUM_PH_4__, which opens __TRILIUM_PH_5__Shared__TRILIUM_PH_6__ and __TRILIUM_PH_7__Bookmark__TRILIUM_PH_8__, then __TRILIUM_PH_9__Note type__TRILIUM_PH_10__, __TRILIUM_PH_11__Template__TRILIUM_PH_12__ and __TRILIUM_PH_13__Full width__TRILIUM_PH_14__, on a page of their own, together with the language of the note: the content language on __TRILIUM_PH_15__Text__TRILIUM_PH_16__ notes (see __TRILIUM_PH_17__Content language & Right-to-left support__TRILIUM_PH_18__), and the language of the code on __TRILIUM_PH_19__Code__TRILIUM_PH_20__ notes. The choices of __TRILIUM_PH_21__Editable__TRILIUM_PH_22__ are listed at the end of that page, under their own heading, instead of in a further submenu.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Note info__TRILIUM_PH_2__, below __TRILIUM_PH_3__Note settings__TRILIUM_PH_4__, which opens the dates, type, ID and size of the note on a page of its own, ending with __TRILIUM_PH_5__Show similar notes__TRILIUM_PH_6__ (see __TRILIUM_PH_7__Similar Notes__TRILIUM_PH_8__).
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Note map__TRILIUM_PH_1__ opens the map in a popup instead of the right sidebar.
The note buttons is an area at the top-right of a note with a few buttons:

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which offers commands for the note or its subtree, such as import, export, viewing the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note source code__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Attachments__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
On some note types such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__File__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and images, there are dedicated buttons (e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_2__ to download the file locally).
The Options section allows the configuration of the TriliumNext client and server.
The Options can be accessed via:
The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Global menu__TRILIUM_PH_1__, by selecting the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Options__TRILIUM_PH_3__ item.
The __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button in the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_2__ which can optionally be hidden if not desirable.
Optionally, a keyboard shortcut can be defined, but it is not assigned by default.
Once in the options section, simply select one of the option categories using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
When entering the options, they are opened in a new __TRILIUM_PH_0__tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__. To close them, simply close the tab.
When using __TRILIUM_PH_0__Synchronization__TRILIUM_PH_1__, some of the options will be kept in sync across all the devices while others can be changed independently.

Generally, the options that relate to appearance are intentionally kept not synced in order to allow per-client customization (layout orientation, theme, vertical/horizontal layout, code block themes).
In Trilium, is possible to work with two or more notes side-by-side.
Press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button to the right of a note's title to open a new split to the right of it.
It is possible to have as many splits as desired, simply press again the button.
Only horizontal splits are possible, vertical or drag & dropping is not supported.
When at least one split is open, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button next to it to close it.
Use the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ or the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ button to move around the splits.

Creating, closing and moving a split can also be triggered from a __TRILIUM_PH_0__keyboard shortcut__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__Create New Split__TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__Close Active Split__TRILIUM_PH_5__, __TRILIUM_PH_6__Move Split Left__TRILIUM_PH_7__ and __TRILIUM_PH_8__Move Split Right__TRILIUM_PH_9__, all unassigned by default) or through the __TRILIUM_PH_10__command palette__TRILIUM_PH_11__.

The focus can be moved from one split to the one next to it with the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Focus Split to the Left__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Focus Split to the Right__TRILIUM_PH_3__ actions, which stop at either end of the tab instead of continuing into the next tab. They are unassigned by default as well.
Each __TRILIUM_PH_0__tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__ has its own split view configuration (e.g. one tab can have two notes in a split view, whereas the others are one-note views).
The tab's title will indicate all the note titles, in the order of the splits from the left to right and separated by a bullet symbol.
The tab's icon will indicate the icon of the last active split, which will be automatically focused when clicking on the tab.
Splits and the note tree & hoisting__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Split View > Splits and the note tree & hoisting

units.source: Clicking on the content of a split will focus that split. While focused, the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ will also indicate the note that is being edited.
units.context: Split View > Splits and the note tree & hoisting

units.source: It is possible for each of the splits to have their own __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Hoisting__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Split View > Splits and the note tree & hoisting

units.source: When a new split is created, it will share the same note hoisting as the previous one. An easy solution to this is to simply hoist the notes after the split is created.
units.context: Split View > Splits and the note tree & hoisting

units.source: This is generally quite useful for reorganizing notes from one place to the other, by hoisting the old place in the first split and hoisting the new place to the second one. This will allow easy cut and paste without the tree jumping around from switching between notes.
units.context: Split View > Splits and the note tree & hoisting

units.source: Since v0.100.0, it's possible to have a split view on the mobile view as well, with the following differences from the desktop version of the split:
On smartphones, the split views are laid out vertically (one on the top and one on the bottom), instead of horizontally as on the desktop.
There can be only one split open per tab.
It's not possible to resize the two split panes.
When the keyboard is opened, the active note will be “maximized”, thus allowing for more space even when a split is open. When the keyboard is closed, the splits become equal in size again.
To create a new split, click the three dots button on the right of the note title and tap __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__New split__TRILIUM_PH_2__ in the row of icons at the top.
This option will only be available if there is no split already open in the current tab.
To close a split, click the three dots button on the right of the note title and select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Close this pane__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Note that this option will only be available on the second note in the split (the one at the bottom on smartphones, the one on the right on tablets).
When long-pressing a link, a contextual menu will show up with an option to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Open note in a new split__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
If there's already a split, the option will replace the existing split instead.
The Outline tab appears in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Right Sidebar__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and displays the headings and highlights for the current note.
The table of contents displays the titles / headings in the current note and allows easy navigation.
The following note types are supported:
The pages of the in-app documentation

units.source: Clicking on a heading will scroll the document to the position of the heading.

Unlike table of contents which supports multiple note types, the highlights are specific to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes.
Text with a foreground color set.
Text with a background color/highlight set.
Clicking on a highlighted text will scroll the document to its position.
Globally, it's possible to toggle the display of each category of highlighted text (as defined above)
Pressing the gear button in the top-right part of the section will reveal a menu to toggle between the highlight categories.
Alternatively, they can be changed by going to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ settings and looking for the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Highlights List__TRILIUM_PH_3__ section.
When __TRILIUM_PH_0__PDFs__TRILIUM_PH_1__ are opened in Trilium, the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Right Sidebar__TRILIUM_PH_3__ is augmented with PDF-specific navigation, with the following features:
All the headings and “bookmarks” will be displayed hierarchically.
The heading on the current page is also highlighted (note that it can be slightly offset depending on how many headings are on the same page).
Clicking on a heading will jump to the corresponding position in the PDF.
A preview of all the pages with a small thumbnail.
Clicking on a page will automatically navigate to that page.
Right-clicking a page and selecting __TRILIUM_PH_0__Copy reference__TRILIUM_PH_1__ copies a link that opens the PDF at that page.
Highlight and comment annotations are listed here.
Right-clicking an annotation and selecting __TRILIUM_PH_0__Copy reference__TRILIUM_PH_1__ copies a link that opens the PDF at that annotation.
If the PDF has its own attachments (not to be confused with Trilium's __TRILIUM_PH_0__Attachments__TRILIUM_PH_1__), they will be displayed in a list.
Some information such as the name and size of the attachment are displayed.
It's possible to download the attachment by clicking on the download button.
A less common feature, if the PDF has toggle-able layers, these layers will be displayed in a list here.
It's possible to toggle the visibility for each individual layer.
The attributes tab provides a more graphical way to view and edit __TRILIUM_PH_0__attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
The attributes are grouped into collapsible sections, each showing the number of attributes it holds next to its name:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Owned__TRILIUM_PH_1__ contains a list of the attributes that belong to this note.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Inherited__TRILIUM_PH_1__ contains the attributes that apply to the current note but come through __TRILIUM_PH_2__Attribute Inheritance__TRILIUM_PH_3__. This section is only displayed if the note inherits attributes.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Definitions__TRILIUM_PH_1__ describe the type of attributes and are used in __TRILIUM_PH_2__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Table__TRILIUM_PH_5__ collections. This section is only displayed if the note has or inherits definitions.
Clicking the name of a section collapses or expands it, and the collapsed state is remembered.
Above the sections there is a toolbar with:
A __TRILIUM_PH_0__Select all__TRILIUM_PH_1__ checkbox, which selects every attribute (see __TRILIUM_PH_2__Selecting attributes__TRILIUM_PH_3__).
A __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button, which only appears after attributes are copied. It lists the copied attributes and offers to paste them into the current note or to clear them.
A __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Add a new attribute__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button, which offers to add a label, a relation, a label definition or a relation definition. This shows the full detail popup.

On a note that cannot be edited (such as a page of the in-app help), the paste and add buttons are replaced by a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Read-only__TRILIUM_PH_2__ indicator. Attributes can still be selected and copied from such a note.
Every item is structured as such:
The icon of each item indicates whether it's a __TRILIUM_PH_0__label__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) or a __TRILIUM_PH_3__relation__TRILIUM_PH_4__ (__TRILIUM_PH_5__, link to another note).
The first text is the name of the label.
The value of the attribute is displayed after the name, if present.
The value is shown in a graphical way: a relation's value is a clickable note link; a color label shows a color chip.
System attributes (that have a special meaning in Trilium) show a small __TRILIUM_PH_0__ cog near the icon and are grouped separately from the user-defined ones.
Clicking on the item (apart from the value and links) reveals a dedicated popup where the name, value and __TRILIUM_PH_0__Attribute Inheritance__TRILIUM_PH_1__ can be defined.
The value of the attributes can be edited in-place:
The input box follows the type defined in a corresponding label definition (date, color, dropdown, numbers), as well as for system attributes that have a specific type (e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_0__).
For labels, clicking on the value edits its in-place.
Press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to confirm or click outside the input box, or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_3__ to dismiss.
For multi-line text, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_3__ confirms whereas __TRILIUM_PH_4__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_5__ creates a newline.
For checkbox attributes, clicking on the checkbox will toggle its state.
For labels without a value, a value can be added by clicking on the __TRILIUM_PH_0__No value__TRILIUM_PH_1__ text which appears while the mouse is hovered on the item.
For relations, there is a dedicated __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button instead.

An attribute can be deleted by pressing the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button to its right, which only appears while hovered. A confirmation screen is displayed first to ensure the attribute is not accidentally deleted.
Attributes can be added in two ways:
A new label, relation or attribute definition can be added from the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button in the __TRILIUM_PH_1__toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_2__. This shows the full detail popup.
To quickly add a label or a relation directly from the sidebar, click the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add attribute__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) item at the end of the list.

The name field will be focused first. By default, a label will be created instead but it can be toggled to a relation by typing __TRILIUM_PH_0__~__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or pressing the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ icon (similarly, typing __TRILIUM_PH_3__ will switch back to a label instead of a relation).

Once the name is filled, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to continue to the value. Type in a value if desired and then press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_3__ again to create the attribute.
Clicking outside the editor will also create the attribute, but only if a name is specified.
Inherited labels or relations are shown in the same fashion as the owned ones.
To the right of the inherited attribute there is a link to the note where the attribute comes from, as well as an __TRILIUM_PH_0__ icon to indicate that it's inheritable.
Clicking on an inherited attribute will reveal the same popup as owned attributes, but it is not editable. To edit it, first navigate to the note where the attribute is defined.
The icon indicates the type of the attribute (text, number).
If an attribute is promoted, it has a small __TRILIUM_PH_0__ chevron icon overlaid on top of it.
The name indicates the name of the attribute it defines (without the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ or __TRILIUM_PH_1__ prefix).
To the right of the name a short summary is displayed which indicates the display name (alias), whether it has multiple values or an inverse relation.
Clicking on a definition reveals a popup, where the name, type, display name and other aspects can be configured.

To add a label definition, click the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add definition__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) item at the end of the list; its type can be changed to a relation from the popup. Both kinds of definitions can also be added from the __TRILIUM_PH_3__ button in the __TRILIUM_PH_4__toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
For inherited definition, there is a link to the note where the definition comes from, as well as an __TRILIUM_PH_0__ icon to indicate that it's inherited.
Multiple attributes can be selected in order to copy or delete them together:
Hovering over an attribute shows a checkbox in place of its icon. Click it to select the attribute.

Alternatively, hold __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__Cmd__TRILIUM_PH_3__ on macOS) while clicking an attribute to select it, or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_5__ to select a range of attributes. A range can span multiple sections.
Once at least one attribute is selected, every attribute shows its checkbox, and clicking anywhere on an attribute selects or deselects it instead of opening the detail popup.

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Select all__TRILIUM_PH_1__ checkbox in the toolbar selects every attribute; while attributes are selected, it shows how many. Clicking it again clears the selection, as does pressing __TRILIUM_PH_2__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
While attributes are selected, the toolbar shows:
A __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button, which copies the selected attributes.

A __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button, which deletes the selected attributes after a confirmation. It only appears if all the selected attributes belong to the current note, since inherited attributes can only be deleted from the note they come from.
Right-clicking an attribute shows a menu with the same actions, as well as pasting. If the attribute is not part of the selection, the menu applies only to that attribute.

units.context: Attributes tab > Copying and pasting attributes

units.source: Attributes can be copied from one note and pasted into another:
units.context: Attributes tab > Copying and pasting attributes

units.source: To copy, select the attributes and press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__C__TRILIUM_PH_3__, or use the __TRILIUM_PH_4__ button in the toolbar or the context menu.
units.context: Attributes tab > Copying and pasting attributes

units.source: To paste, navigate to the destination note and press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__V__TRILIUM_PH_3__ after clicking anywhere in the attributes tab, or use the __TRILIUM_PH_4__ button in the toolbar. Right-clicking an attribute or an empty area of a section also offers to paste.
units.context: Attributes tab > Copying and pasting attributes

units.source: Attributes are copied as text, in the same format as the attributes editor (for example __TRILIUM_PH_0__). As a result:
units.context: Attributes tab > Copying and pasting attributes

units.source: Copied attributes can be pasted into the attributes editor or into a note, and the text of the attributes editor can be pasted into the attributes tab.
units.context: Attributes tab > Copying and pasting attributes

units.source: Attributes can be written by hand in any other application and then pasted into Trilium.
units.context: Attributes tab > Copying and pasting attributes

units.source: When pasting, the attributes become owned attributes of the current note, even if they were inherited in the source note:
units.context: Attributes tab > Copying and pasting attributes

units.source: If the note already has an attribute with the same name, its value is replaced by the pasted one.
units.context: Attributes tab > Copying and pasting attributes

units.source: If a definition marks the attribute as having multiple values (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__), the pasted value is added alongside the existing ones instead, unless the same value is already present.
units.context: Attributes tab > Copying and pasting attributes

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__V__TRILIUM_PH_3__ pastes what the system clipboard holds, whereas the __TRILIUM_PH_4__ button and the context menu paste the attributes last copied in Trilium. The two differ if something else was copied in the meantime.
units.context: Attributes tab > Copying and pasting attributes

units.source: On mobile, the attributes are the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ tab of the note panel (see __TRILIUM_PH_2__Right Sidebar__TRILIUM_PH_3__), which opens as a sheet at the bottom of the screen from the __TRILIUM_PH_4__ button beside the __TRILIUM_PH_5__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_6__. Selecting __TRILIUM_PH_7__Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_8__ in the note menu, below __TRILIUM_PH_9__Backlinks__TRILIUM_PH_10__ and __TRILIUM_PH_11__Note paths__TRILIUM_PH_12__, opens the panel on that tab. Tapping an attribute opens it on a page of its own, with a __TRILIUM_PH_13__ button to return to the list.
On mobile, the __TRILIUM_PH_0__toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_1__ takes the place of the tab's name in the header of the sheet, and each section is displayed as a separate card:
Attributes are added from the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button in the header, or from the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ button above the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Definitions__TRILIUM_PH_3__ card.
To select an attribute, press and hold it. Once an attribute is selected, tapping other attributes selects them as well.
Copying, pasting and deleting work the same way as on desktop, from the header.
Once the __TRILIUM_PH_0__AI__TRILIUM_PH_1__ integration is activated, a __TRILIUM_PH_2__Chat__TRILIUM_PH_3__ entry will appear in the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Right Sidebar__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
Unlike the dedicated note type, the side bar has optional access to the current note, making it easy to ask for information or modifications to a note without having to search for the note first.
To toggle whether the current note is visible to the AI, simply click on the file icon at the bottom of the chat interface.
On the top-right of the sidebar there are three buttons:

__TRILIUM_PH_0__ opens a menu to rename or delete the current conversation, or to save it as a dedicated note in the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Day Notes__TRILIUM_PH_2__, which turns it into a dedicated chat note.
The sidebar chats are stored in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Hidden Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and can be seen in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__AI Chat History__TRILIUM_PH_3__ section.
On mobile, the chat is the __TRILIUM_PH_0__AI chat__TRILIUM_PH_1__ tab of the note panel (see __TRILIUM_PH_2__Right Sidebar__TRILIUM_PH_3__). Its buttons are in the header of the sheet:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ on the left creates a new conversation.
The title of the current conversation, in the middle, lists the previous conversations when tapped.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__, next to the close button, opens the same menu as on desktop.
The connections tab groups together all the information about the current note and how it relates to other notes, in four different sections.

It's generally best to keep only the desired sections expanded as each of the sections have to retrieve additional data that might not otherwise be needed. While collapsed, the sections do not retrieve any additional data.

The note map displays a graph which shows the relation between the current notes and other notes on the hierarchy. There are two types of visualizations, which can be selected from the top-right part of the section:
The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Link map__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__), which displays the __TRILIUM_PH_3__relations__TRILIUM_PH_4__ between notes.
The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Tree map__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__), which displays the hierarchical structure.

The sidebar will remember which visualization is selected, as a global option. Note that note maps also have a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ which describes which visualization to use, but the sidebar deliberately ignores that to keep consistency when switching between notes.

The map can also be expanded by pressing the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button in the top-right of the section. When expanded, the map is displayed in a separate dialog. Alternatively, all other sections can be collapsed, which will make the note map taller and the sidebar can be dragged to make for more lateral space.

The note map view inside the sidebar is deliberately more compact in order to fit the space: the link map would also show notes that don't have a link to the current note from the hierarchy (creating a cloud of dots) but this is only shown while the map is expanded. Similarly, the link strength and pin configuration buttons are not displayed here.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Map (Link map, Tree map)__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for more information on the concept as a whole.

The note paths section displays the locations in which the current note is __TRILIUM_PH_0__cloned__TRILIUM_PH_1__. Each segment of the note path is clickable, in order to navigate to that note or clone. The root note is shown as its icon, the same as in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Breadcrumb__TRILIUM_PH_3__; hovering it shows its title.
A new clone can be created from the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button at the top-right.
Backlinks list the notes that refer to the current note, as well as a preview of the content where the reference to the note is made.
Displays a list of notes that appear similar based on the content of the notes and their attributes. For more information, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Similar Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
The right sidebar displays specific content for the current note. The sidebar is grouped into multiple tabs:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Outline tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which displays the table of contents, highlights and other navigation-related sections depending on the note type.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Attributes tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which provides a visual editor for the current note's __TRILIUM_PH_2__Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__AI chat tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which uses the __TRILIUM_PH_2__AI__TRILIUM_PH_3__ integration to chat, with optional access to the current note.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Connections tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which groups together the note map, note paths, backlinks and similar notes.
Each window keeps its own selected tab, so switching tabs in one window does not affect the others. A newly opened window starts on the tab that was selected last.

units.context: Right Sidebar > Toggling the right sidebar

units.source: There are two ways to toggle the right sidebar:
units.context: Right Sidebar > Toggling the right sidebar

units.source: Via the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ icon near the title bar, which toggles whether the sidebar is docked.
units.context: Right Sidebar > Toggling the right sidebar

units.source: Via the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Toggle right pane__TRILIUM_PH_1__ __TRILIUM_PH_2__keyboard shortcut__TRILIUM_PH_3__, which is not assigned by default.
units.context: Right Sidebar > Toggling the right sidebar

units.source: There is a small strip near the right edge of the app which shows an arrow icon.
When the sidebar is hidden, pressing the edge will __TRILIUM_PH_0__peek__TRILIUM_PH_1__ the sidebar.
In this mode the sidebar is shown temporarily above the content, without shifting the content of your notes.
Clicking outside the sidebar while in peek mode will simply hide the sidebar. Same goes for the X button and clicking on the right edge.
Pressing the pin icon will dock the sidebar.
When the sidebar is docked, pressing the edge will hide the sidebar (similar to the toggle icon at the top).

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Peek Right Pane__TRILIUM_PH_1__ __TRILIUM_PH_2__keyboard shortcut__TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_5__+__TRILIUM_PH_6__]__TRILIUM_PH_7__ by default, does the same as pressing the strip.
On mobile, the right sidebar is replaced by the note panel, which opens as a sheet at the bottom of the screen from the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button beside the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_2__.

The tabs are switched from a bar at the bottom of the sheet. As on desktop, a tab with nothing to show for the current note is left out, and the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Widgets__TRILIUM_PH_1__ tab lists the __TRILIUM_PH_2__right pane widgets__TRILIUM_PH_3__ of scripts.
The sections of a tab are displayed one after the other as cards, each with its name above it, instead of collapsible sections.

The header of the sheet shows the name of the tab, except in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__AI chat__TRILIUM_PH_3__ tabs, where it holds their buttons instead (see __TRILIUM_PH_4__Attributes tab__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and __TRILIUM_PH_6__AI chat tab__TRILIUM_PH_7__).
Tapping a heading of the table of contents, or a page or an annotation of a PDF, closes the panel and scrolls the note to it.

units.context: Recent Changes > Accessing the recent changes

units.source: For an overview of the changes across all documents, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button in the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_2__.
units.context: Recent Changes > Accessing the recent changes

units.source: If there is a __TRILIUM_PH_0__hoisted note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or a __TRILIUM_PH_2__workspace__TRILIUM_PH_3__, the list of recent changes will be limited to the descendents of the hoisted note, or the workspace.
units.context: Recent Changes > Accessing the recent changes

units.source: Right-clicking or pressing and holding the button lists up to 15 of the most recently changed notes that are not open in a tab. Selecting a note opens it in a new tab.
units.context: Recent Changes > Accessing the recent changes

units.source: To limit the list of recent changes to a note and its descendants, look for the corresponding option in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note tree contextual menu__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → Advanced.
units.context: Recent Changes > Accessing the recent changes

units.source: Right-clicking or pressing and holding the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button of the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Tabs__TRILIUM_PH_2__ bar lists the most recently changed notes that are not open in a tab. __TRILIUM_PH_3__All recent changes__TRILIUM_PH_4__, at the bottom of that menu, opens this dialog.
units.context: Recent Changes > Accessing the recent changes

units.source: Notes which were changed will appear in reverse chronological order (latest update first).
The title of the note is displayed, as well as the note path. Clicking on the note title will dismiss the dialog and navigate to that particular note.
Deleted notes will also be listed here, at their time of deletion. Press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Undelete__TRILIUM_PH_1__ link next to them in order to recover them.
Zoom applies to the entire UI, including text.
On the desktop application, use the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Global menu__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to zoom in/out.

On both web browser and the desktop, the keyboard shortcuts __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_3__+__TRILIUM_PH_4__+__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and __TRILIUM_PH_6__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_7__+__TRILIUM_PH_8__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_9__+__TRILIUM_PH_10__-__TRILIUM_PH_11__ can be used.

units.context: Zoom > Adjusting the text size instead

units.source: As an alternative to the zoom, the text size can be individually adjusted by going to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Appearance__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Zoom > Adjusting the text size instead

units.source: The note tooltip is a convenience feature which displays a popup when hovering over an __TRILIUM_PH_0__internal link__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to another note.
The note path, at the top of the popup.
Clicking on the title will open the note in the current tab.
Holding __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ pressed while clicking the title will open in a new tab instead of the current one.
A snippet of the content will be displayed as well.
A button to __TRILIUM_PH_0__quickly edit__TRILIUM_PH_1__ the note in a popup.

For a link to blocks of the note the link is in, the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Jump to block__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button takes its place, or __TRILIUM_PH_3__Jump to heading__TRILIUM_PH_4__ for a heading, and scrolls to them without leaving the note.

For a link to an __TRILIUM_PH_0__attachment__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the tooltip shows the attachment instead: its title after the path of the note that owns it, a line giving its size (for example __TRILIUM_PH_2__Attachment • 20.59 MiB__TRILIUM_PH_3__), a preview of its content where one is available, and the quick edit button opening the attachment.
The tooltip can be found in multiple places, including:
In __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes, when hovering over __TRILIUM_PH_2__Internal (reference) links__TRILIUM_PH_3__ .
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Geo Map View__TRILIUM_PH_1__, when hovering over a marker.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Calendar View__TRILIUM_PH_1__, when hovering over an event.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Table View__TRILIUM_PH_1__, when hovering over a note title, or over a __TRILIUM_PH_2__relation__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

Split view is a feature of __TRILIUM_PH_0__Mermaid Diagrams__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Markdown__TRILIUM_PH_3__ notes which displays both the source code on one side and the preview of the content on the other.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Mermaid Diagrams__TRILIUM_PH_1__ also allow changing between a horizontal or a vertical split, to accommodate for the various sizes of diagrams.

units.context: Note types with split view > Display modes and interaction

units.source: The split comes with three different display modes which can be toggled from the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note buttons__TRILIUM_PH_1__ area:
units.context: Note types with split view > Display modes and interaction

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__(Split view)__TRILIUM_PH_2__, in which both the source code is available on one side and can be edited, and the preview is available on the other side.
units.context: Note types with split view > Display modes and interaction

units.source: In this mode, the size of either the source pane or the preview pane can be adjusted by dragging the small border between them.
units.context: Note types with split view > Display modes and interaction

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ (__TRILIUM_PH_1__Source view)__TRILIUM_PH_2__ which shows the source code on the entire screen for a more focused editing experience.
units.context: Note types with split view > Display modes and interaction

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__(Preview)__TRILIUM_PH_2__ which displays only the rendering of the diagram or text in full screen, especially useful for read-only notes.
units.context: Note types with split view > Display modes and interaction

units.source: The display node is stored at note level.
units.context: Note types with split view > Display modes and interaction

units.source: A Markdown note included in a text note, or a Markdown file embedded in one, has the same three display modes, switched from the title row and the toolbar of the include. See __TRILIUM_PH_0__Included Markdown__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in __TRILIUM_PH_2__Include Note__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Note types with split view > Display modes and interaction
Note types with split view > Relation to read-only notes

units.source: If a note is marked as __TRILIUM_PH_0__read-only__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the source view will not be editable. While in preview mode, marking a note as read-only has no effect since the preview itself is not editable.
units.context: Note types with split view > Relation to read-only notes

units.source: Some note types (such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and saved search) intentionally limit the width of the content.

This might appear surprising at first, but the idea is to make text fit well on wider screens without appearing distorted. This is especially the case if the document contains __TRILIUM_PH_0__Images__TRILIUM_PH_1__, tables or other width-dependent elements.
Configuring the content width and alignment__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Content width > Configuring the content width and alignment

units.source: The content width is expressed in pixels and can be changed from __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Appearance__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Content Width__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and adjusting the __TRILIUM_PH_6__Max content width__TRILIUM_PH_7__ section.
units.context: Content width > Configuring the content width and alignment

units.source: To effectively disable the content width limitation, simply set the width to a value larger than your screen size (e.g. 9999).
units.context: Content width > Configuring the content width and alignment

units.source: By default, the content is aligned to the left, but it can be centered horizontally by checking __TRILIUM_PH_0__Keep content centered__TRILIUM_PH_1__ from the same section as the content width.
units.context: Content width > Configuring the content width and alignment
Content width > Adjusting at note level

units.source: For notes with large elements such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Tables__TRILIUM_PH_1__, it sometimes makes sense to avoid the content width without affecting other notes. To do so:
units.context: Content width > Adjusting at note level

units.source: Go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and toggle __TRILIUM_PH_2__Full width__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Content width > Adjusting at note level

units.source: Or manually apply the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__label__TRILIUM_PH_2__ to the note.
units.context: Content width > Adjusting at note level

units.source: Since v0.107.0, a single table can also be made wider than the content width, in which case it scrolls sideways. See __TRILIUM_PH_0__Tables__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Content width > Adjusting at note level

units.source: Some __TRILIUM_PH_0__note types__TRILIUM_PH_1__ are full width by default, such as the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Canvas__TRILIUM_PH_3__. In that case the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Full width__TRILIUM_PH_5__ toggle will not be displayed and the label will have no effect.
units.context: Content width > Adjusting at note level

units.source: On a __TRILIUM_PH_0__shared page__TRILIUM_PH_1__, a text note is shown at a fixed reading width, whatever the width configured in Options, and the navigation tree, the content and the table of contents are kept together in a column centered on a wide screen. A note with __TRILIUM_PH_2__, or of a type that is full width in the application, uses the whole width of the window there, with the navigation tree and the table of contents at its edges.
Right-clicking the content of some note types such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Code__TRILIUM_PH_3__ reveals a contextual menu.

In a text note being edited, right-clicking a link opens the menu of the link instead, the same as its __TRILIUM_PH_0__More actions__TRILIUM_PH_1__ menu (see __TRILIUM_PH_2__External links__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Internal (reference) links__TRILIUM_PH_5__). A selection holding the link and more text keeps the contextual menu.
On the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Desktop Installation__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Spell Check__TRILIUM_PH_3__ suggestions are shown when right clicking on a misspelled word.

The selected text can be searched either with a search engine (configured in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Other__TRILIUM_PH_3__) or __TRILIUM_PH_4__inside Trilium__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
To remove the web search from the menu, choose __TRILIUM_PH_0__None__TRILIUM_PH_1__ as the search engine.
Performing quick operations using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__In-editor AI assistant__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
