units.source: The status bar displays information about the current note and allows changing settings related to it such as configuring the language or attributes.
On the left side, the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Breadcrumb__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is displayed which indicates the current note as well as its parent notes and allows for quick navigation throughout the hierarchy.
On the right side, specific sections will show depending on the type of the current note.
For __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes, the language mode of the note is indicated (e.g. JavaScript, plain text), as well as allowing easy switching to another mode.

Before it, the position of the cursor is shown as a line and a column, such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ln: 12 Col: 32__TRILIUM_PH_1__. It updates as the cursor moves. While text is selected, the number of selected characters follows, such as __TRILIUM_PH_2__Selected: 120__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
For __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes, the content language is displayed and can be changed, thus configuring the spell-check and the right-to-left support.
Note that this applies to the entire note and not the selection, unlike some text editors.
If a note is placed in multiple places in the tree (cloned), the number of the note paths will be displayed.

Clicking it opens a popup with the full list of note paths, from which the note can also be cloned to a new location. The same list is available in the sidebar's __TRILIUM_PH_0__Connections tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
If a note has attachments, their number will be displayed.
Clicking on it will reveal the list of attachments in a new tab.
If a note is linked from other text notes (backlinks), the number of backlinks will be displayed.

Clicking on it opens a popup with the list of notes that link to this note, as well as an excerpt of where the note is referenced. The same list is available in the sidebar's __TRILIUM_PH_0__Connections tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Regardless of note type, the following items will always be displayed if there is a note:
The creation/modification date of the note.
The type and MIME of the note.
An estimation of the note size of the note itself and its children.
A button to reveal the Similar notes in the sidebar's __TRILIUM_PH_0__Connections tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

When pressing a button which reveals the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Right Sidebar__TRILIUM_PH_1__, it has a specific behavior if the sidebar is hidden: the sidebar will be peeked instead of docked. Regardless the sidebar will be switched to the appropriate tab and the corresponding section will be highlighted.
The breadcrumb allows quickly viewing the note hierarchy of the current note and navigating through it.
It is part of the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Status bar__TRILIUM_PH_1__, displayed in the bottom-left of the screen.
If a note or workspace is hoisted, a badge will appear on the left-most side.
Clicking on the badge will un-hoist the note/workspace.
The left-most icon represents the root note, or the hoisted note or workspace.
Clicking the icon will jump to the root note.
Right clicking the icon will display a menu that allows opening the note in a new tab, split, etc.
Each segment shows the title of a note in the current note hierarchy.
Clicking the icon will jump to that note.

Right clicking will open a menu with multiple options such as opening the note in a different tab/split/window, hoisting, moving/cloning the note, duplicating as well as changing the color of the note.
Clicking the arrow next to each segment will reveal the child notes of the segment on the left.
Clicking on an icon will navigate to that particular note.
To find a child note by its title, start typing: the field at the bottom of the menu filters the list.
It's also possible to create a new child note from here.
The menu can optionally hide the archived notes.
If the current note is deep within a hierarchy, the segments will collapse into a […] button in order not to occupy too much space.
Clicking this button will display each collapsed entry as a menu item. Clicking on it will navigate to that particular note.
Right clicking on an empty space to the right of the breadcrumb (before the other status bar items) will reveal another menu that allows:
Toggling whether archived notes are displayed in the breadcrumb and in the note tree.
Copying the current note path to clipboard.

Alongside its content, the __TRILIUM_PH_0__title__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is one of the two main attributes of a __TRILIUM_PH_2__note__TRILIUM_PH_3__. It's the short, human-readable name shown in the editable field at the top of every note, and it's what identifies the note throughout the interface (in the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_5__, in tabs, in the __TRILIUM_PH_6__Breadcrumb__TRILIUM_PH_7__ and win __TRILIUM_PH_8__Internal (reference) links__TRILIUM_PH_9__.
Internally, notes are identified by a unique __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note ID__TRILIUM_PH_1__ rather than by their title, so the title is purely for your benefit. This has a few consequences:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Titles don't have to be unique.__TRILIUM_PH_1__ You can have any number of notes that share the same title without conflict.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Renaming a note never breaks links to it.__TRILIUM_PH_1__ Links between notes point at the underlying note, so changing a title leaves existing links intact (they'll simply display the new title).
__TRILIUM_PH_0__The title can be left empty.__TRILIUM_PH_1__ Notes with no title display a placeholder (__TRILIUM_PH_2__type note's title here…__TRILIUM_PH_3__) but are otherwise perfectly valid.
There is no limitation on the length of the title, however in exports the title might get trimmed.
There are no forbidden symbols, unsupported characters will get trimmed when exporting.
When exporting to a ZIP file, a meta file will contain the full title which will be recognized by Trilium when importing again.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes have a special title bar behavior in which the __TRILIUM_PH_2__note title__TRILIUM_PH_3__ is initially displayed in a larger font, while also displaying additional information such as the creation and the modification date.
Whenever the title is scrolled past, the fixed title is shown instead.
Note types that take the entirety of the screen, such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Canvas__TRILIUM_PH_3__, will always have only the fixed title bar.
Under the note title, the __TRILIUM_PH_0__New note type switcher__TRILIUM_PH_1__ appears if the note is empty.

To use the fixed title bar for text notes as well, go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Appearance__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__User Interface__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and set __TRILIUM_PH_6__Note title__TRILIUM_PH_7__ to __TRILIUM_PH_8__Compact__TRILIUM_PH_9__. The title then stays in the fixed title bar and the content starts right below it; the creation and modification dates are not shown. The __TRILIUM_PH_10__New note type switcher__TRILIUM_PH_11__ of an empty note appears at the bottom of the note instead. The setting applies to the current device only.
The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Inline title__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which is displayed at the top of the note and can be scrolled past.
The fixed title bar. The title only appears after scrolling past the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Inline title__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

units.context: Title > Inline title > Editing the title

units.source: To rename a note, simply click into the title field and type. Changes are saved automatically as you type.
units.context: Title > Inline title > Editing the title

units.source: You can also begin editing the title directly from the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ by selecting a note and pressing __TRILIUM_PH_2__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_3__ (see __TRILIUM_PH_4__Edit note title__TRILIUM_PH_5__ in __TRILIUM_PH_6__Keyboard Shortcuts__TRILIUM_PH_7__), which focuses the title field for the active note.
units.context: Title > Inline title > Editing the title

units.source: Titles may contain any characters, including Unicode and emoji. For security, any HTML in the title is stripped automatically, so the title is always treated as plain text.
units.context: Title > Inline title > Editing the title

units.source: Easily navigating between the title and the content__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Title > Inline title > Easily navigating between the title and the content

units.source: When the cursor is in the title field, pressing __TRILIUM_PH_0__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_1__ moves focus into the note's content. For __TRILIUM_PH_2__Text__TRILIUM_PH_3__ notes this also inserts a fresh empty paragraph at the very top of the document, so you can start writing immediately — much like other note-taking apps.
units.context: Title > Inline title > Easily navigating between the title and the content

units.source: This makes it possible to create a note, type its title, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_1__, and continue straight into the body without reaching for the mouse.
units.context: Title > Inline title > Easily navigating between the title and the content
Title > Inline title > Working with new notes

units.source: When you create a new note it's given a default title (__TRILIUM_PH_0__new note__TRILIUM_PH_1__) which is pre-selected, so you can type a name right away to replace it. The default title for new notes can be customized per-section — see __TRILIUM_PH_2__Default Note Title__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Title > Inline title > Working with new notes

units.source: If you decide you don't want the note after all, pressing __TRILIUM_PH_0__Escape__TRILIUM_PH_1__ while the title of a freshly created note is still focused will discard it.
units.context: Title > Inline title > Working with new notes

units.source: Some notes get their titles assigned automatically rather than typed:
units.context: Title > Inline title > Automatically generated titles

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Day, week, month and year notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Day Notes__TRILIUM_PH_3__ are named from a configurable date pattern.
units.context: Title > Inline title > Automatically generated titles

units.context: Title > Inline title > Automatically generated titles

units.source: The titles of __TRILIUM_PH_0__Protected Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ are encrypted along with their content. Before entering your password, Trilium cannot decrypt the title: the note tree, the title field, the breadcrumb menus and the tabs label the note __TRILIUM_PH_2__Protected__TRILIUM_PH_3__, and the title cannot be modified.
Once you enter your password and a protected session is active, the real title is decrypted and displayed, and becomes editable again.

Icons are useful for distinguishing notes and are displayed near the note title, as well as in various places such as the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Internal (reference) links__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Jump to & command palette__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
While editing a note, click on the icon next to the title to bring up a chooser gallery.
Icons can be inherited through the use of __TRILIUM_PH_0__Templates__TRILIUM_PH_1__, or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Attribute Inheritance__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

At the technical level, they are set by the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ attribute which adds a CSS class to the note. For example __TRILIUM_PH_1__ will show a calendar instead of the default page or folder icon. Looking up and remembering the CSS class names is not necessary.

Notes can also carry a custom color. Similar to the note icon, this color will be shown in various places such as the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Internal (reference) links__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
To set a custom color, right click on the note in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and select a predefined color from there or use the color picker (last option).

Alternatively, a custom color can be set manually through the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__label__TRILIUM_PH_2__, whose value must be a valid hex color including the leading __TRILIUM_PH_3__ (e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_4__ for red). This color can be carried over across multiple notes via __TRILIUM_PH_5__Attribute Inheritance__TRILIUM_PH_6__.

A __TRILIUM_PH_0__note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in Trilium can __TRILIUM_PH_2__own__TRILIUM_PH_3__ one or more attachments, which can be either images or files. These attachments can be displayed or linked within the note that owns them.

This can be especially useful to include dependencies for your __TRILIUM_PH_0__scripts__TRILIUM_PH_1__. The __TRILIUM_PH_2__Weight Tracker__TRILIUM_PH_3__ shows how to use __TRILIUM_PH_4__chartjs__TRILIUM_PH_5__ which is attached to the script note.

Each note exclusively owns its attachments, meaning attachments cannot be shared or linked from one note to another. If an attachment link is copied to a different note, the attachment itself is duplicated, and the copies are managed independently thereafter.

Attachments, especially image files, are the recommended method for embedding visuals in notes. It is important to link image attachments within the text of the owning note; otherwise, they will be automatically deleted after a configurable timeout period if not referenced.
There are two different types of attachment:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__User content__TRILIUM_PH_1__, representing files or images that are uploaded and part of the content of the note.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__System attachments__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which are used internally by Trilium and can be of multiple types, including:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to store information about views such as the column information for the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Kanban Board__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
Icons and cover images for __TRILIUM_PH_0__Link Previews__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Debug information for some importers such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Microsoft OneNote__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (only if the debug flag was enabled at import time).
The transcript of a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Meeting transcription__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which is also shown above the note's content.

The SVG picture of a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Canvas__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note (__TRILIUM_PH_2__), and of each drawing canvas in a text note (see __TRILIUM_PH_3__Drawing canvases__TRILIUM_PH_4__ in __TRILIUM_PH_5__Include Note__TRILIUM_PH_6__), used for previews and shared pages.
The system attachments are displayed at the end of the attachments list, in a dedicated section (__TRILIUM_PH_0__Generated by Trilium__TRILIUM_PH_1__).
The __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Attachments__TRILIUM_PH_2__ item of the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_4__ opens the list of the note's attachments.
To upload files as attachments, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Upload attachments__TRILIUM_PH_1__ at the top of the list and select one or more files.

Alternatively, drag one or more files from the file explorer and drop them anywhere on the list. Pictures are compressed if __TRILIUM_PH_0__Automatic image compression__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is enabled in __TRILIUM_PH_2__Options__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Media__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
Attaching files from a text note__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Attachments > Attaching files from a text note

units.source: To attach files to a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note and embed them in its content, press the __TRILIUM_PH_2____TRILIUM_PH_3__Attach file__TRILIUM_PH_4__ button in the __TRILIUM_PH_5__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_6__, choose __TRILIUM_PH_7__Attach and embed file__TRILIUM_PH_8__ and select one or more files (see __TRILIUM_PH_9__Embedding an attachment__TRILIUM_PH_10__ below). The same menu offers __TRILIUM_PH_11__Image__TRILIUM_PH_12__, which inserts pictures (see __TRILIUM_PH_13__Images__TRILIUM_PH_14__), and __TRILIUM_PH_15__Attach file as a link__TRILIUM_PH_16__, which links the files instead. Both file actions are also available as __TRILIUM_PH_17__Attach file as a link__TRILIUM_PH_18__ and __TRILIUM_PH_19__Attach and embed file__TRILIUM_PH_20__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_21__Slash Commands__TRILIUM_PH_22__. On a phone, the menu also offers __TRILIUM_PH_23__Camera__TRILIUM_PH_24__ (see __TRILIUM_PH_25__Mobile Frontend__TRILIUM_PH_26__).
units.context: Attachments > Attaching files from a text note

units.source: When files are attached as links:
units.context: Attachments > Attaching files from a text note

units.source: Each file becomes an attachment of the note, and a link to it is inserted at the cursor. Several files produce several links, separated by a space.
units.context: Attachments > Attaching files from a text note

units.source: While a file uploads, its link shows the file name and a toast shows the progress.
units.context: Attachments > Attaching files from a text note

units.source: Pictures appear as links rather than images, and are attached exactly as they are, without being compressed. To display a picture in the text, use __TRILIUM_PH_0__Image__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in the same menu instead (see __TRILIUM_PH_2__Images__TRILIUM_PH_3__).
units.context: Attachments > Attaching files from a text note

units.source: Dragging a file that is not a picture from the file explorer onto the text also attaches it and inserts a link to it.
units.context: Attachments > Attaching files from a text note
Attachments > Acting on an attachment link

units.source: Right-clicking a link to an attachment shows the ways to open it, followed by actions on the attachment: opening it externally, downloading it, uploading a new revision, renaming or deleting it, and converting it into a note. In a text note being edited, the same entries are in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__More actions__TRILIUM_PH_2__ menu of the popup of the link, which right-clicking the link opens. The popup also has a __TRILIUM_PH_3__ __TRILIUM_PH_4__Download__TRILIUM_PH_5__ button.
units.context: Attachments > Acting on an attachment link

units.source: Links follow changes to their attachment: renaming it updates the title they show, and deleting it removes them from the text notes open for editing at that moment. Converting it into a note turns its links into links to the new note.
units.context: Attachments > Acting on an attachment link

units.source: An attachment can be shown in the text instead of linked, the way __TRILIUM_PH_0__Include Note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ shows a note: a picture is displayed, a PDF, a video or a document is previewed, a code or text file is shown with syntax highlighting, and a Markdown file such as a __TRILIUM_PH_2__ file is shown rendered. An embedded code file can also be edited in place (see __TRILIUM_PH_3__Editing an include in place__TRILIUM_PH_4__ in __TRILIUM_PH_5__Include Note__TRILIUM_PH_6__), and an embedded Markdown file shows its source, its rendering or both, as an included Markdown note does (see __TRILIUM_PH_7__Included Markdown__TRILIUM_PH_8__ there).

To attach files and embed them straight away, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Attach file__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button and choose __TRILIUM_PH_3__Attach and embed file__TRILIUM_PH_4__. Each file gets an embed of its own, which shows the file name while the file uploads.
To embed an attachment that is already linked, right-click a link to it in a text note being edited and select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Convert link to an embed__TRILIUM_PH_1__, near the end of the menu.

A drawing canvas, inserted with __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Drawing canvas__TRILIUM_PH_2__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_3____TRILIUM_PH_4__Insert__TRILIUM_PH_5__ menu, is an embed of a __TRILIUM_PH_6__ attachment that can be drawn on in place. An attached Excalidraw file (__TRILIUM_PH_7__) is embedded as a drawing canvas too (see __TRILIUM_PH_8__Drawing canvases__TRILIUM_PH_9__ in __TRILIUM_PH_10__Include Note__TRILIUM_PH_11__).

An embed gets the box size that suits the attachment, as a new included note does (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Box sizes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ there). To change its size, select the embed and use the box size menu in its toolbar, or the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Size__TRILIUM_PH_3__ submenu of its __TRILIUM_PH_4____TRILIUM_PH_5__More actions__TRILIUM_PH_6__ menu. A __TRILIUM_PH_7__Resizable__TRILIUM_PH_8__ embed can also be resized by dragging its handles, and an __TRILIUM_PH_9__Expandable__TRILIUM_PH_10__ one in height (see __TRILIUM_PH_11__Resizing__TRILIUM_PH_12__ there). A __TRILIUM_PH_13__Resizable__TRILIUM_PH_14__ embed can be placed at the left or the right of the note, with or without the text running beside it, from the __TRILIUM_PH_15__Position__TRILIUM_PH_16__ submenu of its menu (see __TRILIUM_PH_17__Positioning__TRILIUM_PH_18__ there).
An embed can have a caption, as an included note can (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Caption__TRILIUM_PH_1__ there).

To show only the attachment, turn off __TRILIUM_PH_0__Show title__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in the embed's __TRILIUM_PH_2____TRILIUM_PH_3__More actions__TRILIUM_PH_4__ menu, as for an included note (see __TRILIUM_PH_5__Title__TRILIUM_PH_6__ there).
To open the attachment in a new tab, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ (__TRILIUM_PH_1__Open in new tab)__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button at the end of the embed's title.

An embed of size __TRILIUM_PH_0__Compact__TRILIUM_PH_1__ shows only the title of the attachment and its size, in a single row, whatever the attachment is: a drawing canvas or a video shows nothing of its content there. Its buttons are __TRILIUM_PH_2____TRILIUM_PH_3__Open externally__TRILIUM_PH_4__ and __TRILIUM_PH_5____TRILIUM_PH_6__Download__TRILIUM_PH_7__. An audio file at __TRILIUM_PH_8__Compact__TRILIUM_PH_9__ is a row of player controls instead, without its title until __TRILIUM_PH_10__Show title__TRILIUM_PH_11__ is turned on.

To show an embed of size __TRILIUM_PH_0__Resizable__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Full__TRILIUM_PH_3__ on the whole screen, press the __TRILIUM_PH_4__ (__TRILIUM_PH_5__Fullscreen)__TRILIUM_PH_6__ button at the end of its title. To return, press __TRILIUM_PH_7__ (__TRILIUM_PH_8__Exit fullscreen)__TRILIUM_PH_9__ in the top-right corner, or __TRILIUM_PH_10__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_11__.

To turn the embed back into a link, choose __TRILIUM_PH_0__Convert to link__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in the menu that right-clicking the title row of the embed or pressing its __TRILIUM_PH_2____TRILIUM_PH_3__More actions__TRILIUM_PH_4__ button opens. It is in the last group, after __TRILIUM_PH_5____TRILIUM_PH_6__Delete block__TRILIUM_PH_7__, which removes the embed from the note, and __TRILIUM_PH_8____TRILIUM_PH_9__Delete attachment...__TRILIUM_PH_10__, which deletes the attachment itself. __TRILIUM_PH_11____TRILIUM_PH_12__Convert attachment into note...__TRILIUM_PH_13__ follows it.

An embed follows its attachment like a link does. Converting the attachment into a note turns the embed into an included note. Since a single note can appear into multiple places in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ via a process called __TRILIUM_PH_2__Cloning Notes__TRILIUM_PH_3__, it's recommended to choose a generalized name that fits into all locations instead of something more specific to avoid confusion.
In some cases this isn't possible so Trilium provides "branch prefixes", which is shown before the note name in the tree and as such provides a specific kind of context.
The prefix is location-specific, so it's displayed only in the note tree.
Trilium's core feature is the ability to structure your notes into hierarchical tree-like structure.
It is expected then that you'll have an elaborate and deep note hierarchy - each subtree will represent a more refined and specialized view of your knowledge base.
This is a pretty powerful approach, but it also carries a hidden assumption that each "subtopic" is "owned" by one parent. I'll illustrate this with an example - let's say my basic structure is this:

Now, I'm starting to learn about __TRILIUM_PH_0__Bash__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and would like to create notes related to this topic. But now I'm facing a problem of where to categorize this. The issue here is that Bash is both a programming language and a tool (shell) very much tied into Linux. It seems it belongs to both of these, I can't (and don't want to) choose one over the other.
The solution to the problem shown above is to allow notes to have multiple parents.
I call these "clones", but that is a bit misleading - there's no original and cloned note - the notes in both of the parents categories are identical.

Another misleading thing about "cloning" is that it suggests that a copy of the note has been made. That's not really true, the note itself stays in just one original, it is just referenced in multiple places in the tree hierarchy. So changing it in one category changes it in all the others, because they're all the same note.
Here's the final structure with cloning:
So now the "Bash" subtree appears on multiple locations in the hierarchy. Both the Bash subtrees are the same and contain the same sub-categories and notes.

In the demo, you can see how a clone can be created using the context menu. It's possible to do this also using the Add Link dialog or with __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__C__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_5__+__TRILIUM_PH_6__V__TRILIUM_PH_7__ __TRILIUM_PH_8__keyboard shortcuts__TRILIUM_PH_9__.
You can view the list of all available clones:
In the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Status bar__TRILIUM_PH_1__, by looking for the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ icon.
In the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Connections tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Right Sidebar__TRILIUM_PH_3__, by looking at the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Note paths__TRILIUM_PH_5__ section.

In the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__, on desktop and on mobile, the title of a cloned note is followed by a __TRILIUM_PH_2__ icon, to easily see that the note is also placed into some other location. A shared note is followed by a __TRILIUM_PH_3__ icon in the same way.
With clones, it might not be immediately obvious how deleting works.
If you try to delete a note, it works like this:
if the note has multiple clones, delete just this clone and leave the actual note (and its other clones) as it is.
if this note doesn't have any other clones, delete the note
Run the whole process starting with 1. on all note's children notes

Trilium is designed to store a wide variety of data, including sensitive information such as personal journals, credentials, or confidential documents. To safeguard this type of content, Trilium offers the option to protect notes, which involves the following measures:

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Encryption:__TRILIUM_PH_1__ Protected notes are encrypted using a key derived from your password. This ensures that without the correct password, protected notes remain indecipherable. Even if someone gains access to your Trilium __TRILIUM_PH_2__database__TRILIUM_PH_3__, they won't be able to read your encrypted notes.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Time-limited access:__TRILIUM_PH_1__ To access protected notes, you must first enter your password, which decrypts the note for reading and writing. However, after a specified period of inactivity (10 minutes by default), the note is unloaded from memory, requiring you to re-enter your password to access it again.

The session timeout is extended automatically while you're interacting with the protected note, so if you're actively editing, the session remains open. However, if you switch to an unprotected note, the session timer starts, and the session expires after 10 minutes of inactivity unless you return to the protected notes.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Protection scope:__TRILIUM_PH_1__ Protected notes ensure the confidentiality of their content and partially their integrity. While unauthorized users cannot read or edit protected notes, they can still delete or move them outside of the protected session.
By default, notes are unprotected. To protect a note, simply click on the shield icon next to the note's title, as shown here:
Trilium encrypts the data within protected notes but not their metadata. Specifically:
Note structure (i.e., it remains visible that there are protected notes)
Metadata, such as the last modified date
The following steps outline how encryption and decryption work in Trilium:
The password is passed through the __TRILIUM_PH_0__scrypt__TRILIUM_PH_1__ algorithm along with a "password verification" __TRILIUM_PH_2__salt__TRILIUM_PH_3__ to confirm that the password is correct.
The password is then processed again through scrypt with an "encryption" salt, which generates a hash.
Scrypt is used for __TRILIUM_PH_0__key stretching__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to make the password harder to guess.
The generated hash is used to decrypt the actual __TRILIUM_PH_0__data encryption key__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
The data encryption key is encrypted using __TRILIUM_PH_0__AES-128__TRILIUM_PH_1__ with a random __TRILIUM_PH_2__IV__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

The data encryption key is randomly generated during the __TRILIUM_PH_0__database__TRILIUM_PH_1__ initialization and remains constant throughout the document’s lifetime. When the password is changed, only this key is re-encrypted.
The data encryption key is then used to decrypt the actual content of the note, including its title and body.
The encryption algorithm used is AES-128 with __TRILIUM_PH_0__CBC mode__TRILIUM_PH_1__, where a unique IV is generated for each encryption operation and stored with the cipher text.
Protected notes cannot be shared in the same way as regular notes. Their encryption ensures that only authorized users with the correct password can access them.

Such notes are then by default not shown in the autocomplete and in the full text __TRILIUM_PH_0__search__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

Trilium supports seamless versioning of notes by storing snapshots ("revisions") of notes at regular intervals.
To display the revisions, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and select __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note revisions…__TRILIUM_PH_3__ (__TRILIUM_PH_4__).
This documentation matches the redesign of the note revisions dialog on v0.103.0, older versions have a similar dialog but with some differences.
The full list of revisions are displayed on the left in reverse chronological order.
The revisions are grouped by the date the revision was taken.
This list does not contain the __TRILIUM_PH_0__current state__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of the note, so it is possible to have notes with no revisions/snapshots saved.
The icon of a revision indicates the __TRILIUM_PH_0__source__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of that revision (e.g. a __TRILIUM_PH_2__ icon for a manually saved revision).

Checking the interval and limit for this note (see below).

For supported notes (text, code), changes are highlighted. This behavior can be toggled via the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Highlight changes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ at the top of the dialog.
The highlighted changes are relative to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__current state of the note__TRILIUM_PH_1__, not to the revision prior to this one.
For any given revision, the buttons on the top-right allow operating on it:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ Restoring the revision, which replaces the current content of the note with the one from the revision. Another revision is saved containing the current content of the note.
Named revisions are a new feature of Trilium v0.103.0 which allows adding a short description of what the changes in the snapshot contain.

units.source: The value of __TRILIUM_PH_0__ is a comma-separated list of levels, written like the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ of a __TRILIUM_PH_2__search__TRILIUM_PH_3__. Each level is one of:
A label on the child notes, written with __TRILIUM_PH_0__, such as __TRILIUM_PH_1__.
One of the properties __TRILIUM_PH_0__, __TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__, written without __TRILIUM_PH_3__.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__, which only the notes with children of their own have (see __TRILIUM_PH_1__Grouping__TRILIUM_PH_2__ below).
A level can be followed by __TRILIUM_PH_0__ or __TRILIUM_PH_1__ to set its direction; otherwise it follows __TRILIUM_PH_2__.

The child notes are sorted by the first level. Notes that are equal at that level are sorted by the second level, and so on. Notes equal at every level are sorted by title, in the direction of __TRILIUM_PH_0__.
A child note that doesn't have a level's label is placed after every child that has it, whichever direction the level runs in. Between two notes that both lack it, the next level decides.

sorts them as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Taxes__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Book report__TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__Groceries__TRILIUM_PH_5__, __TRILIUM_PH_6__Ideas__TRILIUM_PH_7__. A value that is a single name without __TRILIUM_PH_0__ is read the way older versions did: __TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__ or __TRILIUM_PH_3__ is a property, and any other name is a label, so __TRILIUM_PH_4__ sorts by the __TRILIUM_PH_5__ label of the children.

In v0.106.0 the names were written bare, as in __TRILIUM_PH_2__; such a value now reads both names as properties that don't exist, and the notes fall back to sorting by title. When a note is in read-only mode, it is presented to the user in a non-editable view, with the option to switch to editing mode if needed.

For optimization purposes, Trilium will automatically set very large notes to read-only. Displaying such lengthy notes in editing mode can slow down performance, especially when editing is unnecessary.
This behavior can be disabled on a per-note basis, by following the instructions of the next section.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Execute badge__TRILIUM_PH_2__, for __TRILIUM_PH_3__scripts__TRILIUM_PH_4__ or __TRILIUM_PH_5__saved SQL queries__TRILIUM_PH_6__ which have an execute button or a description.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Template badge__TRILIUM_PH_2__, for __TRILIUM_PH_3__Templates__TRILIUM_PH_4__ (including workspace templates, for which the badge reads __TRILIUM_PH_5__Workspace template__TRILIUM_PH_6__). Notes created from a template inherit its attributes, so the badge is a reminder that changing them affects every such note. Clicking the badge switches the template between being offered everywhere and only while hoisted into its workspace, the latter only for a template inside a workspace (see __TRILIUM_PH_7__Workspaces__TRILIUM_PH_8__). It also opens __TRILIUM_PH_9__Template properties...__TRILIUM_PH_10__, where the default title and location of new notes are set.
For __TRILIUM_PH_0__Active content__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (e.g. scripts, styles), a dedicated badge will be shown indicating the type of note and with an option to easily enable or disable it.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Saving__TRILIUM_PH_2__, if the changes are being saved.

In a text note, the changes are saved once typing pauses for a second, and at least every ten seconds while typing continues.
After all changes have been saved, the indicator will hide automatically after a few seconds.
Note is a central entity in Trilium. Main attributes of note are __TRILIUM_PH_0__title__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and content.

The main note type is a rich-text note type called __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__. For diagrams and drawing there is __TRILIUM_PH_2__Canvas__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Mermaid Diagrams__TRILIUM_PH_5__.

There are also more complex note types such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Saved Search__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Render Note__TRILIUM_PH_3__ that usually go hand-in-hand with __TRILIUM_PH_4__Scripting__TRILIUM_PH_5__.

In Trilium there's no specific "folder" note type. Any note can have children and thus be a folder. To make a note that only shows its children, like a folder in other applications, use a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Grid View__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__List View__TRILIUM_PH_3__ collection. See also __TRILIUM_PH_4__FAQ__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
There's one special note called "root note" which is root of the note tree. All other notes are placed below it in the structure.
Importantly, note itself doesn't carry information on its placement in note tree. See __TRILIUM_PH_0__Cloning Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for details.

Tree structure of notes can resemble file system - but compared to that notes in Trilium can act as both file and directory - meaning that note can both have its own content and have children. "Leaf note" is a note which doesn't have any children.
When you delete a note in Trilium, it is actually only marked for deletion (soft-delete) - the actual content, title, attributes etc. are not deleted, only hidden.

Within (by default) 7 days, it is possible to undelete these soft-deleted notes - open the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Recent Changes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ dialog, and you will see a list of all modified notes including the deleted ones. Notes available for undeletion have a link to do so. This is kind of "trash can" functionality known from e.g. Windows.

Clicking an undelete will recover the note, its content and attributes - note should be just as before being deleted. This action will also undelete note's children which have been deleted in the same action.

To be able to undelete a note, it is necessary that deleted note's parent must be undeleted (otherwise there's no place where we can undelete it to). This might become a problem when you delete more notes in succession - the solution is then undelete in the reverse order of your deletion.

After the 7 days (configurable) the notes will be "erased" - their title, content, revisions and attributes will be erased, and it will not be possible anymore to recover them (unless you restore a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Backup__TRILIUM_PH_1__).
This page explains the basic concepts related to the tree structure of notes in TriliumNext.
A note is the central entity in TriliumNext. For more details, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

A branch describes the placement of a note within the note tree. Essentially, it is a tuple of __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and __TRILIUM_PH_1__, indicating that the given note is placed as a child under the specified parent note.
Each note can have multiple branches, meaning any note can be placed in multiple locations within the tree. This concept is referred to as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Cloning Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

A prefix is a branch-specific title modifier for a note. If you place your note in two different locations within the tree and want to alter the title slightly in one of those placements, you can use a prefix.
To edit a prefix, right-click on the note in the tree pane and select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Edit branch prefix__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

The prefix is not part of the note itself and is not encrypted when the note is protected. This can be useful if you want part of the title to remain visible in the tree for easier navigation, even when the note is protected.
A subtree consists of a particular note (the subtree root) and all its children and descendants. Some operations, such as exporting, work on entire subtrees.
One of the Trilium's goals is to provide fast and comfortable navigation between notes.

To move back and forward in the history of viewed notes, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__←__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_5__+__TRILIUM_PH_6__→__TRILIUM_PH_7__, or use the __TRILIUM_PH_8__ and __TRILIUM_PH_9__ buttons to the left of the __TRILIUM_PH_10__Tabs__TRILIUM_PH_11__.
This works identically to browser backwards / forwards, it's actually using built-in browser support for this.

To go several notes back or forward at once, right-click one of the buttons or press and hold it. The back button lists the notes before the current one and the forward button the notes after it, the nearest first. Each entry shows the note's title, with the path of its parent notes at the end of the row. Selecting a note goes straight to it.

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Go to Previous Note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Go to Next Note__TRILIUM_PH_3__ launchers of the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_5__ list the same notes, below the launch bar's own items.

This is useful to quickly find and view arbitrary notes - click on __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button on the top or press __TRILIUM_PH_1__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_2__ + __TRILIUM_PH_3__J__TRILIUM_PH_4__ . Then type part of the note name and autocomplete will help you pick the desired note.
See __TRILIUM_PH_0__Jump to Note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for more information.

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Quick search__TRILIUM_PH_1__ function does a full-text search (that is, it searches through the content of notes and not just the title of a note) and displays the result in an easy-to-access manner.
The alternative to the quick search is the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search__TRILIUM_PH_1__ function, which opens in a dedicated tab and has support for advanced queries.
For even faster navigation, it's possible to use __TRILIUM_PH_0__Jump to & command palette__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which will only search through the note titles instead of the content.
Based on the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Vertical and horizontal layout__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the quick search is placed:
On the vertical layout, it is displayed right above the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
On the horizontal layout, it is displayed in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_1__, where it can be positioned just like any other icon.

Under the hood > Progressive Search Strategy

units.source: Trilium uses a progressive search strategy that performs exact matching first, then adds fuzzy matching when needed.
units.context: Under the hood > Progressive Search Strategy
Under the hood > Progressive Search Strategy

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Phase 1 - Exact Matching__TRILIUM_PH_1__: When you search, Trilium first looks for exact matches of your search terms. This handles the vast majority of searches (90%+) and returns results almost instantly.
units.context: Under the hood > Progressive Search Strategy

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Phase 2 - Fuzzy Fallback__TRILIUM_PH_1__: If Phase 1 doesn't find enough high-quality results (fewer than 5 results with good relevance scores), Trilium automatically adds fuzzy matching to find results with typos or spelling variations.
units.context: Under the hood > Progressive Search Strategy

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Result Ordering__TRILIUM_PH_1__: Exact matches always appear before fuzzy matches, regardless of individual scores. This ensures that when you search for "project", notes containing the exact word "project" will appear before notes containing similar words like "projects" or "projection".
units.context: Under the hood > Progressive Search Strategy

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Speed__TRILIUM_PH_1__: Most searches complete using only exact matching

units.source: Note search enables you to find notes by searching for text in the title, content, or __TRILIUM_PH_0__attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of the notes. You also have the option to save your searches, which will create a special search note which is visible on your navigation tree and contains the search results as sub-items.
There are multiple types of searches, all using the same search mechanism and query language:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Quick search__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which can be found in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_3__ for small one-off searches.
The results are shown in a popup and it has an infinite scroll.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Full search__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is the more advanced search mechanism.
The results are displayed in a separate page and it has multiple advanced features (search script, fast search, include archived notes, order by, limit).
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Bulk Actions__TRILIUM_PH_1__ such as adding a label/relation can be applied to the results.
The results are paginated and they can be displayed in any __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_1__ view (e.g. grid, list, calendar, table).
Some __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_1__ such as board view have a dedicated search bar which applies to that collection.
In this case, the results are displayed directly in the collection instead of a popup and they are limited to the collection but the query language remains the same.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Jump to note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is a similar concept but it's mainly used to search for notes by title, not by content. Nevertheless, it also features a way to search in full text if the results are unsatisfactory.
From the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_1__, look for the dedicated __TRILIUM_PH_2__ search button.

To limit the search to a note and its children, select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search in subtree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) from the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Note tree contextual menu__TRILIUM_PH_4__ or press __TRILIUM_PH_5__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_6__+__TRILIUM_PH_7__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_8__+__TRILIUM_PH_9__S__TRILIUM_PH_10__.

Go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Jump to & command palette__TRILIUM_PH_1__, look for something then press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Show in full search__TRILIUM_PH_3__ below the results (or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_5__+__TRILIUM_PH_6__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_7__).
To search for notes, click on the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ icon in the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_2__ or press the keyboard __TRILIUM_PH_3__shortcut__TRILIUM_PH_4__.
Set the text to search for in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search string__TRILIUM_PH_1__ field.
Apart from searching for words literally, there is also the possibility to search for attributes or properties of notes.
See the examples below for more information.
To limit the search to a note and its sub-children, set a note in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ancestor__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
This value is also pre-filled if the search is triggered from a __TRILIUM_PH_0__hoisted note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or a __TRILIUM_PH_2__workspace__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
To search the entire database, keep the value empty.

To limit the search to only a few levels of hierarchy (e.g. look in sub-children but not in sub-sub-children of a note), set the __TRILIUM_PH_0__depth__TRILIUM_PH_1__ field to one of the provided values.
In addition to that, the search can be configured via the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add search option__TRILIUM_PH_1__ menu, as described in the follow-up section.
Press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) to trigger the search. The results are displayed below the search configuration pane.

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search & Execute actions__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) entry in the menu beside __TRILIUM_PH_3__Search__TRILIUM_PH_4__ is only relevant if at least one action has been added (as described in the section below).

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Save to note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) entry in the same menu will create a new note with the search configuration. For more information, see __TRILIUM_PH_3__Saved Search__TRILIUM_PH_4__.
To help with the syntax, Trilium offers an autocomplete functionality which can be triggered by pressing __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Space__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

Some suggestions also open on their own as you type: label and relation names after __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and __TRILIUM_PH_1__, fields after __TRILIUM_PH_2__, operators, values, and notes after __TRILIUM_PH_3__. Keywords such as __TRILIUM_PH_4__, __TRILIUM_PH_5__, __TRILIUM_PH_6__, __TRILIUM_PH_7__ and __TRILIUM_PH_8__ appear only on __TRILIUM_PH_9__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_10__+__TRILIUM_PH_11__Space__TRILIUM_PH_12__, since a plain word is usually a search term.

No suggestion is selected when a list opens on its own, so __TRILIUM_PH_0__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_1__ runs the search as typed. To insert a suggestion, select it with __TRILIUM_PH_2__Down__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and press __TRILIUM_PH_4__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_5__. The list opened with __TRILIUM_PH_6__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_7__+__TRILIUM_PH_8__Space__TRILIUM_PH_9__ and the notes after __TRILIUM_PH_10__ open on the best match instead, so __TRILIUM_PH_11__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_12__ inserts it.
Basic operators such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and keywords (__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__).
Fields for object-like fields such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ or __TRILIUM_PH_1__, triggered by typing __TRILIUM_PH_2__.
A small gear on the name's icon indicates a system attribute.
After typing the label name, the value is also autocompleted with values that are present in the database.

If the note ID is under a valid syntax, it will be shown as a chip of the note instead of the raw ID.
This is especially useful for queries that make use of the note ID such as searching by template: __TRILIUM_PH_0__
The search input features syntax highlighting, making recognized fields such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and operators like __TRILIUM_PH_1__ stand out.

The same highlighting is available in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes, for example to keep a collection of queries: set the language of the note to __TRILIUM_PH_2__Trilium Search Query__TRILIUM_PH_3__. The language is not enabled by default; add it from __TRILIUM_PH_4__Options__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Code Notes__TRILIUM_PH_7__ → __TRILIUM_PH_8__Available MIME types in the dropdown__TRILIUM_PH_9__.
The search is also checked for errors in two phases, which will be displayed as a red squiggle:
Linter errors which identify common error patterns and also provide a way to fix them.
Search errors which are checked by the server, without indicating the exact place the error occurred.

An error the search only runs into while running, such as an operator that note content cannot be searched with, is shown in a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search error__TRILIUM_PH_1__ card instead: below the search string, or at the top of the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Quick search__TRILIUM_PH_3__ results.
Long or complicated searches can be formatted by using newlines, similar to SQL queries. Newlines are treated just like spaces.
To add a new line, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
Multiline is available only for the full search, other inputs such as the quick search or the collection filter are single line.
Click __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add search option__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to choose an option to apply.
For each search option selected, the search configuration will update to reveal the entry. Each search option will have its own configuration.
To remove a search option, simply press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button to the right of it.
This feature allows writing a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note that will handle the search on its own.
The search will not look into the content of the notes, but it will still look into note titles and attributes, relations (based on the search query).
This method can speed up the search considerably for large __TRILIUM_PH_0__databases__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Archived Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ will also be included in the results, whereas otherwise they would be ignored.
Allows changing the criteria for ordering the results, for example to order by creation date or alphabetically instead of by relevancy (default).
It's also possible to change the order (ascending or descending) of the results.
Limits the results to a given maximum.
This can help if the number of results would otherwise be high, at the cost of not being able to view all the results.
This will print additional information in the server log (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Error logs__TRILIUM_PH_1__), regarding how the search expression was parsed.
This function is especially useful after understanding the search functionality in detail, in order to determine why a complex search query is not working as expected.

The same menu ends with a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Bulk actions__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section for applying changes such as adding a label or a relation to the matched notes. Its groups—__TRILIUM_PH_2__Labels__TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__Relations__TRILIUM_PH_5__, __TRILIUM_PH_6__Notes__TRILIUM_PH_7__ and __TRILIUM_PH_8__Other__TRILIUM_PH_9__—each open a list of the actions in the corresponding group of the __TRILIUM_PH_10__Bulk Actions__TRILIUM_PH_11__ dialog, which is an alternative for operating directly with notes within the __TRILIUM_PH_12__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_13__. Choosing one adds it to the search; unlike the other options, the same action can be added more than once (e.g. to apply multiple labels). After defining the actions, first press __TRILIUM_PH_14__Search__TRILIUM_PH_15__ to check the matched notes and then choose __TRILIUM_PH_16__Search & Execute actions__TRILIUM_PH_17__ from the menu beside it to trigger the actions.

Results appear below the search pane, by default in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search preview__TRILIUM_PH_1__ view. Each result is drawn as a __TRILIUM_PH_2__snippet card__TRILIUM_PH_3__ with the note title, the path to it, a short excerpt of the matching text, and the attributes that matched. The excerpt of a code note keeps its indentation and is shown in the code font.

To show the results as a plain note list instead, choose __TRILIUM_PH_0__List__TRILIUM_PH_1__ from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Collection Properties__TRILIUM_PH_3__ bar. The __TRILIUM_PH_4__List__TRILIUM_PH_5__ view shows one row per note, with the note's title and content preview.
The search will also highlight the words from the title or content that matched:
With a solid underlined green for a direct match;
With a dotted underline orange for a partial match (matched by the fuzzy search).
In addition, the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search preview__TRILIUM_PH_1__ view offers:
The __TRILIUM_PH_0__total number of results__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is always shown, so you can immediately tell how broad a query is.

A __TRILIUM_PH_0__page-size selector__TRILIUM_PH_1__ lets you choose how many results to display per page. Your choice is remembered and synced across your devices (stored in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ option), so you do not have to reset it on every device.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Clicking a result's title__TRILIUM_PH_1__ opens the note and jumps straight to the first match. The in-note find bar opens pre-filled with the first word of your search, so you can step through its matches with the find controls. Frequently used notes can be bookmarked, which will make them appear in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for easy access.

If bookmarks don't appear in the launch bar, then most likely the bookmark section has been hidden. Go to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_1__ configuration from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Global menu__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and ensure __TRILIUM_PH_4__Bookmarks__TRILIUM_PH_5__ is in the __TRILIUM_PH_6__Visible Launchers__TRILIUM_PH_7__ section.
Space in the left panel is limited, and you might want to bookmark many items. One possible solution is to bookmark a folder, so it shows its children:

To do this, bookmark a folder, then right click its button in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and check __TRILIUM_PH_2__Show as a folder__TRILIUM_PH_3__. The button then opens a menu instead of the note itself: the note is at the top, followed by its children. Uncheck __TRILIUM_PH_4__Show as a folder__TRILIUM_PH_5__ to turn it back into a regular bookmark.

A child that has children of its own shows an arrow at the end of its row. Click the arrow to list its children in a submenu, or click the rest of the row to open the note. Submenus nest up to four levels deep. A menu that lists more than 15 children shows a filter field above them: type part of a title to list only the notes that match. A note whose subtree is hidden (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Hiding the subtree__TRILIUM_PH_1__) doesn't list its children here either.

The notes in the menu open the way links do: a middle click or __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+click opens a note in a new tab, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_3__+click opens it in a new window, and a right click lists the other places it can be opened in.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Show as a folder__TRILIUM_PH_1__ assigns the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ label to the note, so adding the label by hand works as well. Because the label belongs to the note, a note that is both bookmarked and dropped onto the launch bar shows its children in both places.

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Quick edit__TRILIUM_PH_1__ provides an alternative to the standard tab-based navigation and editing.

Instead of clicking on a note which switches the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to the newly selected note, or navigating between two different __TRILIUM_PH_2__Tabs__TRILIUM_PH_3__, the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Quick edit__TRILIUM_PH_5__ feature opens as a popup window that can be easily dismissed.

This feature is also well integrated with __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_1__ such as the calendar view, which makes it easy to edit entries without having to go back and forth between the child note and the calendar.
All note types are supported, including __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

For __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes, depending on user preference, both the floating and classic editors are supported. See __TRILIUM_PH_2__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
The title and the note and the icon are editable, just like a normal tab.
The note's actions and its menu are shown in the header of the popup, as in the title row of a tab.
When other notes link to the note, a button with a link icon lists the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Backlinks__TRILIUM_PH_1__. Pressing one opens that note in the popup.
The menu items that only work in a tab are not shown: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note map__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Full width__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Convert into attachment__TRILIUM_PH_5__.

It searches the note in the popup, not the note in the tab behind it.
A help page opened from the popup, such as through the help button of the note type, opens in a second popup on top of it. Closing that popup returns to the note being edited.

This integrates well with __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_1__ where there are predefined attributes such as the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Start date__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__End date__TRILIUM_PH_5__, allowing for easy editing.

By default, Trilium comes with a set of icons called Boxicons v2. Since v0.102.0, custom icon packs allow a wider selection of icons for notes.
Icon packs are specific to Trilium, so they must either be created from scratch (see below) or imported from a ZIP file from a third-party developer.
The Trilium team maintains a few icon packs that are not shipped with Trilium. These icon packs can be found on the official website on the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Resources page__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

units.source: Apart from the __TRILIUM_PH_0__sample icon packs__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the Trilium maintainers are not responsible for keeping icon packs up to date. If you have an issue with a specific icon pack, then the issue must be reported to the third-party developer responsible for it, not the Trilium team.
units.context: Icon Packs > Importing an existing icon pack

units.source: Since __TRILIUM_PH_0__Safe import__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is disabled, make sure you trust the source as it could contain dangerous third-party scripts. One good way to check if the icon pack is safe is to manually extract the .zip and inspect the file contents. Icon packs should only contain a font file and a JSON file. Other files (especially scripts) are to be considered harmful.

units.source: Each entry is named after its note, so renaming the note renames the entry. The setting refers to the note itself rather than to its name, and keeps working across a rename.

units.source: Some fonts support programming ligatures, which will turn character combinations such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ into __TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__ as __TRILIUM_PH_3__ in __TRILIUM_PH_4__Code blocks__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and __TRILIUM_PH_6__Code__TRILIUM_PH_7__ notes.

Trilium comes with a couple pre-installed color themes, with the default being a light theme. To switch to a dark theme or any other available theme, navigate to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ Options menu (accessible via the app icon in the top-left corner), select the Appearance tab, and choose your preferred theme. The __TRILIUM_PH_1__Theme__TRILIUM_PH_2__ submenu of the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Global menu__TRILIUM_PH_4__ switches the theme and the color scheme as well.

While a dark theme is active, Trilium asks the Dark Reader browser extension not to darken the page a second time. Dark Reader still darkens the light themes. After switching from a dark theme to a light one, reload the page (__TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__R__TRILIUM_PH_3__) for Dark Reader to take effect again.

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__GitHub-Flavored Markdown__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is the main syntax that Trilium is following.
When exporting, images are usually kept in the basic Markdown syntax but will use the HTML syntax if the image has a custom width. Figures are always embedded as HTML.
Simple tables are supported with the Markdown syntax. If the table is too complex or contains elements that would render as HTML, the table is also rendered as HTML.
Trilium internal links (that mirror a note's title and display its icon) are embedded as HTML in order to preserve the information on import.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Anchors__TRILIUM_PH_1__ are kept as HTML as well, so links to an anchor still lead to it after the note is imported again.
Both inline and display equations are supported, using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and __TRILIUM_PH_1__ syntaxes.
The Markdown syntax for admonitions as supported by Trilium is the one that GitHub uses, which is as follows:
There are currently no plans of supporting alternative admonition syntaxes such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__.

Tabs use the syntax of __TRILIUM_PH_0__Material for MkDocs__TRILIUM_PH_1__: each tab starts with a __TRILIUM_PH_2__ line, followed by its content indented by four spaces. Consecutive tabs form one tabs block, and __TRILIUM_PH_3__ starts a new block right after another one:

Tabs can be nested by indenting the inner tabs inside the content of a tab. A tab title is plain text, so its formatting is not kept on export. For how tabs blocks work in a text note, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Content tabs__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Basic support for wikilinks has been added in v0.96.0:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ will look for the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ file in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ directory and turn it into an internal link.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ will look for the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ file in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ directory and turn it into an image.
This feature is import-only, which means that it will turn wikilinks into Trilium-compatible syntax, but it will not export Trilium Notes into Markdown files with this syntax.

The path to pages in wikilinks is resolved relatively to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__import root__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and not the current directory of the note. This is to be inline with other platforms that use wikilinks such as SilverBullet.
The root path of the import is determined as follows:
If there is a single directory within the archive at root level, then that directory is considered the root.
If there are multiple files & directories at root level, then the archive root (containing all of these items) is considered the root.
Background highlights are supported in two ways:
The Markdown __TRILIUM_PH_0__ extension which is supported by other Markdown-based applications such as Obsidian:
The canonical HTML representation of highlights, as supported by Trilium:
When the yellow highlight is used, import/export prefers the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ syntax whereas the canonical HTML reprepresentation is used otherwise.
Trilium supports Markdown for both import and export, while trying to keep compatibility as high as possible.
If you want to import just a chunk of markdown from clipboard, you can do it from editor block menu:
You can also import Markdown files from files:
whole tree of markdown files (packaged into __TRILIUM_PH_0__.zip__TRILIUM_PH_1__ archive)

You can use e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_0__7-zip__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to package directory of markdown files into the ZIP file
You can export whole subtree to ZIP archive which will have directory structured modelled after subtree structure:
If you want to export just single note without its subtree, you can do it from Note actions menu:
If you want to export protected notes, enter a protected session first! This will export the notes in an unencrypted form, so if you reimport into Trilium, make sure to re-protect these notes.

OneNote's __TRILIUM_PH_0__Tags__TRILIUM_PH_1__ functionality is imported in Trilium as __TRILIUM_PH_2__Icons__TRILIUM_PH_3__ using the default icon pack or emojis (if there is no suitable replacement).
Custom tags are not supported by OneNote's Graph API so Trilium cannot import them.
These remain formatted as paragraphs, with the glyph prepended to the text. A paragraph can carry several tags at once, in which case their glyphs stack.
These become __TRILIUM_PH_0__To-do Lists__TRILIUM_PH_1__, with the glyph inside the item with the tick state preserved:

Trilium allows importing from OneNote. Currently the only mechanism supported is via the Microsoft Graph API which requires you to authenticate in a browser in order for the notes to be obtained by Trilium.
In the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__, right click and select __TRILIUM_PH_2__Import into note__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
On the desktop app, you will be redirected to Microsoft's authentication screen where you can log into your account.
On the web app, the process is slightly more involved as it requires copying the code to clipboard, accessing the link, pasting the code and then signing in once more.

After the connection is successful, you should be able to see a list of sections that can be imported. Simply check the ones to import and press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Import selected__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button.
Wait for the import to finish.
The following features are preserved by Trilium during the import process:
Basic formatting (bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, subscript, super script, font sizes, headings, colors, highlights).
Black-colored text is intentionally stripped to allow it to work in dark themes.
Inline code is automatically detected and formatted. Paragraphs that use the Code style are also converted to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code blocks__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Unfortunately the indentation of the code might be lost because the information is simply not present in the data from the Microsoft API.
Cell backgrounds are preserved, including a best-effort hue correction because the colors returned by the Graph API are sometimes incorrect.
Cell widths are also preserved proportionally, with the only difference that tables in Trilium have a percentage-based width, not fixed pixel sizes.
Screen clippings are also properly supported since v0.104.1, displaying their timestamp as a figure caption.
Hand-drawing is preserved and displayed as an SVG image inside the note
OneNote's default color (black) is special since it also renders as white for dark themes. Since v0.104.1, this is also supported by using a special SVG tweak which reacts to light/dark themes.

Links between other imported pages are converted to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Internal (reference) links__TRILIUM_PH_1__ if the text of the link matches the name of the page, or plain links otherwise. If the pages are not part of the import, the original __TRILIUM_PH_2__ link is kept.

Tags (apart from to-do lists) are preserved by converting them to __TRILIUM_PH_0__inline icons__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which are searchable by the icon's name and can be recolored like any other icon. Some icons are turned into emojis instead.
The order of the pages within a section is maintained.
Sub-pages and section groups are maintained by nesting notes in a hierarchical structure.
Creation and modification of both notes and sections is preserved. The order of section or section groups is not preserved (see limitations).

units.context: Microsoft OneNote > Error management and reporting

units.source: The OneNote importer uses Microsoft's Graph API which handles the HTML export (that we later post-process for Trilium use). The Graph API itself has to process the OneNote pages before sending them to us, and as such it's a time-consuming operation that is directly proportional to the number of notes and the complexity/size of the notes.
units.context: Microsoft OneNote > Error management and reporting

units.source: The Graph API throttles access if it detects too many operations. The importer takes that into account, but sometimes this means that most of the time is spent waiting for the Graph API to unblock access rather than actually importing data.
units.context: Microsoft OneNote > Error management and reporting

units.source: In addition, some pages may fail at the Graph API level due to an internal timeout on their side or other issues. Trilium will try to refetch pages in order to avoid that but sometimes pages cannot be retrieved even after multiple retries. In that case, the importer will still create a corresponding note in Trilium but with an error report instead of a content. This preserves __TRILIUM_PH_0__Internal (reference) links__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and makes it easy to identify and manually fix the pages that failed.
units.context: Microsoft OneNote > Error management and reporting

units.source: At the end of the import, the top-level note called __TRILIUM_PH_0__OneNote__TRILIUM_PH_1__ __TRILIUM_PH_2__import__TRILIUM_PH_3__ will contain information about how the import went:

units.source: A list of notes that could not be imported, as well as the failure reason;
units.context: Microsoft OneNote > Error management and reporting

units.source: Pages whose images/attachments failed to download
units.context: Microsoft OneNote > Error management and reporting

units.source: How long the import spent waiting out throttling.
units.context: Microsoft OneNote > Error management and reporting

units.source: To avoid cases in which the import is fundamentally broken (e.g. an expired sign-in), the import will error out if it fails to import 6 pages in a row.
units.context: Microsoft OneNote > Error management and reporting

units.context: Microsoft OneNote > Limitations > Regarding OneNote's freehand structure

units.source: OneNote is fundamentally different to Trilium in structure because it allows freehand drawing to coexist with text, and text boxes can be placed anywhere in the document (e.g. a common use case is to have columns). Trilium has a document flow mechanism for __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes which means that it can't be freely positioned.
units.context: Microsoft OneNote > Limitations > Regarding OneNote's freehand structure

units.source: To cope with this difference, Trilium will flatten the text structure into normal paragraphs. The paragraphs will be ordered visually based on the original position of the text boxes, but their horizontal position will not be preserved. Parallel text such as columns may appear interleaved which can cause problems.
units.context: Microsoft OneNote > Limitations > Regarding OneNote's freehand structure

units.source: In addition, drawing in OneNote can be interleaved with text boxes. Text notes in Trilium do not allow for this feature, so all drawing will appear at the end. For some use cases (diagrams, for example) this will work fine, but if you have highlights or other text-dependent drawings they will appear out of order.
units.context: Microsoft OneNote > Limitations > Regarding OneNote's freehand structure

units.source: There are plans to support drawing-heavy notes that interleave with text boxes by converting them to a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Canvas__TRILIUM_PH_1__ instead.
units.context: Microsoft OneNote > Limitations > Regarding OneNote's freehand structure

units.source: OneNote supports encryption at section level; when importing a notebook that contains these password-protection sections, Trilium will not be able to read the content of password-protected sections so they will appear empty. This is not a limitation of Trilium, the information is simply not available from the source (Graph API).
The section itself is kept for reference and all the sections that could not be imported will be shown in the report (the top-level note called __TRILIUM_PH_0__OneNote import__TRILIUM_PH_1__).

To unprotect a section in OneNote Desktop, right click on the protected section → __TRILIUM_PH_0__Password Protect This Section__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Remove Password__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and sync. Then re-import either only the protected sections or remove everything and start the import from scratch.
The following are known limitations due to how the information comes from the import (Microsoft Graph API), which means that they cannot be fixed.
The order of the sections (and section groups) is not available, the sections are ordered by creation date instead.
Paragraph indentation, as well as code block indentation.
Drawings inside titles, the title might appear incomplete or “Untitled”.

When importing notes, you might find that some text is not rendered properly or the structure is not properly maintained. As long as this issue is not a fundamental issue (like the issue with freehand text not being preserved exactly), it's a good idea to __TRILIUM_PH_0__report it__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
When reporting, make sure that you provide the following information:

Import again the section, checking the debug checkbox before importing. This preserves the original document (and the hand-drawing data if any) as it came through from OneNote's cloud API so that it can be used for comparison.
Export only the affected page as ZIP, making sure not to accidentally expose any sensitive information.
Take screenshots of how the note looked like in OneNote and how it ends up in Trilium.
Attach the ZIP and the screenshots to the issue report.

Every page property that can be preserved according to the table above is saved as a label or relation to the corresponding note (except for creation and modification dates which are saved at note level).

Basic formatting (bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, colors, highlights, superscript, subscript, text alignment, inline code).
The hierarchy of headings (these are shifted to start with H2 because H1 is reserved for note title, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Headings__TRILIUM_PH_1__)
To-do lists. The new task format is collapsed to standard to-do lists
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Admonitions__TRILIUM_PH_1__ are preserved, including its emoji (added as part of the content).
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Code blocks__TRILIUM_PH_1__, with a best-effort attempt to restore the language.
Internal links are re-written to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Internal (reference) links__TRILIUM_PH_1__ if the target note is part of the same import.

The size limit of one import is 250Mb. If the total size of your files is larger, you can increase the __TRILIUM_PH_0__upload limit__TRILIUM_PH_1__, or divide your files, and run the import as many times as necessary.
All resources (except for images) are created as notes’ attachments.
If you have HTML inside ENEX files, the HTML formatting may be broken or lost after import in Trilium. See __TRILIUM_PH_0__Reporting issues__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

The first step is to export the data from Anytype:
Press the […] at the top-right of the window and select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Export__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Ensure the following options are set:
Select the desired channel from the left bar.
Underneath the channel icon in the left sidebar, press the name of the channel with an arrow and select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Channel Settings__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
In the left sidebar, look for the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Integrations__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section and select __TRILIUM_PH_2__Export__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
Ensure the following options are set:
In the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__, right click and select __TRILIUM_PH_2__Import into note__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

Exporting collections individually can sometimes miss information that would otherwise be picked up from an export of the entire channel. The reason is that Anytype leaves out some information when exporting individual pages/collections.
The following features are preserved by Trilium during the import process:
Basic formatting (bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, headings, colors, highlights, inline code).
Highlight blocks are imported as block quotes.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Code blocks__TRILIUM_PH_1__, with a best-effort attempt to restore the language.
Links between other imported pages are converted to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Internal (reference) links__TRILIUM_PH_1__ if they are part of the same import.
Applies to both block links and inline links.
Collections are imported as Trilium-native __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (see below).
Files inside collections are imported as __TRILIUM_PH_0__File__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes.
Dividers (line, dots) are imported as horizontal rules.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Admonitions__TRILIUM_PH_1__ are preserved, including its emoji (added as part of the content).
Creation and modification date of pages is preserved.
Collections created in Anytype are imported on a best-effort basis, preserving both the view mode and the page properties as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
The following view modes are supported:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Calendar__TRILIUM_PH_1__, preserving the attribute which identifies the date.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Kanban Board__TRILIUM_PH_1__, preserving the board group column.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Table__TRILIUM_PH_1__, also used as fallback for unsupported collection layouts.
The files are preserved as attachments, and a link to them is prepended to the content of the note for visibility.
When importing your Anytype notes, you might find issues in how a note is imported; in that case consider __TRILIUM_PH_0__reporting__TRILIUM_PH_1__ it.
