A .zip export of the original note (and children if applicable). This allows us to reproduce the issue.
A screenshot with how it originally looked like before the import and how it looks after the import.
Although Obsidian was indirectly supported through the standard __TRILIUM_PH_0__Markdown__TRILIUM_PH_1__ import, its vault structure is distinct enough to warrant its own dedicated import channel.
The first step is to obtain a .zip of your Obsidian vault:

First, identify where your Obsidian vault is located. The easiest way to do so is to open Obsidian and right clicking the name of the vault at the bottom of the left sidebar and then selecting __TRILIUM_PH_0__Show in system explorer__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

In your system explorer, right click the directory containing your Obsidian vault and compress it to a ZIP file (e.g. on Windows, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Compress To__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__ZIP__TRILIUM_PH_3__).

When zipping, you can either ZIP the outer folder of the vault, or the contents of the vault as Trilium will automatically determine the position of the vault in the archive via the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ directory.
In the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__, right click and select __TRILIUM_PH_2__Import into note__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
Upload the ZIP obtained in the previous step.

Alternatively, simply drag & drop the .zip archive in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and Trilium will auto-detect it as an Obsidian import provided there is a __TRILIUM_PH_2__ directory. If not, follow the previous steps instead.
The following features are preserved by Trilium during the import process:
Basic Markdown formatting (bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, headings).
Non-Markdown files in the Vault are treated as attachments by default if they are referenced by at least one note.
Otherwise, they will be imported as __TRILIUM_PH_0__File__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes.
Transclusions are converted to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Include Note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Images__TRILIUM_PH_3__ (depending on type).
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Code blocks__TRILIUM_PH_1__, with a best-effort attempt to restore the language.
Links between pages are converted to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Internal (reference) links__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Obsidian has many more types of callouts (__TRILIUM_PH_0__, __TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__), these are all mapped to one of Trilium's existing admonition types (e.g. Note, Tip, Important).
Custom titles are kept and shown as a bold line at the top of the admonition, since there is no concept of admonition title in Trilium.
Foldable callouts are imported expanded and without a fold marker.

Notes created by the __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Excalidraw__TRILIUM_PH_2____TRILIUM_PH_3__ community plugin for Obsidian are converted to __TRILIUM_PH_4__Canvas__TRILIUM_PH_5__ (same underlying technology).
Note that custom features introduced by that plugin will not be supported.
Modification date is preserved via the information obtained from the .zip archive, creation date is not recoverable so it's kept the same as the modification date.

Properties are Obsidian's equivalent of __TRILIUM_PH_0__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__. One of the core differences between the two is where the property information is stored (i.e. name and type): in Obsidian everything is stored at vault level and shared across all notes, whereas in Trilium each page can have individual promoted attributes, shared through __TRILIUM_PH_2__Templates__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Attribute Inheritance__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
Another important difference is that promoted attributes in Trilium are always displayed, even if empty. In Obsidian, these are simply suggested when creating a new property.
To reconcile all these differences, properties are converted to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ at note level.
The following note types are supported:
Obsidian has a few reserved property names, which are treated differently in Trilium as well:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__, where every tag is turned into its own __TRILIUM_PH_1__label__TRILIUM_PH_2__ (e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__ when __TRILIUM_PH_5__).
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ are simply mapped to individual __TRILIUM_PH_1__ labels

The closest equivalent in Trilium would be __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_1__ but they work fundamentally different because bases don't store particular notes, they act more like a __TRILIUM_PH_2__Saved Search__TRILIUM_PH_3__ with a collection view.
Since the base query format is quite different to Trilium's __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search__TRILIUM_PH_1__ syntax, it's unlikely they'll ever be supported.
When a base is encountered, it is simply ignored from the import.
Theoretically they could map to either __TRILIUM_PH_0__Canvas__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Relation Map__TRILIUM_PH_3__ but they are too different to reconcile.
Links to a specific heading in another note will still point to the right note, but the heading anchor will be dropped.
Dangling links (pointing to a note that doesn't exist) and ambiguous links (same base name in 2+ notes) are unwrapped to plain text.

Trilium natively supports the following formats for both import and export.
This is the main format used by Trilium, where standard tags are used to represent basic formatting and layout (e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_0__, __TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__).

Note that HTML is not a standardized format so some more specific features such as admonitions or __TRILIUM_PH_0__Internal (reference) links__TRILIUM_PH_1__ might not be supported by other applications.
The notes can also be exported as __TRILIUM_PH_0__static HTML that can be used for web publishing__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Most of the formatting is preserved, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Supported syntax__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

To import from other applications such as OneNote, Notion and others, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Importing data from other applications__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Versions prior to v0.104.0 had an upload limit of 250 MiB that could be bypassed via a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ environment variable; with v0.104.0 this limit was removed.

Nevertheless, there is still a limit for the maximum size of a __TRILIUM_PH_0__single item__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (whether it's a __TRILIUM_PH_2__File__TRILIUM_PH_3__, an __TRILIUM_PH_4__Attachments__TRILIUM_PH_5__ or even a __TRILIUM_PH_6__Text__TRILIUM_PH_7__ note). The limit is approximately 374 MiB and it's determined by the __TRILIUM_PH_8__Synchronization__TRILIUM_PH_9__ protocol. Attempts to import such large files will be refused.
During large imports or exports, memory consumption might spike but it will remain somewhere around the 2 gigabyte mark. Tested with a 2.4 GB database with ~21k notes.

A quick import, from the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
The import dialog (via right click in the note tree → __TRILIUM_PH_0__Import into note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or from __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_3__).
When dealing with large files (multi-gigabyte), prefer using the import dialog as it has a special mechanism which makes sure that the file is read directly from disk rather than uploaded again.

The Zen Mode can be activated by accessing the global menu and selecting the “Zen mode” option:

Aside from the global menu, it's also possible to activate this mode by using a keyboard shortcut (which is __TRILIUM_PH_0__F9__TRILIUM_PH_1__ since TriliumNext 0.92.5 and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_3__+__TRILIUM_PH_4__Z__TRILIUM_PH_5__ for older versions). units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Active content__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is a generic name for powerful features in Trilium, these range from customizing the UI to advanced scripting that can alter your notes or even your PC.
Active content problem of safety, especially when this active content comes from a third-party such as if it is downloaded from a website and then imported into Trilium.

When __TRILIUM_PH_0__importing__TRILIUM_PH_1__ into Trilium, __TRILIUM_PH_2__safe mode__TRILIUM_PH_3__ is active by default which will try to prevent untrusted code from executing. For example, a __TRILIUM_PH_4__custom widget__TRILIUM_PH_5__ needs the __TRILIUM_PH_6__ __TRILIUM_PH_7__label__TRILIUM_PH_8__ in order to function; safe import works by renaming that label to __TRILIUM_PH_9__.

This applies to every attribute an import creates: those in a Trilium .zip export, and those made from the properties of other formats (such as the YAML front matter of a Markdown file, an Evernote tag, or a Notion, Anytype or Obsidian property).

Sometimes active content can cause issues with the UI or the server, preventing it from functioning properly. __TRILIUM_PH_0__Safe mode__TRILIUM_PH_1__ allows starting Trilium in such a way that active content is not loaded by default at start-up, allowing the user to fix the problematic scripts or widgets.

Common request is to allow multiple users collaborate, share notes etc. So far I'm resisting this because of these reasons:

it's a huge feature, or rather a Pandora's box of collaboration features like user management, permissions, conflict resolution, real-time editing of a note by multiple people etc. This would be a huge amount of work. Trilium Notes is project made mostly by one person in free time and that's unlikely to change in the future.
given its size it would probably pivot the attention away from my main focus which is a personal note-taking

the assumption that only single person has access to the app simplifies many things, or just outright makes them possible. In multi-user app, our __TRILIUM_PH_0__scripting__TRILIUM_PH_1__support would be a XSS security hole, while with the single user assumption it's an endless customizable tool.

units.source: Trilium stores notes in a __TRILIUM_PH_0__database__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which is an SQLite database. People often ask why doesn't Trilium rather use flat files for note storage - it's fair question since flat files are easily interoperable, work with SCM/git etc.
units.context: FAQ > Why database instead of flat files?

units.source: Short answer is that file systems are simply not powerful enough for what we want to achieve with Trilium. Using filesystem would mean fewer features with probably more problems.
units.context: FAQ > Why database instead of flat files?
FAQ > Why database instead of flat files?

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__clones__TRILIUM_PH_1__ are what you might call "hard directory link" in filesystem lingo, but this concept is not implemented in any filesystem
units.context: FAQ > Why database instead of flat files?

units.source: filesystems make a distinction between directory and file while there's intentionally no such difference in Trilium
units.context: FAQ > Why database instead of flat files?

units.source: files are stored in no particular order and user can't change this
units.context: FAQ > Why database instead of flat files?

units.source: Trilium allows storing note __TRILIUM_PH_0__attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which could be represented in extended user attributes but their support differs greatly among different filesystems / operating systems
units.context: FAQ > Why database instead of flat files?

units.source: Trilium makes links / relations between different notes which can be quickly retrieved / navigated (e.g. for __TRILIUM_PH_0__note map__TRILIUM_PH_1__). There's no such support in file systems which means these would have to be stored in some kind of side-car files (mini-databases).
units.context: FAQ > Why database instead of flat files?

units.source: Filesystems are generally not transactional. While this is not completely required for a note-taking application, having transactions make it way easier to keep notes and their metadata in predictable and consistent state.
units.context: FAQ > Why database instead of flat files?

A specific pair_:_ __TRILIUM_PH_0__, __TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__, __TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__, __TRILIUM_PH_5__, __TRILIUM_PH_6__, __TRILIUM_PH_7__, __TRILIUM_PH_8__. Choosing one applies it to every note, regardless of its content language.

Type the text to replace and the replacement, then press Enter. Existing ones are shown as chips and removed with the × on each.

A custom replacement is applied when the text is typed as a whole word and followed by a space, so longer words that begin with it are left alone — a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ replacement does not rewrite the end of __TRILIUM_PH_1__, and __TRILIUM_PH_2__ can still be typed.
Capitalization follows what you type, unless the replacement has capitals of its own:
The text to replace is matched literally; it is not a pattern.
Typing a "text to replace" that already exists in the list of replacements will update the existing one instead. It's not possible to have multiple replacements for the same text.
The same “text to replace” with different capitalization (e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and __TRILIUM_PH_1__ co-existing) doesn't work because it would interfere with the capitalization rules above.

units.source: Block references are __TRILIUM_PH_0__links__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to a block of a text note, such as a paragraph, a heading, a list item or a table, or to a range of consecutive blocks. A block reference can be pasted in another note as a link, or turned into an __TRILIUM_PH_2__Include Note__TRILIUM_PH_3__ that shows only the referenced blocks.
Place the cursor in the block to reference. To reference several consecutive blocks, select them.

Right-click the block handle, the sequence of dots to the left of the block (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_1__), and select __TRILIUM_PH_2__Copy reference__TRILIUM_PH_3__. With the fixed formatting toolbar, clicking the block handle opens the same menu. Alternatively, right-click the text and select __TRILIUM_PH_4__Copy reference to this block__TRILIUM_PH_5__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_6__Copy__TRILIUM_PH_7__ submenu, or __TRILIUM_PH_8__Copy reference to these blocks__TRILIUM_PH_9__ for a selection. The referenced blocks flash briefly.
Go to the note where to insert the link and press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__V__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

Inside a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Content tabs__TRILIUM_PH_1__ block, the reference points to the whole block. To link to a single tab, use __TRILIUM_PH_2__Copy reference to this tab__TRILIUM_PH_3__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_4__ __TRILIUM_PH_5__More actions__TRILIUM_PH_6__ menu of the tabs block instead. Inside a __TRILIUM_PH_7__Multicolumn layout__TRILIUM_PH_8__, the reference points to the blocks in the column, and an include shows them without the layout around them.

The link shows the title of the note, followed by the beginning of the referenced text. A link to blocks of the same note shows only the beginning of the referenced text, and a link to a heading of the same note shows the whole heading.

If the note is __TRILIUM_PH_0__shared__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the menu of the block handle also offers __TRILIUM_PH_2__Copy public link__TRILIUM_PH_3__. It copies the web address of the shared page with the reference added, to send to people who read the note outside Trilium. Opening the address scrolls the shared page to the referenced blocks and flashes them. On a shared page, a link to blocks of another shared note does the same.
The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Paste__TRILIUM_PH_1__ submenu of the context menu offers two more ways to insert a copied reference:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Paste reference as a link__TRILIUM_PH_1__ inserts only the link, even when the reference was copied as plain text or along with other content.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Paste reference as an excerpt__TRILIUM_PH_1__ inserts an include of the referenced blocks, as described below.
In a browser, the context menu of the text editor opens only when right-clicking selected text. Elsewhere the browser shows its own menu.

units.context: Block references > Linking to a heading

units.source: Since v0.107.0, a link to a heading of the same note can be created from the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add link__TRILIUM_PH_1__ dialog:
units.context: Block references > Linking to a heading

units.source: Place the cursor at the desired position of the link, or select the text to turn into a link.
units.context: Block references > Linking to a heading

units.source: Press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__K__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or the __TRILIUM_PH_4__ button in the __TRILIUM_PH_5__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_6__, then select __TRILIUM_PH_7__Heading / anchor__TRILIUM_PH_8__ at the top of the dialog. Alternatively, choose __TRILIUM_PH_9__Link to a heading or anchor__TRILIUM_PH_10__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_11__Slash Commands__TRILIUM_PH_12__, which opens the dialog on that page.
units.context: Block references > Linking to a heading

units.source: Under __TRILIUM_PH_0__Headings__TRILIUM_PH_1__, click the desired heading to check it. Sub-headings are listed under their heading and start collapsed; expand or collapse a heading with the arrow in front of it, or with __TRILIUM_PH_2__→__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__←__TRILIUM_PH_5__ while it is focused. Optionally, type a __TRILIUM_PH_6__Link title__TRILIUM_PH_7__.
units.context: Block references > Linking to a heading
Block references > Linking to a heading

units.source: When the link title is not set, the link displays the text of the heading. If the heading gets changed, the link is renamed automatically to the new text, shortly after you stop typing. A link with a title of its own keeps that title.
units.context: Block references > Linking to a heading

units.source: The link is a block reference to the heading, so it keeps working when the heading is moved. To change the link, click it and press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Edit link__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button in its popup. For a link with a title of its own, placing the cursor inside it and pressing __TRILIUM_PH_3__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_4__+__TRILIUM_PH_5__K__TRILIUM_PH_6__ works too. The dialog opens on __TRILIUM_PH_7__Heading / anchor__TRILIUM_PH_8__, with the heading checked. Emptying the __TRILIUM_PH_9__Link title__TRILIUM_PH_10__ there makes the link display the text of the heading again.
units.context: Block references > Linking to a heading

units.source: Clicking a block reference opens the note, scrolls to the referenced blocks and flashes them. If a referenced block was deleted, an error message is shown instead, along with the blocks of the range that still exist.

A link to blocks of the note it is in, such as a link to a heading, scrolls to them and flashes them without leaving the note, as a link within a web page does. This works in read-only notes and on shared pages too. While editing, clicking the link shows its popup: press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Jump to heading__TRILIUM_PH_1__ there, or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Jump to block__TRILIUM_PH_3__ for other blocks.

units.context: Block references > Including the referenced blocks

units.source: To show the referenced blocks inside another note, right-click the link in a note being edited and select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Convert link to note excerpt__TRILIUM_PH_1__, or paste the copied reference with __TRILIUM_PH_2__Paste__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Paste reference as an excerpt__TRILIUM_PH_5__. The include shows only the referenced blocks, not the rest of the note, and marks them with an __TRILIUM_PH_6__Excerpt__TRILIUM_PH_7__ badge in its title. It starts at the __TRILIUM_PH_8__Full__TRILIUM_PH_9__ box size, so all the referenced blocks are visible. To see the whole note, press the __TRILIUM_PH_10__ button in the same title, which opens the note in a new tab. Converting the include back to a link keeps the reference.
units.context: Block references > Including the referenced blocks

units.source: To edit the referenced blocks without leaving the note, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Edit excerpt__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button in the title of the include, or turn on __TRILIUM_PH_3__Editable__TRILIUM_PH_4__ (__TRILIUM_PH_5__) in its toolbar, as for any __TRILIUM_PH_6__Include Note__TRILIUM_PH_7__. Press the button again to stop editing. The changes are saved to the referenced blocks, and the rest of the note stays as it is. The button is grayed out where the blocks cannot be edited, such as in a read-only note. An excerpt has no __TRILIUM_PH_8__Fullscreen__TRILIUM_PH_9__ button.
units.context: Block references > Including the referenced blocks

units.source: If a referenced block was deleted, the include shows __TRILIUM_PH_0__Broken reference__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Block references > Including the referenced blocks

units.source: References can be copied only from a note being edited, and not in the mobile layout.
An include of a range that covers only part of a list or a quote, such as from its second item to a paragraph after it, cannot be edited in place.
Deleting a block breaks the references to it.
Block references are not kept when exporting to Markdown. On a __TRILIUM_PH_0__shared page__TRILIUM_PH_1__, a block reference opens the whole note.
Collapsible blocks are sections of content that can be expanded and collapsed, letting you hide detail until it's needed.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__An arrow__TRILIUM_PH_1__ that expands or collapses the block when clicked.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__A summary line__TRILIUM_PH_1__ that acts as the block's title. With the cursor in the summary line, press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_3__+__TRILIUM_PH_4__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_5__ to expand or collapse the block.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__A drag handle__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for repositioning the block within the note.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__The body__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which is hidden while the block is collapsed. It can hold any kind of content, including nested collapsible blocks. To break out of a collapsible block and continue typing outside it, press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_3__ twice at the end of the block.
You can use the arrow keys to move freely with the cursor between the summary line, the block's body, and the text around the block.

units.context: Collapsible blocks > Inserting a collapsible block

units.source: In the formatting bar, go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Insert__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Collapsible Block__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Collapsible blocks > Inserting a collapsible block

units.source: Place multiple collapsible blocks one after another to create an accordion, where each block can be expanded or collapsed independently.
units.context: Collapsible blocks > Inserting a collapsible block

units.source: A heading can be collapsed to hide the content under it, up to the next heading of the same or a higher level. A lower heading is hidden along with the rest, and keeps its own state.

To collapse or expand a heading, click the arrow at the end of the heading. The arrow appears while the mouse is over the heading or the cursor is in it, and stays visible while the heading is collapsed.
To use the keyboard instead, place the cursor in the heading and press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_3__+__TRILIUM_PH_4__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
The menu of the drag handle beside a heading also offers __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collapse section__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Expand section__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
The collapsed state is saved with the note, so a heading stays collapsed when the note is opened again.

units.context: Collapsible headings > Editing around a collapsed heading

units.source: Pressing __TRILIUM_PH_0__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_1__ at the end of a collapsed heading adds a new heading of the same level below the hidden content.
units.context: Collapsible headings > Editing around a collapsed heading

units.source: The arrow keys move the cursor past the hidden content.
units.context: Collapsible headings > Editing around a collapsed heading

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Backspace__TRILIUM_PH_1__ right below a collapsed heading's content, or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Delete__TRILIUM_PH_3__ at the end of a collapsed heading, expands the heading instead of deleting the hidden content. If the line right below the hidden content is empty, either key deletes that empty line instead.
units.context: Collapsible headings > Editing around a collapsed heading

units.source: Dragging a collapsed heading by its drag handle moves its hidden content along with it.
units.context: Collapsible headings > Editing around a collapsed heading

units.source: A collapsed heading expands when content is added to its section, for example by pasting or by dropping a block under it.
units.context: Collapsible headings > Editing around a collapsed heading

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search in note__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the table of contents and links to a block show hidden content when they lead to it, without expanding the heading.
units.context: Collapsible headings > Editing around a collapsed heading

units.source: The arrow also works in notes shown read-only (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Read-Only Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__), but there the changes are not saved: the note shows its saved state again when it is reopened.

To use the keyboard there, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to move to a heading that has content under it, then __TRILIUM_PH_2__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Space__TRILIUM_PH_5__ to collapse or expand it.
Shared notes and printouts always show all the content.
The collapsed state is kept in HTML exports, but not in Markdown exports.
The spell-checking of the note, when in a browser. The desktop installation has a dedicated spellchecking section.
Whether the text is displayed from right-to-left, for languages such as Arabic, Hebrew, etc.

How typed quotes are __TRILIUM_PH_0__automatically replaced__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (e.g. English uses __TRILIUM_PH_2__, whereas some languages use __TRILIUM_PH_3__). This applies only if __TRILIUM_PH_4__Options__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Text__TRILIUM_PH_7__ → __TRILIUM_PH_8__Single/Double quotation marks__TRILIUM_PH_9__ is set to __TRILIUM_PH_10__Based on note's content language__TRILIUM_PH_11__.
Which languages are offered by the __TRILIUM_PH_0__In-editor AI assistant__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for translation.
The language and the text direction the content is marked with on a __TRILIUM_PH_0__shared page__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which screen readers and browsers follow.
Setting the language of a single note__TRILIUM_PH_0__

units.source: To set the language of the content of a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note, there is a language selector in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Status bar__TRILIUM_PH_3__ indicated by a __TRILIUM_PH_4__ icon.

units.source: By default, no language is configured. To configure them, go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Language & Region__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Content languages__TRILIUM_PH_5__, or select the __TRILIUM_PH_6__Configure languages...__TRILIUM_PH_7__ item when setting the language. The enabled languages are listed by their native names, sorted alphabetically, which is also the order the language selector shows them in. Here you can:
units.context: Content language & Right-to-left support > Adjusting the list of languages

units.source: Add a language by pressing the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Add a language__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button (__TRILIUM_PH_3__Add another language__TRILIUM_PH_4__ once one is enabled), which also shows how many languages are left, and then selecting it.
units.context: Content language & Right-to-left support > Adjusting the list of languages

Content language & Right-to-left support > Default content language

units.source: Notes that do not have a language of their own follow __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Language & Region__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Default content language__TRILIUM_PH_5__. It is set to English initially, and can be set to any content language, or to __TRILIUM_PH_6__Based on the application's language__TRILIUM_PH_7__.

units.source: Content tabs group several titled panels of content into one block that shows a single panel at a time. They suit content that comes in variants (such as installation steps for each operating system or the same snippet in several programming languages).
__TRILIUM_PH_0__A single row of tab titles__TRILIUM_PH_1__, above the panel or, when the tabs are aligned at the bottom, below it. The title of the panel that is showing is highlighted.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__The panel of the active tab.__TRILIUM_PH_1__ A panel can hold any kind of content (including nested tabs blocks).

units.context: Content tabs > Inserting a tabs block

units.source: In the formatting bar, go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Insert__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Tabs__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Content tabs > Inserting a tabs block

units.source: Alternatively, type __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and press __TRILIUM_PH_1__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_2__, as described in __TRILIUM_PH_3__Slash Commands__TRILIUM_PH_4__.
units.context: Content tabs > Inserting a tabs block

units.source: A new block contains two tabs, named “Tab 1” and “Tab 2”. Any content that was selected prior to inserting the tabs will be moved into the first tab. The title of the first tab is selected, so typing replaces it.
units.context: Content tabs > Inserting a tabs block
Content tabs > Scrolling through the titles

units.source: When the titles of a block do not fit on their row, a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button and a __TRILIUM_PH_1__ button appear at its ends:
units.context: Content tabs > Scrolling through the titles

units.source: To scroll the titles, click one of the buttons. Holding a button down scrolls the titles continuously until it is released.
units.context: Content tabs > Scrolling through the titles

units.source: On a touch screen, the titles can also be swiped sideways.
units.context: Content tabs > Scrolling through the titles

units.source: Whenever another tab is shown (for example by clicking its title, by moving the cursor into it or by following a link to it), the row scrolls so that its whole title is visible. This works the same while editing, in read-only notes and on shared pages.
units.context: Content tabs > Scrolling through the titles

units.source: To show a tab, click its title or move the cursor into it.
To move from a title into its panel, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
The label of a tab can be formatted just like normal text, including support for __TRILIUM_PH_0__Icons__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
While the cursor is inside a tabs block, a toolbar appears above it with the following buttons:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__(Add tab)__TRILIUM_PH_2__ inserts a tab after the current one and selects its title.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__(Remove tab)__TRILIUM_PH_2__ removes the current tab. Removing the last tab removes the whole block.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__(Move tab left)__TRILIUM_PH_2__ and __TRILIUM_PH_3__ (__TRILIUM_PH_4__Move tab right)__TRILIUM_PH_5__ change the order of the tabs.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__(More actions)__TRILIUM_PH_2__ opens a menu with the actions of the toolbar and a few more.
The __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__More actions__TRILIUM_PH_2__ menu has the following entries:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Add new tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__ inserts a tab after the current one, like the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ button.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Copy reference to this tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__ copies a link to the current tab, as described below.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Move tab right__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Move tab left__TRILIUM_PH_3__ change the order of the tabs.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Tab alignment__TRILIUM_PH_1__ places the tab titles above the panel (__TRILIUM_PH_2__Align tabs at top__TRILIUM_PH_3__, the default) or below it (__TRILIUM_PH_4__Align tabs at bottom__TRILIUM_PH_5__).
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Delete tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__ removes the current tab, like the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ button.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Delete all tabs__TRILIUM_PH_1__ removes the whole tabs block and leaves an empty paragraph in its place. In a tabs block nested inside another, only the inner block is removed.
The tab that is showing is not saved with the note: every tabs block opens on its first tab.

units.context: Content tabs > Editing tabs > Adding tabs

units.source: While the cursor is in a tab, either in its title or in its panel, you can use these key combinations:
units.context: Content tabs > Editing tabs > Adding tabs

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ + __TRILIUM_PH_2__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_3__: Add a tab after the current one.
units.context: Content tabs > Editing tabs > Adding tabs

units.context: Content tabs > Editing tabs > Adding tabs

units.source: The new tab is shown and its title is selected, so typing replaces it.
units.context: Content tabs > Editing tabs > Adding tabs

Content tabs > Editing tabs > Reordering tabs

units.source: While the cursor is in a tab, either in its title or in its panel, you can use these key combinations:
units.context: Content tabs > Editing tabs > Reordering tabs

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ + __TRILIUM_PH_2__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_3__ + __TRILIUM_PH_4__Right__TRILIUM_PH_5__: Move the tab to the right.

Content tabs > Editing tabs > Reordering tabs

Content tabs > Moving content between tabs

units.source: To move content to another tab, select it in the panel, and then use these key combinations:
units.context: Content tabs > Moving content between tabs

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ + __TRILIUM_PH_2__Right__TRILIUM_PH_3__: Move to the tab on the right.

Content tabs > Moving content between tabs
Content tabs > Moving content between tabs

units.source: The tab that receives the content is shown, with the content still selected, so pressing the key again moves it on to the next tab. Paragraphs, list items, tables and other blocks move whole, even when only part of them is selected. Content moved to a tab on the left goes to the end of that tab, and content moved to a tab on the right goes to its start, so it keeps its place in the reading order.
units.context: Content tabs > Moving content between tabs

units.source: Without a selection, or with a selection in a tab title, these keys keep their usual function: moving the cursor by word, or selecting up to the start or end of the tab.
units.context: Content tabs > Moving content between tabs

units.source: When a tabs block and a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Multicolumn layout__TRILIUM_PH_1__ are nested in one another, the key combinations act on the one closest to the cursor.
units.context: Content tabs > Moving content between tabs

units.source: In __TRILIUM_PH_0__Read-Only Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and on __TRILIUM_PH_2__Sharing__TRILIUM_PH_3__, tabs blocks work as tabs as well:
To show a tab, click its title, or focus it and press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Space__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
To move between the titles of a block, use the arrow keys, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Home__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__End__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
A tab without a title shows “Tab title” in place of one.
In read-only notes, a title too long for its tab fades out where it is cut off. To read the rest of it, swipe it sideways or drag it with the mouse.

units.context: Content tabs > Linking to a tab

units.source: A link can point to a single tab, much like a link to a block (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Block references__TRILIUM_PH_1__):
units.context: Content tabs > Linking to a tab

units.source: Place the cursor in the tab, either in its title or in its panel.
units.context: Content tabs > Linking to a tab

units.source: In the toolbar of the tabs block, open the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__More actions__TRILIUM_PH_2__ menu and select __TRILIUM_PH_3__Copy reference to this tab__TRILIUM_PH_4__. Alternatively, right-click the text and select __TRILIUM_PH_5__Copy__TRILIUM_PH_6__ → __TRILIUM_PH_7__Copy link to this tab__TRILIUM_PH_8__. The tab flashes briefly.
units.context: Content tabs > Linking to a tab

units.source: Go to the note where to insert the link and press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__V__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

Markdown export and import write tabs blocks in the content tabs syntax of Material for MkDocs, described in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Supported syntax__TRILIUM_PH_1__. __TRILIUM_PH_2__Markdown__TRILIUM_PH_3__ notes use the same syntax, show the blocks as tabs in their preview and insert them with __TRILIUM_PH_4__. When editing a document that becomes too large, you can split it into sub-notes:
Select the desired text and cut it to the clipboard.
Create a new sub-note and name it.
Paste the content from the clipboard into the sub-note.

Trilium can automate this process. Select some text within the note, and in the selection toolbar, click the scissors icon for the "cut & pasted selection to sub-note" action. The heading is automatically detected and the new sub-note is named accordingly. You can also assign a keyboard shortcut for this action. This functionality is available through the block toolbar icon. On a phone, the scissors are at the end of the text formatting row, which shows as you select text.
The code blocks feature allows entering pieces of code in text notes.
Note that this feature is meant for generally small snippets of code. For larger files such as an entire log, see the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note type instead.

units.source: Since TriliumNext v0.90.12, Trilium will try to offer syntax highlighting to the code block. Note that the syntax highlighting mechanism is slightly different than the one in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes as different technologies are involved.
units.context: Code blocks > Syntax highlighting & color schemes
Code blocks > Syntax highlighting & color schemes

units.source: When the language is set to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Auto-detected__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (by default), Trilium will try to identify the programming language (or similar) that corresponds to the given snippet of text and highlight it. Only the languages enabled in __TRILIUM_PH_2__Options__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Code Notes__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Available MIME types in the dropdown__TRILIUM_PH_7__ are considered. If this is problematic, consider changing the language of the code block manually.
units.context: Code blocks > Syntax highlighting & color schemes

units.source: When the language is set to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Plain text__TRILIUM_PH_1__, there will be no syntax highlighting.
units.context: Code blocks > Syntax highlighting & color schemes

units.source: Note that when editing a text note, syntax highlighting is automatically disabled if the code block is too big (somewhere around 500 lines). In __TRILIUM_PH_0__Read-Only Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__, in print and on a __TRILIUM_PH_2__shared page__TRILIUM_PH_3__, a code block of more than 500 lines or 50,000 characters is shown without syntax highlighting. These limits are not configurable.
units.context: Code blocks > Syntax highlighting & color schemes

units.source: In order to configure this new feature, a section has been added in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Appearance__TRILIUM_PH_3__ to control the syntax highlighting. There the color scheme can be chosen, from a builtin selection of themes from Highlight.js. __TRILIUM_PH_4__VS Code (Light)__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and __TRILIUM_PH_6__VS Code (Dark)__TRILIUM_PH_7__ use the same colors as the default themes of __TRILIUM_PH_8__Code__TRILIUM_PH_9__ notes, so a code block and a code note color the same code alike.
units.context: Code blocks > Syntax highlighting & color schemes

units.source: It is possible to disable the syntax highlighting for all the notes by selecting “No syntax highlighting” in the “Color scheme” option.
units.context: Code blocks > Syntax highlighting & color schemes

units.source: Word wrapping is disabled by default, but can be configured from the same section.
units.context: Code blocks > Syntax highlighting & color schemes

units.source: The tab width can also be adjusted from Options.
units.context: Code blocks > Syntax highlighting & color schemes
Code blocks > Syntax highlighting & color schemes

units.source: In order to achieve the syntax highlight, the Highlight.js library is being used. Do note that support for syntax highlighting in code blocks is not a supported feature of the text editor we are using CKEditor), but rather a hack which makes use of the highlights API (used for highlighting search results for example). Nevertheless, we haven't noticed any major issues during the development of the feature, but feel free to report any issues you might have.
units.context: Code blocks > Syntax highlighting & color schemes

units.source: Most of the work to achieve the syntax highlight itself was already done by __TRILIUM_PH_0__antoniotejada__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in __TRILIUM_PH_2__https://github.com/antoniotejada/Trilium-SyntaxHighlightWidget__TRILIUM_PH_3__. On our side we added customization but also additional functionality.
units.context: Code blocks > Syntax highlighting & color schemes

units.context: Code blocks > Syntax highlighting & color schemes > Migrating from existing syntax highlight plugins

units.source: If you are already using a syntax highlighting plugin such as the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Trilium-SyntaxHighlightWidget__TRILIUM_PH_1__ we are basing off of, it is important to disable that plugin before upgrading in order for it not to conflict with our implementation.

Code blocks > Text replacements and ligatures

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Automatic replacements__TRILIUM_PH_1__ are a feature of text notes which converts some character sequences into another and some of them interfere with programming text, such as the conversion of quotes. While in a code block, the automatic replacements __TRILIUM_PH_2__are not effect__TRILIUM_PH_3__. The only way the automatic replacements can interfere is if the text is typed/pasted before being put in a code block.
units.context: Code blocks > Text replacements and ligatures

units.source: A different feature is __TRILIUM_PH_0__programming ligatures__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which is simply a display affordance which turns __TRILIUM_PH_2__ into __TRILIUM_PH_3__ or __TRILIUM_PH_4__ as __TRILIUM_PH_5__ . These come from the __TRILIUM_PH_6__font__TRILIUM_PH_7__. The underlying text is not actually changed, and copying it out gives you back __TRILIUM_PH_8__ and __TRILIUM_PH_9__.
units.context: Code blocks > Text replacements and ligatures

units.source: Ligatures can be disabled in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1____TRILIUM_PH_2__→ Appearance → Fonts → Programming ligatures.__TRILIUM_PH_3__
units.context: Code blocks > Text replacements and ligatures

units.source: Extended code blocks are experimental, and they change as they mature. To use them, turn on __TRILIUM_PH_0__Extended code blocks__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in __TRILIUM_PH_2__Options__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Advanced__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Experimental Options__TRILIUM_PH_7__.

An extended code block is a code block that is edited with the code editor of a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note, inside the text. It has the same syntax highlighting and code folding as a code note, and it suits longer pieces of code.

To insert one, open the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Insert__TRILIUM_PH_2__ menu of the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_4__ and choose __TRILIUM_PH_5__ __TRILIUM_PH_6__Extended code block__TRILIUM_PH_7__, after __TRILIUM_PH_8__Columns__TRILIUM_PH_9__. It is also available as __TRILIUM_PH_10__Extended code block__TRILIUM_PH_11__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_12__Slash Commands__TRILIUM_PH_13__.

A new block is empty and editable, in a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Full__TRILIUM_PH_1__ box, and takes the focus. Its language is the one set last on an extended code block, or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Plain text__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
A click places the cursor in the code, as in a code block. Over a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Small__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Medium__TRILIUM_PH_3__ box, the mouse wheel scrolls the code.

The block shows in a box like the one of an included code note, with the corners and the shadow of a code block. While the block is editable, its language shows in its top corner, as for a code block. While it is read-only, because __TRILIUM_PH_0__Editable__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is unchecked or the note is one of the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Read-Only Notes__TRILIUM_PH_3__, that corner has a __TRILIUM_PH_4__ __TRILIUM_PH_5__Copy to clipboard__TRILIUM_PH_6__ button instead, as a code block of a read-only note does.

Its toolbar has the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Change language mode__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Change tab width__TRILIUM_PH_3__ menus of an embedded code file, described in __TRILIUM_PH_4__Editing an include in place__TRILIUM_PH_5__ in __TRILIUM_PH_6__Include Note__TRILIUM_PH_7__, and the __TRILIUM_PH_8__ __TRILIUM_PH_9__Copy to clipboard__TRILIUM_PH_10__ button, which copies the code as the one of a code block does. Its __TRILIUM_PH_11__ __TRILIUM_PH_12__More actions__TRILIUM_PH_13__ menu has __TRILIUM_PH_14__Editable__TRILIUM_PH_15__, which shows the code read-only once unchecked, the __TRILIUM_PH_16__Word wrap__TRILIUM_PH_17__ and __TRILIUM_PH_18__Line numbers__TRILIUM_PH_19__ submenus, the __TRILIUM_PH_20__Size__TRILIUM_PH_21__ submenu, with __TRILIUM_PH_22__Resizable__TRILIUM_PH_23__, __TRILIUM_PH_24__Full__TRILIUM_PH_25__ and __TRILIUM_PH_26__Default__TRILIUM_PH_27__, the __TRILIUM_PH_28__Position__TRILIUM_PH_29__ submenu, and __TRILIUM_PH_30__ __TRILIUM_PH_31__Delete block__TRILIUM_PH_32__, which removes the block from the note.

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Position__TRILIUM_PH_1__ submenu places the block as it places an include, described in __TRILIUM_PH_2__Positioning__TRILIUM_PH_3__ in __TRILIUM_PH_4__Include Note__TRILIUM_PH_5__: on lines of its own at the left, the center or the right, or at the left or the right with the text running beside it. Only a __TRILIUM_PH_6__Resizable__TRILIUM_PH_7__ box can be placed, and it takes the full width of the note until it is resized narrower. In the mobile layout, a block with a position other than __TRILIUM_PH_8__Align center__TRILIUM_PH_9__ takes the full width.
The changes made in the block are part of the undo history of the text note.

The code stays in the note as a code block of its language. The Markdown export, __TRILIUM_PH_0__shared pages__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and printing show it as a code block, and copying it into another application pastes a code block. Pasted into a text note, it becomes an extended code block again, with its settings.

Turning __TRILIUM_PH_0__Extended code blocks__TRILIUM_PH_1__ off again removes them from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert__TRILIUM_PH_3__ menu and the slash commands only: the extended code blocks already in notes keep working. A version of Trilium without this feature shows them as code blocks, and saves them back as code blocks, without their box size and other settings.
Inline code formats text using a monospace font to indicate technical content in a sentence such as code, paths, etc.

Via the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_1__, look for the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ button.
Type `code` where __TRILIUM_PH_0__ is the desired text to be automatically formatted as inline code.

Code blocks display a snippet of code as a dedicated block:
A code block with JavaScript syntax highlight enabled.

This allows marking a portion of text as a shortcut key.

To apply this style, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button in __TRILIUM_PH_1__ group from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_3__. On the floating toolbar, the buttons appear when selecting a text.

Alternatively, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_3__+__TRILIUM_PH_4__K__TRILIUM_PH_5__ combination to apply keyboard shortcut formatting to the current text selection.
The formatting can be removed by pressing again the button (from the UI or from the keyboard), or by using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Remove formatting__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button.
Footnotes are a good place to insert references to a paragraph or details that are displayed at the bottom of the note.

To insert a new footnote, open the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Insert__TRILIUM_PH_2__ menu of the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_4__ and choose __TRILIUM_PH_5__ __TRILIUM_PH_6__Footnote__TRILIUM_PH_7__ (or select __TRILIUM_PH_8__New footnote__TRILIUM_PH_9__ in its submenu).

To insert a reference to an existing footnote, open the submenu of __TRILIUM_PH_0__Footnote__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and select __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert footnote__TRILIUM_PH_3__, followed by the number of the footnote to insert.
Hovering over a reference (e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_0__) will display the content of the footnote in a tooltip for easy reference.
Clicking on a reference in the text (e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_0__) will navigate to the corresponding footnote.
Similarly, clicking on the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button of a footnote will navigate to the corresponding reference in the text.

The Format Painter is a feature in text notes that allows users to copy the formatting of text (such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__bold__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__italic__TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__Strikethrough__TRILIUM_PH_5__, etc.) and apply it to other parts of the document. It helps maintain consistent formatting and accelerates the creation of rich content.

Click the text that you want to copy the formatting from and use the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Copy formatting__TRILIUM_PH_1__ toolbar button (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) to copy the style. Then select the target text with your mouse, or click a word, to apply the formatting.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__To copy the formatting__TRILIUM_PH_1__: Place the cursor inside text with some formatting and click the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Copy formatting__TRILIUM_PH_3__ toolbar button. The mouse cursor changes to indicate the painter is armed.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__To paint with the copied formatting__TRILIUM_PH_1__: Select the target text with your mouse. The formatting is applied when you release the button, and the painter disarms — the cursor returns to normal. Clicking or tapping a word applies it to the whole word.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__To paint a selection made otherwise__TRILIUM_PH_1__, such as with the keyboard or the selection handles of a touch screen: select the target text, then use the toolbar button again, which reads __TRILIUM_PH_2__Apply formatting__TRILIUM_PH_3__ once the selection has moved. On a phone, the formatting row stays open while the painter is armed, so the button stays in reach.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__To cancel without painting__TRILIUM_PH_1__: Click the toolbar button again before selecting other text, or press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Escape__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

Painting with block-level formatting (like headings or image styles) is not supported yet. This is because, in __TRILIUM_PH_0__CKEditor__TRILIUM_PH_1__, they are considered a part of the content rather than text formatting.
A click outside a word, such as between two spaces or at the end of a line, only primes the caret, so text you type there takes the copied formatting.
The painter is one-shot; each paint requires copying the formatting again.
Trilium allows two different editing experiences for text notes, based on your preference.

The type of formatting toolbar can be changed by going to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and then looking for the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Text Notes__TRILIUM_PH_3__ section. In it, look for the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_5__ category.
The floating bar is a more minimalist option, in which the formatting is hidden behind two different popups.
The first popup is the block-level popup. This will appear to the left of the current paragraph you are currently editing, as a sequence of dots:__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__
Clicking this popup will reveal the formatting options that are specific to the entire paragraph, such as setting a heading, lists, tables, etc.

The dots are also a drag handle: drag them to move the paragraph, all the selected paragraphs, or a selected element such as an image, a table or an included note to another place in the note. Right-clicking them opens a menu that copies a reference to the paragraph or to the selected paragraphs, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Block references__TRILIUM_PH_1__. The menu is headed by the type of the block it acts on, such as __TRILIUM_PH_2__Paragraph__TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__Table__TRILIUM_PH_5__ or __TRILIUM_PH_6__List item__TRILIUM_PH_7__, or by the number of blocks when there are several. For a single block other than a paragraph, the __TRILIUM_PH_8__ button at the end of the heading opens the help page of its type in a split beside the note. Its first items, __TRILIUM_PH_9__Insert above__TRILIUM_PH_10__ and __TRILIUM_PH_11__Insert below__TRILIUM_PH_12__, list the __TRILIUM_PH_13__Slash Commands__TRILIUM_PH_14__ that insert content or turn a paragraph into another block, and add the one picked in a new paragraph above or below the paragraph. Beside a list item, __TRILIUM_PH_15__Insert item above__TRILIUM_PH_16__, __TRILIUM_PH_17__Insert item below__TRILIUM_PH_18__ and __TRILIUM_PH_19__Insert child item__TRILIUM_PH_20__ take their place and add an empty item. After them, __TRILIUM_PH_21__Cut__TRILIUM_PH_22__ and __TRILIUM_PH_23__Copy__TRILIUM_PH_24__ put the whole paragraph or the selected paragraphs on the clipboard, even when only part of their text is selected; __TRILIUM_PH_25__Cut__TRILIUM_PH_26__ also removes them. Once an AI provider is configured, __TRILIUM_PH_27__AI assistant__TRILIUM_PH_28__ follows them, with the same items as the __TRILIUM_PH_29__ button of the toolbar, and works on the whole paragraph or the selected paragraphs rather than on the selected text, see __TRILIUM_PH_30__In-editor AI assistant__TRILIUM_PH_31__. Its last item, __TRILIUM_PH_32__Delete__TRILIUM_PH_33__, deletes the paragraph or the selected paragraphs at once, without asking for confirmation; __TRILIUM_PH_34__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_35__+__TRILIUM_PH_36__Z__TRILIUM_PH_37__ brings them back.
The inline popup appears automatically when selecting a text:
All the options here apply only to the selected portion of text, such as changing the font size, or making the text bold.
The fixed formatting offers a more traditional editing paradigm, usually useful if a lot of formatting is needed.

All the options are combined into a single toolbar that will appear at the above the note. When using __TRILIUM_PH_0__Split View__TRILIUM_PH_1__, a single toolbar will be available to save space and it acts on the active note.

The sequence of dots to the left of the current paragraph is still shown as a drag handle: drag it to move the paragraph, all the selected paragraphs, or a selected element such as an image, a table or an included note to another place in the note. Releasing it above the first paragraph or below the last one moves it to the start or the end of the note. Clicking or right-clicking it opens a menu that copies a reference to the block, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Block references__TRILIUM_PH_1__. The last item of that menu, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Delete__TRILIUM_PH_3__, deletes the blocks that a drag would move, without asking for confirmation; __TRILIUM_PH_4__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_5__+__TRILIUM_PH_6__Z__TRILIUM_PH_7__ brings them back. Hovering the drag handle shades the blocks that it moves, and they stay shaded while its menu is open: inside a table, this is the paragraph in the current cell, and with several cells selected, the whole table. The menu is headed by the type of the shaded block, such as __TRILIUM_PH_8__Paragraph__TRILIUM_PH_9__, __TRILIUM_PH_10__Table__TRILIUM_PH_11__ or __TRILIUM_PH_12__List item__TRILIUM_PH_13__, or by the number of shaded blocks when there are several. For a single block other than a paragraph, the __TRILIUM_PH_14__ button at the end of the heading opens the help page of its type in a split beside the note. Its first items, __TRILIUM_PH_15__Insert above__TRILIUM_PH_16__ and __TRILIUM_PH_17__Insert below__TRILIUM_PH_18__, list the __TRILIUM_PH_19__Slash Commands__TRILIUM_PH_20__ that insert content or turn a paragraph into another block, and add the one picked in a new paragraph above or below the shaded blocks; typing while one of them is open filters it. They are shown only while slash commands are turned on. Beside a list item, __TRILIUM_PH_21__Insert item above__TRILIUM_PH_22__, __TRILIUM_PH_23__Insert item below__TRILIUM_PH_24__ and __TRILIUM_PH_25__Insert child item__TRILIUM_PH_26__ take their place and add an empty item: above the item, below it and its nested items, or as its first nested item. In a table cell, __TRILIUM_PH_27__Insert row above__TRILIUM_PH_28__ and __TRILIUM_PH_29__Insert row below__TRILIUM_PH_30__ follow them. After them, __TRILIUM_PH_31__Cut__TRILIUM_PH_32__ and __TRILIUM_PH_33__Copy__TRILIUM_PH_34__ put the shaded blocks on the clipboard, and __TRILIUM_PH_35__Cut__TRILIUM_PH_36__ also removes them. Once an AI provider is configured, __TRILIUM_PH_37__AI assistant__TRILIUM_PH_38__ follows them, with the same items as the __TRILIUM_PH_39__ button of the toolbar, and works on the shaded blocks rather than on the selected text, see __TRILIUM_PH_40__In-editor AI assistant__TRILIUM_PH_41__. The drag handle is not shown in the mobile layout.

Beside an empty paragraph, the dots turn into a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button. Clicking it opens the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Slash Commands__TRILIUM_PH_2__ that insert content or turn the paragraph into another block as a menu, with a box at its top to filter them, and right-clicking it still opens the menu of the block. The button is shown only while __TRILIUM_PH_3__Options__TRILIUM_PH_4__ → __TRILIUM_PH_5__Text Notes__TRILIUM_PH_6__ → __TRILIUM_PH_7__Features__TRILIUM_PH_8__ → __TRILIUM_PH_9__Slash commands__TRILIUM_PH_10__ is turned on.

By default, if the toolbar does not fit on the screen, the rest of the options will be grouped into a single option at the end. It is possible to display items on multiple lines by checking the corresponding option in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section.
Trilium provides headings to define sections within text. Headings are numbered from 2 to 6.
The reason why Heading 1 is missing from the list is that it is being reserved for the title of note.
To turn a heading back into a normal text, select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Paragraph__TRILIUM_PH_1__ from the list.
Apart from using the UI, it is also possible to quickly insert headings using the Markdown-like shortcuts:
A heading can be collapsed to hide the content under it, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collapsible headings__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
One way to highlight a portion of text is to increase the size of the font.
To do so, select some text and choose an option from the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Font size__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) selector (as pictured to the right).
Unlike other text editors such as Microsoft Word, the font size is relative (i.e. “Tiny”, “Small” instead of a number like 12).
Avoid using this feature just to simply make all text bigger. In that case it's generally better to adjust the font size for all notes in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or by zooming.

This is mostly useful for units of measure (e.g. cm3 for cubic centimeters) and chemical notations (e.g. NaHCO3)
For mathematical formulas, prefer the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Math Equations__TRILIUM_PH_1__ feature instead.

units.context: General formatting > Font color and background color

units.source: Selected text can be colored with one of the predefined colors from a palette or any color can be selected using the color picker (__TRILIUM_PH_0__).
units.context: General formatting > Font color and background color

units.source: Once there is at least one color defined in the document, it will appear in the list for easy reuse.
units.context: General formatting > Font color and background color

units.source: Colors adapt to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__theme__TRILIUM_PH_1__. Trilium shows each color in a lighter or darker shade that suits the current theme, so the text stays readable after switching between light and dark themes. The hue stays the same: red text is red in both themes, only lighter or darker. This applies to the palette, the color picker and the document colors alike, and to shared notes too. The swatches of the font color and background color dropdowns show the same shades on a sample text, "Ab": as the color of the text, or as the background behind it. Printed notes and PDF exports always use the shades of light themes, which suit white paper. The note itself keeps the color as it was picked, so an exported note shows it unchanged.
units.context: General formatting > Font color and background color

units.source: Colors applied with older versions of Trilium are shown exactly as they were picked, until the note is next edited.
units.context: General formatting > Font color and background color

units.source: Older browsers that can't adapt colors show them exactly as they were picked.
units.context: General formatting > Font color and background color

units.source: To remove either the background or foreground color of a text, select the corresponding formatting button (__TRILIUM_PH_0__ or __TRILIUM_PH_1__) and press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Remove color__TRILIUM_PH_3__ (__TRILIUM_PH_4__) or use the __TRILIUM_PH_5__Remove formatting__TRILIUM_PH_6__ (__TRILIUM_PH_7__) toolbar item.
units.context: General formatting > Font color and background color

units.source: The __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Remove formatting__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button is a quick way to eliminate the general formatting styling of a particular text.
Simply select the text and press the button to remove the formatting (bold, italic, colors, sizes, etc.). If the text does not have any removable formatting, the button will appear disabled.
Note that heading styles are not taken into consideration, these must be manually changed back to a paragraph according to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Headings__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section.

When pasting content that comes with undesired formatting, an alternative to pasting and then removing formatting is pasting as plain text via __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_3__+__TRILIUM_PH_4__V__TRILIUM_PH_5__.

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Format Painter__TRILIUM_PH_1__ allows users to copy the formatting of text (such as bold, italic, Strikethrough, etc.) and apply it to other parts of the document. It helps maintain consistent formatting and accelerates the creation of rich content.
When exported to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Markdown__TRILIUM_PH_1__, most of the general formatting is maintained such as headings, bold, italic, underline, etc.
This page has been relocated to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Outline tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Image references are an easy way to embed the preview of another note type into a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note.
Go to one of the supported notes (listed above) and look for the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button in the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Note buttons__TRILIUM_PH_2__ area.
Go to a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note and use the Paste function to insert the reference to that note.
Double-clicking an image reference from a text note will automatically open the target note.
Clicking an image reference while __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is pressed will open the target note in a new tab.
Modifying the target note should also update the image reference. If that doesn't happen, consider __TRILIUM_PH_0__Refreshing the application__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Trilium supports storing and displaying images. Supported formats are PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, WebP, AVIF and SVG.

An image can be uploaded in the form of note's __TRILIUM_PH_0__attachment__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or as a standalone __TRILIUM_PH_2__note__TRILIUM_PH_3__ placed into the __TRILIUM_PH_4__note tree__TRILIUM_PH_5__. Its reference can be copied into a text note, in order to display it in the text itself.
To add an image to the note:
Simply drag it from file explorer onto the note editor inside Trilium and the image will be uploaded.

Alternatively, in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_1__, press the __TRILIUM_PH_2____TRILIUM_PH_3__Attach file__TRILIUM_PH_4__ button and select __TRILIUM_PH_5__Image__TRILIUM_PH_6__.
On the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Mobile Frontend__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the same menu also offers __TRILIUM_PH_2__Camera__TRILIUM_PH_3__, which takes a photo and inserts it.
You can also copy and paste an image from web (see section below).

Where the image goes depends on the cursor. In an empty paragraph, the image is displayed on a line of its own. In a list item, or after some text in a paragraph, the image is inserted __TRILIUM_PH_0__In line__TRILIUM_PH_1__, inside the text. To change it afterwards, use the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Image position__TRILIUM_PH_3__ button described in the alignment section below.

To link a picture instead of displaying it, attach it with __TRILIUM_PH_0__Attach file as a link__TRILIUM_PH_1__, from the __TRILIUM_PH_2____TRILIUM_PH_3__Attach file__TRILIUM_PH_4__ button. See __TRILIUM_PH_5__Attachments__TRILIUM_PH_6__.

units.context: Images > Clipboard & automatic download of images

units.source: Trilium has a special handling for images copied to and pasted from the clipboard.
units.context: Images > Clipboard & automatic download of images

units.source: For a mix of text and images, the images are downloaded automatically by the server (or desktop app, depending on what is being used).
units.context: Images > Clipboard & automatic download of images

units.source: This means that the image must be publicly accessible and reachable from wherever Trilium is running. Inaccessible images will end up as broken images.
units.context: Images > Clipboard & automatic download of images

units.source: If a single image is pasted into Trilium, it will prefer the image that comes in the clipboard. This makes it possible to copy images that Trilium would not otherwise be able to reach, such as Google Chat, Slack, etc.
units.context: Images > Clipboard & automatic download of images

units.source: When a text with images is copied from Trilium and pasted in another app (such as Microsoft Word or LibreOffice Writer), the images will be preserved.
units.context: Images > Clipboard & automatic download of images

units.source: The automatic download of images is enabled by default and can be toggled from __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Media__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Download images automatically.__TRILIUM_PH_5__
units.context: Images > Clipboard & automatic download of images

units.source: Clicking on an image will reveal a popup with multiple options:__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__

The first button of the popup, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Image position__TRILIUM_PH_1__, shows the icon of the image's current position. It opens a menu that groups the positions by how text runs around the image:
The image sits inside a paragraph, like a large character, and moves with the text around it. Use drag & drop or cut-paste to move it around.
The image is displayed on a line of its own, at the left, in the center or at the right; text continues above and below it but not beside it.
The image is displayed at the left or the right, and the text flows beside it.

units.context: Images > Configuring the images > Drawing over an image

units.source: To draw or write over an image, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Convert image to a drawing canvas__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button of its toolbar. The image becomes a drawing canvas that shows all of it, locked in place. See the drawing canvases section of __TRILIUM_PH_3__Include Note__TRILIUM_PH_4__.
units.context: Images > Configuring the images > Drawing over an image

units.source: Since Trilium isn't really meant to be primary storage for image data, it attempts to compress and resize (with pretty aggressive settings) uploaded images before storing them to the database. You may then notice some quality degradation. Basic quality settings is available in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Media__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

If you want to save images in their original resolution, it is recommended to save them as attachment to note (look for the contextual menu in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Import files__TRILIUM_PH_3__).
There are generally two ways to display images side by side:
If they are roughly the same size, simply make the two images in-line, according to the alignment section above. The images can be dragged & dropped onto the same line.
If they are on different size, create a __TRILIUM_PH_0__table__TRILIUM_PH_1__ with invisible borders.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Quick actions__TRILIUM_PH_1__ are a feature of the __TRILIUM_PH_2__In-editor AI assistant__TRILIUM_PH_3__ for __TRILIUM_PH_4__Text__TRILIUM_PH_5__ notes which automatically triggers an LLM suggestion based on a defined prompt. The built-in quick actions come with a predefined prompt, but it is also possible to define your own quick actions.

units.context: Custom AI quick actions > Creating a custom quick action
Custom AI quick actions > Creating a custom quick action

units.source: Right-click the note where you want to place the quick action.
units.context: Custom AI quick actions > Creating a custom quick action
Custom AI quick actions > Creating a custom quick action

units.source: Select __TRILIUM_PH_0__More__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__AI Quick Action__TRILIUM_PH_3__. The entry appears only when AI is enabled.
units.context: Custom AI quick actions > Creating a custom quick action

units.source: Afterwards, simply type in the content of the note the desired prompt. The text can be formatted in the same manner as a normal text note and it will be passed to the LLM as Markdown.
units.context: Custom AI quick actions > Creating a custom quick action

units.source: The title of the note will become the title of the quick action.

units.source: Once a quick action is defined, the action will appear under the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Quick Actions__TRILIUM_PH_1__ dropdown in a group called __TRILIUM_PH_2__Custom__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Custom AI quick actions > Using a quick action

units.source: The AI assistant works on the text you are already writing: select a passage and have it rewritten, translated or turned into a table, or ask for new content at the cursor. Unlike the __TRILIUM_PH_0__AI chat__TRILIUM_PH_1__, it does not open a conversation window, the result is previewed in place and only enters the note when you accept it.

The assistant is only available once at least one provider is configured in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__AI / LLM__TRILIUM_PH_3__, with at least one model selected for it. Until then the toolbar entry is not shown at all.

units.context: In-editor AI assistant > Accessing the AI assistant
In-editor AI assistant > Accessing the AI assistant

units.source: Look for the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button in the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_2__. Press the button itself to enter the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Ask AI__TRILIUM_PH_4__ mode or press the arrow key next to it to access the quick commands and the model selection. On a phone, the button has no arrow: tapping it opens the same menu at the bottom of the screen, with __TRILIUM_PH_5__Ask AI…__TRILIUM_PH_6__ at its top, and a group such as __TRILIUM_PH_7__Translate__TRILIUM_PH_8__ opens as a page of its own.
units.context: In-editor AI assistant > Accessing the AI assistant

units.source: Look for __TRILIUM_PH_0__AI assistant__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or any of the __TRILIUM_PH_2__AI__TRILIUM_PH_3__-prefixed quick commands in __TRILIUM_PH_4__Slash Commands__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
units.context: In-editor AI assistant > Accessing the AI assistant
In-editor AI assistant > Accessing the AI assistant

units.source: Select a text and choose the __TRILIUM_PH_0__AI assistant__TRILIUM_PH_1__ option in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note contextual menu__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: In-editor AI assistant > Accessing the AI assistant

units.source: Click or right-click the drag handle to the left of a paragraph and choose __TRILIUM_PH_0__AI assistant__TRILIUM_PH_1__, see __TRILIUM_PH_2__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_3__. It offers the same items as the toolbar button, and works on the blocks that the handle shades. If the assistant is already open, it starts over on these blocks, and a response you have not inserted is dropped.
units.context: In-editor AI assistant > Accessing the AI assistant
In-editor AI assistant > What the assistant works on

In-editor AI assistant > What the assistant works on
In-editor AI assistant > What the assistant works on

units.source: Nothing is selected, and you pick a quick action
units.context: In-editor AI assistant > What the assistant works on

units.source: The paragraph the cursor is in.
units.context: In-editor AI assistant > What the assistant works on

units.source: Nothing is selected, and you type your own prompt
units.context: In-editor AI assistant > What the assistant works on

units.source: Nothing, the response is new content written at the cursor.
