units.source: Where the preview data comes from__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Link Previews > Where the preview data comes from

units.source: When you insert a link preview, Trilium fetches metadata once and stores it with the note:
units.context: Link Previews > Where the preview data comes from

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__YouTube URLs__TRILIUM_PH_1__: the title, the channel name and the shape of the video are fetched via YouTube's public oEmbed endpoint, and the video's thumbnail is downloaded at up to 1280×720.
units.context: Link Previews > Where the preview data comes from

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Audio and video files__TRILIUM_PH_1__: Trilium reads the start of the file, enough to tell audio from video and, for most MP4 and WebM files, the shape of the video. The rest of the file is not downloaded, and the file is not copied into Trilium. Once a video file is inserted, the editor takes a picture of a frame a few seconds into it as its thumbnail. The frame is read through the Trilium server, so the site of the file sees the server and not your browser. The standalone (browser) and mobile versions have no such server: they read the frame from the site directly, and a video whose site does not let other sites read it has no thumbnail.
units.context: Link Previews > Where the preview data comes from

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__All other URLs__TRILIUM_PH_1__: Trilium fetches the page and reads OpenGraph tags (__TRILIUM_PH_2__, __TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__, __TRILIUM_PH_5__), falling back to the page's __TRILIUM_PH_6__ and __TRILIUM_PH_7__. The site's favicon and the page's image are downloaded as well.
units.context: Link Previews > Where the preview data comes from

units.source: The text is kept in the note's HTML. The images are kept as system __TRILIUM_PH_0__Attachments__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of the note, listed under __TRILIUM_PH_2__Generated by Trilium__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Link Previews > Where the preview data comes from

units.source: Because the data is stored in the note itself, link previews continue to render correctly when you reopen the note, share/publish it, or export to HTML — without any further network requests.
units.context: Link Previews > Where the preview data comes from

units.source: The metadata is captured __TRILIUM_PH_0__at insertion time__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and is not automatically refreshed. If the linked page later changes its title or thumbnail, you'll need to re-insert the link to pick up the new values. To refresh a link, simply create it again.
units.context: Link Previews > Where the preview data comes from

units.source: A YouTube embed inserted before v0.107.0 keeps its smaller thumbnail, shown blurred, until the link is inserted again.
units.context: Link Previews > Where the preview data comes from

units.source: When accessing a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Server Installation__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the data is fetched from the remote URL by the server and not the client.
units.context: Link Previews > Where the preview data comes from

units.source: The Embed display mode supports YouTube and audio and video files. Pages of other video and media platforms fall back to a Card preview.

An audio or video file plays from its address: it needs that address to be reachable, and stops playing when the file is moved or deleted. It plays only in a format that the browser, or the desktop app, supports.
A file served over plain __TRILIUM_PH_0__ might not play in the desktop app or from a Trilium server reached over __TRILIUM_PH_1__.
An audio file shows no visualizer and no waveform, unlike an audio __TRILIUM_PH_0__File__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note, since the site of the file does not generally let Trilium read its sound.
Pages that block automated fetches may produce a minimal preview (hostname only).
Link previews require the Trilium server to reach the target URL, so they won't generate previews for pages on networks the server can't see.

An external link is a standard web link targeting for example a website. For example, __TRILIUM_PH_0__https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_China_Sea__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is an external link to a Wikipedia page.
To create a link without a custom text:
Press __TRILIUM_PH_0__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_2__, or press __TRILIUM_PH_3__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_4__+__TRILIUM_PH_5__K__TRILIUM_PH_6__:

Since v0.107.0, the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add link__TRILIUM_PH_1__ dialog opens on __TRILIUM_PH_2__Web page__TRILIUM_PH_3__, in a popup next to the cursor on desktop. Type or paste the address, and optionally a __TRILIUM_PH_4__Link title__TRILIUM_PH_5__; without one, the link shows its address. The __TRILIUM_PH_6__ __TRILIUM_PH_7__Paste__TRILIUM_PH_8__ button at the end of the address field replaces its text with the text on the clipboard. This button is shown only where Trilium can read the clipboard: in the desktop app, and in a browser over HTTPS unless access to the clipboard was blocked.

When you leave the address field, or paste with the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Paste__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button, an empty __TRILIUM_PH_2__Link title__TRILIUM_PH_3__ is filled with the title of the web page; a spinner at its end shows while it loads. A title you type is kept. To turn this off, go to __TRILIUM_PH_4__Options__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Text Notes__TRILIUM_PH_7__ and turn off __TRILIUM_PH_8__Automatically retrieve titles for text links__TRILIUM_PH_9__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_10__Features__TRILIUM_PH_11__ section.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Display as__TRILIUM_PH_1__ inserts the address as __TRILIUM_PH_2__Text__TRILIUM_PH_3__, or as one of the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Link Previews__TRILIUM_PH_5__: __TRILIUM_PH_6__Icon & text__TRILIUM_PH_7__, __TRILIUM_PH_8__Card__TRILIUM_PH_9__ or, for a YouTube video or the address of an audio or video file, __TRILIUM_PH_10__Embed__TRILIUM_PH_11__.

Alternatively, use __TRILIUM_PH_0__Slash Commands__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and choose __TRILIUM_PH_2__Link to a web page__TRILIUM_PH_3__, which opens the same dialog. __TRILIUM_PH_4__Link to a web page (with icon)__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and __TRILIUM_PH_6__Link to a web page (as a card)__TRILIUM_PH_7__ open it with that display already picked.
A simpler way is to paste the raw link and press space to turn it automatically into a link.

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button and __TRILIUM_PH_1__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_2__+__TRILIUM_PH_3__L__TRILIUM_PH_4__ of __TRILIUM_PH_5__Internal (reference) links__TRILIUM_PH_6__ open the same dialog on __TRILIUM_PH_7__Note__TRILIUM_PH_8__. Select __TRILIUM_PH_9__Web page__TRILIUM_PH_10__ at the top of the dialog to create an external link from there.

An address without a scheme, such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__, gets __TRILIUM_PH_1__. The dialog does not insert an address that is not a valid URL, or a __TRILIUM_PH_2__, __TRILIUM_PH_3__ or __TRILIUM_PH_4__ link, since those can run code, and shows the reason under the address field. A URL pasted into the __TRILIUM_PH_5__Note__TRILIUM_PH_6__ field, or picked from its search, switches the dialog to __TRILIUM_PH_7__Web page__TRILIUM_PH_8__. The dialog also opens on __TRILIUM_PH_9__Web page__TRILIUM_PH_10__ when the selected text is a URL.
To create a link with a custom text:
First, type and select the text which will be turned into a link.

Open the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add link__TRILIUM_PH_1__ dialog as above (via the formatting toolbar, or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_3__+__TRILIUM_PH_4__K__TRILIUM_PH_5__). The selected text becomes the text of the link, so the dialog does not offer __TRILIUM_PH_6__Display as__TRILIUM_PH_7__.
Alternatively, simply paste (__TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__V__TRILIUM_PH_3__) over the selected text to turn it into a link.
The text inside the link can be changed if needed but the link itself will remain.

To modify the link, click on the link to display the popup and press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Edit link__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button. It opens the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Edit link__TRILIUM_PH_4__ dialog, filled with the link's address and text, as do placing the cursor inside the link and pressing __TRILIUM_PH_5__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_6__+__TRILIUM_PH_7__K__TRILIUM_PH_8__, __TRILIUM_PH_9__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_10__+__TRILIUM_PH_11__L__TRILIUM_PH_12__ or one of the link buttons. __TRILIUM_PH_13__Save link__TRILIUM_PH_14__ changes the whole link, its text included, and the dialog can also turn it into a link to a note.

To remove a link, click on it, open the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__More actions__TRILIUM_PH_2__ menu at the end of the popup and choose __TRILIUM_PH_3__ __TRILIUM_PH_4__Unlink__TRILIUM_PH_5__. The text stays, without the link.

The same menu has __TRILIUM_PH_0__Open link__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Edit link__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Copy address (URL)__TRILIUM_PH_5__, and __TRILIUM_PH_6__Display as__TRILIUM_PH_7__, which turns the link into one of the __TRILIUM_PH_8__Link Previews__TRILIUM_PH_9__, as does the __TRILIUM_PH_10__Display__TRILIUM_PH_11__ menu of the popup.
Right-clicking a link opens the same menu.

To follow an external link in a note being edited, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+click or double-click it, which opens it in a new tab or window, place the cursor in it and press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_3__+__TRILIUM_PH_4__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_5__, or right-click it and choose __TRILIUM_PH_6__Open link__TRILIUM_PH_7__. On a touch device, touch and hold the link, then choose __TRILIUM_PH_8__Open link__TRILIUM_PH_9__. A link in an __TRILIUM_PH_10__included note__TRILIUM_PH_11__ that is not __TRILIUM_PH_12__Editable__TRILIUM_PH_13__ opens on a click, as in a read-only note.
Internal links are links to other notes within Trilium.
You can open an internal link by clicking it. You can also see a read-only preview of an internal link's contents by hovering over it.
Since v0.107.0, clicking an internal link while editing a text note shows its popup instead, as clicking an external link does:

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Open note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ opens the linked note, or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Open attachment__TRILIUM_PH_3__ for a link to an attachment. A link into the same note reads __TRILIUM_PH_4__Jump to heading__TRILIUM_PH_5__, __TRILIUM_PH_6__Jump to block__TRILIUM_PH_7__ or __TRILIUM_PH_8__Jump to anchor__TRILIUM_PH_9__ instead, and scrolls to it without leaving the note.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Download__TRILIUM_PH_2__, for a link to an attachment, downloads the attachment.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Edit link__TRILIUM_PH_2__ changes the link, as described below.

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__More actions__TRILIUM_PH_2__ menu, with __TRILIUM_PH_3__ __TRILIUM_PH_4__Open note__TRILIUM_PH_5__ first, which does what the first button does, then __TRILIUM_PH_6__ __TRILIUM_PH_7__Open note in a new tab__TRILIUM_PH_8__, __TRILIUM_PH_9__ __TRILIUM_PH_10__Open note in a new split__TRILIUM_PH_11__, __TRILIUM_PH_12__ __TRILIUM_PH_13__Open note in a new window__TRILIUM_PH_14__ and __TRILIUM_PH_15__ __TRILIUM_PH_16__Quick edit__TRILIUM_PH_17__, then __TRILIUM_PH_18__Edit link__TRILIUM_PH_19__ and __TRILIUM_PH_20__ __TRILIUM_PH_21__Unlink__TRILIUM_PH_22__, which turns the link into plain text. A link that shows the title of the note ends with __TRILIUM_PH_23__Convert link to an included note__TRILIUM_PH_24__, described in __TRILIUM_PH_25__Include Note__TRILIUM_PH_26__. A link to an attachment lists the actions on the attachment between __TRILIUM_PH_27__Edit link__TRILIUM_PH_28__ and __TRILIUM_PH_29__Unlink__TRILIUM_PH_30__, except __TRILIUM_PH_31__ __TRILIUM_PH_32__Delete attachment...__TRILIUM_PH_33__, which follows __TRILIUM_PH_34__Unlink__TRILIUM_PH_35__, and ends with converting the attachment into a note. A link to blocks of the same note leaves out the ways to open the note elsewhere.
In a note being edited, right-clicking a link also opens this menu.

To follow the link without the popup, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+click or double-click it, which does what the first button of the popup does, or place the cursor in it and press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_3__+__TRILIUM_PH_4__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_5__. On a touch device, touch and hold the link, then choose the first entry of its menu, such as __TRILIUM_PH_6__Open note__TRILIUM_PH_7__ or __TRILIUM_PH_8__Jump to heading__TRILIUM_PH_9__. To open the note in a new tab, click it with the middle mouse button. The preview does not show while the popup is open.
A link in an __TRILIUM_PH_0__included note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ that is not __TRILIUM_PH_2__Editable__TRILIUM_PH_3__ opens on a click, as in a read-only note.
Internal links can be created at the current position in a text note by:

Pressing __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ + __TRILIUM_PH_2__L__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or the __TRILIUM_PH_4__ button underneath the __TRILIUM_PH_5__ menu in the __TRILIUM_PH_6__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_7__, or by choosing __TRILIUM_PH_8__Link to a note (internal link)__TRILIUM_PH_9__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_10__Slash Commands__TRILIUM_PH_11__. On desktop, the __TRILIUM_PH_12__Add link__TRILIUM_PH_13__ dialog opens in a popup next to the cursor.

Searching for the title of the desired note to link. It's also possible to create new notes from this dialog by typing a non-existing note title and selecting either __TRILIUM_PH_0__Create note__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which places it in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note Inbox__TRILIUM_PH_3__ (today's day note, or the top level, when no inbox is set), or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Create child note__TRILIUM_PH_5__, which places it under the note being edited.
There are two link types, depending on the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Link title__TRILIUM_PH_1__ field of the dialog:
When the link title is not set, the link will display the title of the note. If the title of the note gets changed, the link will be renamed automatically to the new name.
This is sometimes also called "reference link".
The icon of the linked note will also be displayed.

If the linked note is deleted, the link keeps the last title it showed, in red and with a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ icon instead of the note icon. Clicking it while editing opens the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Fix link__TRILIUM_PH_2__ dialog, which searches for that title; picking a note, or creating a new one, replaces the link with one to that note.
When a link title is typed, the link shows that text instead.
This will create a traditional hyperlink, where the text of the link can be different from the note title.

Since v0.107.0, to change a link, click it and press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Edit link__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button in its popup. For a link with a title of its own, placing the cursor inside it and pressing __TRILIUM_PH_3__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_4__ + __TRILIUM_PH_5__L__TRILIUM_PH_6__ or the __TRILIUM_PH_7__ button works too. The __TRILIUM_PH_8__Edit link__TRILIUM_PH_9__ dialog opens on the linked note, with its anchor and, for a link with a title of its own, the link's text; __TRILIUM_PH_10__Save link__TRILIUM_PH_11__ changes the whole link. Emptying the __TRILIUM_PH_12__Link title__TRILIUM_PH_13__ there turns the link into one that displays the title of the note, and typing one gives it a title of its own. For a link to an attachment, the dialog shows only the __TRILIUM_PH_14__Link title__TRILIUM_PH_15__, and emptying it makes the link display the title of the attachment.
You can also insert internal links “inline” by using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ symbol:
Type __TRILIUM_PH_0__ in a text note, which will open the note search menu.

Search for the desired note's title by typing a few characters. Use __TRILIUM_PH_0__Up__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Down__TRILIUM_PH_3__ to select the correct note, and press __TRILIUM_PH_4__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_5__ or __TRILIUM_PH_6__Tab__TRILIUM_PH_7__ to create the link. units.source: Each entry names the note the reference comes from, followed by one of:

In the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Connections tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Right Sidebar__TRILIUM_PH_3__, as a dedicated section.

Slash commands is a feature of __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes which allows easily accessing commonly used commands simply by using the keyboard, without having to remember dedicated __TRILIUM_PH_2__Keyboard Shortcuts__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

As the name suggests, to trigger the slash commands simply press the / key to trigger it. Note that this can be anywhere in a paragraph as long as it's not part of the word, if it doesn't show up simply press a space and press the / key again.
Use ↑ and ↓ keys to navigate between options.
By default, the full list of commands is displayed.
To search, simply start typing: commands are found by their title or by other names they go by (for example __TRILIUM_PH_0__ for __TRILIUM_PH_1__Heading 2__TRILIUM_PH_2__).
To trigger the highlighted action, press Enter or Tab.

With the fixed __TRILIUM_PH_0__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the block handle beside an empty paragraph turns into a __TRILIUM_PH_2__ button. Clicking it opens the commands that insert content or turn the paragraph into another block, such as a heading, a list, a table or a link, as a menu, with a box at its top that finds them by their title, their description or the other names they go by. The commands that only change the paragraph, such as alignment or indentation, are left out of that menu.

The menu of the block handle, described in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_1__, starts with __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert above__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Insert below__TRILIUM_PH_5__, which list the same commands and add the one picked in a new paragraph above or below the block. Beside a list item, items that add an empty list item take their place.

units.context: Slash Commands > Integration with other features

units.source: Apart from the common set of commands, some features are specially integrated with the slash commands:
units.context: Slash Commands > Integration with other features

units.source: For __TRILIUM_PH_0__admonitions__TRILIUM_PH_1__, each admonition type (e.g. note, tip) will be individually displayed.
units.context: Slash Commands > Integration with other features

units.source: Every __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text Snippets__TRILIUM_PH_1__ will also appear individually, making it easy to insert them.
units.context: Slash Commands > Integration with other features

units.source: For __TRILIUM_PH_0__links__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Link to a web page__TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__Link to a note (internal link)__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and __TRILIUM_PH_6__Link to a heading or anchor__TRILIUM_PH_7__ open the __TRILIUM_PH_8__Add link__TRILIUM_PH_9__ dialog on the matching page. __TRILIUM_PH_10__Link to a web page (with icon)__TRILIUM_PH_11__ and __TRILIUM_PH_12__Link to a web page (as a card)__TRILIUM_PH_13__ also pick how the web link is displayed, as described in __TRILIUM_PH_14__Link Previews__TRILIUM_PH_15__.
units.context: Slash Commands > Integration with other features

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__In-editor AI assistant__TRILIUM_PH_1__: dedicated __TRILIUM_PH_2__Ask AI__TRILIUM_PH_3__ item as well as all the predefined and __TRILIUM_PH_4__custom quick actions__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
units.context: Slash Commands > Integration with other features
Slash Commands > Integration with other features

units.source: Sorting the selection is experimental, and it changes as it matures. To use it, turn on __TRILIUM_PH_0__Sort selection in text editor__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in __TRILIUM_PH_2__Options__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Advanced__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Experimental Options__TRILIUM_PH_7__.
Trilium can sort the items of a list, a group of paragraphs or the rows of a table in a text note, comparing numbers, dates and times by their value.

To sort, place the cursor in a list or a table, or select the paragraphs to sort, then press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Sort__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button of the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_4__ to sort in ascending order. The arrow beside it offers __TRILIUM_PH_5__Ascending__TRILIUM_PH_6__ and __TRILIUM_PH_7__Descending__TRILIUM_PH_8__. With the floating toolbar, the button is in the block-level popup.

When the selection covers several paragraphs, list items or table cells, the same choices are also in a submenu of the menu of the block handle (the sequence of dots to the left of the block), just above __TRILIUM_PH_0__Delete__TRILIUM_PH_1__, and in the right-click menu of the selection. The submenu is named after what it sorts: __TRILIUM_PH_2__Sort blocks__TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__Sort list items__TRILIUM_PH_5__ or __TRILIUM_PH_6__Sort rows__TRILIUM_PH_7__.
On the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Mobile Frontend__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the button is in the main row of the toolbar and in the row of the __TRILIUM_PH_2__List ›__TRILIUM_PH_3__ button.
A sort can be undone with __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Z__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__List items__TRILIUM_PH_1__: with the cursor in a list, the items at its level are sorted. Nested items move with the item they belong to and keep their own order. To sort only some of the items, select them.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Paragraphs and other blocks__TRILIUM_PH_1__: select two or more paragraphs, headings, quotes, collapsible blocks or images. Each block is sorted by its first text: a collapsible block by its title, a quote by its first paragraph and an image by its caption. A selection that mixes a list with other blocks cannot be sorted.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Table rows__TRILIUM_PH_1__: the rows are sorted by the column of the cursor, as described in __TRILIUM_PH_2__Sorting rows__TRILIUM_PH_3__ in __TRILIUM_PH_4__Tables__TRILIUM_PH_5__. Inside a table cell, a list or several selected paragraphs are sorted instead of the rows.
Values are compared the same way as table rows, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__How values are compared__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in __TRILIUM_PH_2__Tables__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

The lines of a code block, or of a paragraph split with __TRILIUM_PH_0__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_3__, are not sorted one by one. A __TRILIUM_PH_4__Code__TRILIUM_PH_5__ note can sort its lines, see __TRILIUM_PH_6__Transforming text__TRILIUM_PH_7__ there.

Trilium supports spell checking for your notes. How it works depends on whether you're using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__desktop application__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (Electron) or accessing Trilium through a __TRILIUM_PH_2__web browser__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
The desktop app uses Chromium's built-in spellchecker. You can configure it from __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Spell Check__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

units.context: Spell Check > Desktop > Enabling spell check

units.source: Toggle __TRILIUM_PH_0__Check spelling__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to enable or disable the spellchecker. A restart is required for changes to take effect — use the restart button at the bottom of the section.
units.context: Spell Check > Desktop > Enabling spell check

units.source: When spell check is enabled, a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Spell Check Languages__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section appears listing all languages available on your system. Select one or more languages by checking the boxes. The spellchecker will accept words that are valid in __TRILIUM_PH_2__any__TRILIUM_PH_3__ of the selected languages.

The available languages depend on your operating system's installed language packs. For example, on Windows you can add languages through __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Time & Language__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Language & Region__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Add a language__TRILIUM_PH_7__.
The changes take effect only after restarting the application.
This function is available starting with Trilium v0.103.0.

Words you add to the dictionary (e.g. via the right-click context menu → "Add to dictionary") are stored in a __TRILIUM_PH_0__synced note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ inside Trilium. This means your custom dictionary automatically syncs across all your devices.

You can view and edit the dictionary directly from __TRILIUM_PH_0__Settings__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Spell Check__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Custom Dictionary__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Edit dictionary__TRILIUM_PH_7__. This opens the underlying note, which contains one word per line. You can add, remove, or modify entries as you like.
Changes to the custom dictionary (whether from the editor or the context menu) take effect after restarting the application.

units.context: Spell Check > Desktop > Custom dictionary > How the custom dictionary works

units.source: When you right-click a misspelled word and choose "Add to dictionary", the word is saved both to Electron's local spellchecker and to the synced dictionary note.
units.context: Spell Check > Desktop > Custom dictionary > How the custom dictionary works

units.source: On startup, Trilium loads all words from the dictionary note into the spellchecker session.
units.context: Spell Check > Desktop > Custom dictionary > How the custom dictionary works

units.source: If Trilium detects words in Electron's local dictionary but the dictionary note is empty (e.g. on first use), it performs a __TRILIUM_PH_0__one-time import__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of those words into the note.
units.context: Spell Check > Desktop > Custom dictionary > How the custom dictionary works

units.source: Words that are in Electron's local dictionary but __TRILIUM_PH_0__not__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in the note (e.g. you removed them manually) are cleaned up from the local dictionary on startup.
units.context: Spell Check > Desktop > Custom dictionary > How the custom dictionary works
Spell Check > Desktop > Custom dictionary > Known limitations

units.source: On Windows and macOS, Electron delegates "Add to dictionary" to the operating system's user dictionary. This means:
units.context: Spell Check > Desktop > Custom dictionary > Known limitations

units.source: Words added via the context menu are also written to the OS-level dictionary (e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_0__ on Windows).
units.context: Spell Check > Desktop > Custom dictionary > Known limitations

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Removing a word__TRILIUM_PH_1__ from the Trilium dictionary note prevents it from being loaded into the spellchecker on next startup, but does __TRILIUM_PH_2__not__TRILIUM_PH_3__ remove it from the OS dictionary. The word may still be accepted by the OS spellchecker until you remove it from the OS dictionary manually.
units.context: Spell Check > Desktop > Custom dictionary > Known limitations

units.source: When accessing Trilium through a web browser, spell checking is handled entirely by the browser itself. Trilium does not control the browser's spellchecker — language selection, dictionaries, and all other settings are managed through your browser's preferences.

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note contextual menu__TRILIUM_PH_1__ has a special behavior in which a right-clicked word (without selection) shows the browser's default contextual menu which allows the spellcheck to function.
The Spell Check settings page in Trilium will indicate that these options apply only to desktop builds.
Do I need to restart after every change?__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Spell Check > Frequently asked questions > Do I need to restart after every change?

units.source: Yes. Spell check language selection and the custom dictionary are loaded once at startup. Any changes require a restart to take effect.
units.context: Spell Check > Frequently asked questions > Do I need to restart after every change?

units.source: Can I use multiple spell check languages at the same time?__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Spell Check > Frequently asked questions > Can I use multiple spell check languages at the same time?

units.source: Yes. Select as many languages as you need from the checklist. The spellchecker will accept words from any of the selected languages.
units.context: Spell Check > Frequently asked questions > Can I use multiple spell check languages at the same time?

units.source: My custom words disappeared after syncing to a new device — what happened?__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Spell Check > Frequently asked questions > My custom words disappeared after syncing to a new device — what happened?

units.source: On the first launch of a new device, Trilium may import existing local dictionary words into the note. If the note already has words from another device (via sync), those are preserved. Make sure sync completes before restarting the application on a new device.
units.context: Spell Check > Frequently asked questions > My custom words disappeared after syncing to a new device — what happened?

units.source: I removed a word from the dictionary note but it's still accepted__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Spell Check > Frequently asked questions > I removed a word from the dictionary note but it's still accepted

units.source: This is likely due to the OS-level dictionary retaining the word (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Known limitations__TRILIUM_PH_1__ above). You can manually remove it from your operating system's user dictionary.
units.context: Spell Check > Frequently asked questions > I removed a word from the dictionary note but it's still accepted

units.source: This page has been relocated to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Outline tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Tables are a powerful feature for __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes, since editing them is generally easy.
To create a table, simply press the table button and select with the mouse the desired amount of columns and rows, as indicated in the adjacent figure.
Since v0.107.0, the same menu starts with an __TRILIUM_PH_0__Insert table…__TRILIUM_PH_1__ item, for a table larger than the grid or to type its size instead:
Click the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button and select __TRILIUM_PH_1__Insert table…__TRILIUM_PH_2__. A small form opens at the cursor.

Enter the number of __TRILIUM_PH_0__Columns__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (up to 100) and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Rows__TRILIUM_PH_3__ (up to 1000). The table can have at most 5000 cells in total, for example 1000 rows of 5 columns.

Optionally, turn on __TRILIUM_PH_0__Use headers__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and enter the number of __TRILIUM_PH_2__Header columns__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Header rows__TRILIUM_PH_5__. A table cannot have more header columns or rows than it has columns or rows.

To close the form without inserting a table, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or click outside it. From the keyboard, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Tab__TRILIUM_PH_3__ moves between __TRILIUM_PH_4__Insert table…__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and the grid while the menu is open.

On the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Mobile Frontend__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the table is inserted from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ button of the formatting toolbar: its __TRILIUM_PH_3__Insert table__TRILIUM_PH_4__ tile lists common sizes, from 2 × 2 to 3 × 4 (rows × columns). Tap one to insert a table of that size; to make it larger, insert rows and columns afterwards.
When a table is selected, a special formatting toolbar will appear:

On the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Mobile Frontend__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the toolbar does not float over the table. Instead, press the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ button after __TRILIUM_PH_3__Undo__TRILIUM_PH_4__ and __TRILIUM_PH_5__Redo__TRILIUM_PH_6__ in the formatting toolbar at the bottom of the screen to show the table's toolbar there.
Since v0.106.0, right-clicking anywhere inside a table opens a context menu with the most common table operations:

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Insert row above__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert row below__TRILIUM_PH_3__ insert a blank row next to the row of the current cell. When the selection spans multiple rows, the same number of rows is inserted.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Insert column to the left__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert column to the right__TRILIUM_PH_3__ work the same way for columns.

Since v0.107.0, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Set as header__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Set header up to this row__TRILIUM_PH_3__, depending on the selection, turns rows into header rows, which always start at the top of the table:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Set as header__TRILIUM_PH_1__ shows when the selection starts at the first row, and makes every selected row a header row.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Set header up to this row__TRILIUM_PH_1__ shows when the selection is in a single row below the first, and makes that row and every row above it header rows.
Neither shows when the selection spans several rows below the first.

A check mark shows that the rows are already header rows. Choosing the item again turns them, and every header row below them, back into regular rows. For example, in a table with five header rows, choosing __TRILIUM_PH_0__Set header up to this row__TRILIUM_PH_1__ on the third row leaves only the first two as header rows.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Merge cells__TRILIUM_PH_1__ merges the selected cells into one. The selected cells must form a rectangle.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Split cell__TRILIUM_PH_1__ splits each selected cell in two, either __TRILIUM_PH_2__Vertically__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Horizontally__TRILIUM_PH_5__. __TRILIUM_PH_6__Unmerge cells__TRILIUM_PH_7__, in the same submenu, turns each merged cell in the selection back into the single cells it covers, keeping its content in the top-left one; cells that are not merged stay as they are.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Distribute columns evenly__TRILIUM_PH_1__ splits the combined width of the columns the selection touches equally between them. The other columns and the width of the table stay as they are. It needs a selection spanning at least two columns; a merged cell counts for every column it covers.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Cut__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Copy__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Copy as Markdown__TRILIUM_PH_5__ act on the selected cells. Since v0.107.0, __TRILIUM_PH_6__Copy__TRILIUM_PH_7__ and __TRILIUM_PH_8__Paste__TRILIUM_PH_9__ open submenus with their variants, such as __TRILIUM_PH_10__Copy as Markdown__TRILIUM_PH_11__ and __TRILIUM_PH_12__Paste as plain text__TRILIUM_PH_13__; clicking __TRILIUM_PH_14__Copy__TRILIUM_PH_15__ or __TRILIUM_PH_16__Paste__TRILIUM_PH_17__ itself still copies or pastes:

Cutting or copying produces a smaller table holding just the selected cells. Pasting it over a cell selection replaces those cells; pasting elsewhere inserts it as a table of its own. Cutting clears the cells without removing rows or columns.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Copy as Markdown__TRILIUM_PH_1__ converts the selected cells to a Markdown table. A selected header row becomes the Markdown header; without one, an empty header row is emitted, since Markdown tables require one.

Since v0.107.0, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Paste rows above__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Paste rows below__TRILIUM_PH_3__, in the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Paste__TRILIUM_PH_5__ submenu, paste the clipboard as new rows next to the row of the current cell, instead of over the cells from the cursor on. They show only when the selection is in a single row, and, like __TRILIUM_PH_6__Paste__TRILIUM_PH_7__, only where the clipboard can be read:

A copied table becomes one new row for each of its rows, filled from the first column. When it has more columns than the table, the table gains columns, as with a regular paste. Other content goes in the first cell of a single new row.
The new rows are selected afterwards.
When merged cells join the row to others, the new rows go above or below that whole block of rows.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Sort__TRILIUM_PH_1__, below the clipboard section, sorts the rows by the column of the current cell, in __TRILIUM_PH_2__Ascending__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Descending__TRILIUM_PH_5__ order. See __TRILIUM_PH_6__Sorting rows__TRILIUM_PH_7__.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Delete row__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Delete column__TRILIUM_PH_3__, below __TRILIUM_PH_4__Sort__TRILIUM_PH_5__, remove every row or column the selection touches, even when only some of their cells are selected.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Delete table__TRILIUM_PH_1__ removes the whole table and leaves an empty paragraph in its place. In a table nested inside another, only the inner table is removed.

Since v0.107.0, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Select__TRILIUM_PH_1__, below __TRILIUM_PH_2__Delete table__TRILIUM_PH_3__, selects the cells of every row (__TRILIUM_PH_4__Row__TRILIUM_PH_5__) or column (__TRILIUM_PH_6__Column__TRILIUM_PH_7__) the selection touches, or every cell of the table (__TRILIUM_PH_8__Table__TRILIUM_PH_9__). Unlike the __TRILIUM_PH_10__ button, which selects the table as a whole, __TRILIUM_PH_11__Table__TRILIUM_PH_12__ selects its cells, so cell operations such as __TRILIUM_PH_13__Merge cells__TRILIUM_PH_14__ apply to all of them. In a table nested inside another, __TRILIUM_PH_15__Table__TRILIUM_PH_16__ selects only the cells of the inner table.
Right-clicking a cell that is not part of the current selection moves the cursor there first, so the menu always applies to the cell under the pointer.

In the browser, Trilium's menu replaces the browser's own context menu inside tables. To reach the browser's menu (for example for its spell checking suggestions), hold __TRILIUM_PH_0__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_1__ while right-clicking. The desktop application is unaffected, since its menu already includes the spelling suggestions. In the browser, the menu also offers __TRILIUM_PH_2__Paste__TRILIUM_PH_3__ only when the page can read the clipboard, which requires a secure (HTTPS) context and your permission; otherwise, paste with __TRILIUM_PH_4__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_5__+__TRILIUM_PH_6__V__TRILIUM_PH_7__.
Click on a cell to focus it.
Click the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button at the top or the bottom of a table to insert an empty paragraph near it.
Click the __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1____TRILIUM_PH_2__ button at the top-left of the table to select it entirely (for easy copy-pasting or cutting) or drag and drop it to relocate the table.
Use the arrow keys on the keyboard to easily navigate between cells.
It's also possible to use __TRILIUM_PH_0__Tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to go to the next cell and Shift+Tab to go to the previous cell.
Unlike arrow keys, pressing __TRILIUM_PH_0__Tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__ at the end of the table (last row, last column) will create a new row automatically.
To select multiple cells, hold __TRILIUM_PH_0__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_1__ while using the arrow keys.
Since v0.107.0, touching a table outlines the cell with the cursor, or the selected cells, and shows a handle at each corner of the outline.

To select multiple cells, drag one of the handles across the table. The cell at the opposite corner stays selected, so the selection grows or shrinks as the finger moves. The note and wide tables scroll when the handle reaches the edge of the screen.
Columns can be resized by hovering the mouse over the border of two adjacent cells and dragging it.

To give several columns the same width, select cells across them and choose __TRILIUM_PH_0__Distribute columns evenly__TRILIUM_PH_1__ from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ button of the formatting toolbar or from the __TRILIUM_PH_3__context menu__TRILIUM_PH_4__.
By default, the row height is not adjustable using the mouse, but it can be configured from the cell settings (see below).
To adjust exactly the width (in pixels or percentages) of a cell, select the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button.

units.context: Tables > Resizing cells > Resizing with touch

units.source: Since v0.107.0, touching a table shows a bar at the bottom of the note, above the formatting toolbar on mobile. The bar has a segment for each column of the table, with a divider at the end of each column. Only the divider of the column with the cursor is a handle that resizes; the other dividers only mark where the columns meet, so a swipe across them scrolls instead. When several cells are selected, each column they cover has a handle.
units.context: Tables > Resizing cells > Resizing with touch

units.source: To resize a column, place the cursor in one of its cells or tap its segment, then drag its handle. The table grows or shrinks with the column, and scrolls when the handle reaches the edge of the screen. The column snaps to its starting width and to the widths of the columns beside it.
units.context: Tables > Resizing cells > Resizing with touch

units.source: To cancel a resize, drag the handle back to where it started, or touch the screen with a second finger.
units.context: Tables > Resizing cells > Resizing with touch

units.source: To give a column and the next one the same width, double-tap the handle between them.
units.context: Tables > Resizing cells > Resizing with touch

units.source: To select a column, tap its segment. To open the column menu, touch and hold the segment.
units.context: Tables > Resizing cells > Resizing with touch

units.source: To scroll a wide table sideways, swipe along the bar.
units.context: Tables > Resizing cells > Resizing with touch

units.source: A wide table scrolls a little past its end, so the handle of its last column stays away from the edge of the screen, where a swipe navigates back.
units.context: Tables > Resizing cells > Resizing with touch

units.source: Since v0.107.0, a table can be wider than the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Content width__TRILIUM_PH_1__. Such a table scrolls sideways, while the rest of the note keeps its width.

A new table is as wide as the content. To make it wider, drag the right border of its last column past the edge of the content. The border snaps to the edge and holds there briefly, so the table is easy to bring back to the width of the content.
To set an exact width, enter a percentage above __TRILIUM_PH_0__ or a width in pixels in the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ __TRILIUM_PH_2__table properties__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
A table whose content needs more room than the note, such as a pasted table with many columns, also scrolls instead of stretching the note.
Wide tables scroll the same way in read-only notes and on shared pages.
When printing or exporting to PDF, a wide table is shrunk to fit the page.
Tables inside other blocks, such as block quotes, admonitions, collapsible blocks, columns or tabs, are limited to the width of their block and do not scroll.

On the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Mobile Frontend__TRILIUM_PH_1__, a table keeps the width it has on a desktop and scrolls sideways, instead of squeezing its columns into the width of the screen. The full width of a table is the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Max content width__TRILIUM_PH_3__ set in __TRILIUM_PH_4__Options__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Appearance__TRILIUM_PH_7__ → __TRILIUM_PH_8__Content Width__TRILIUM_PH_9__ on the mobile device, 1200 pixels by default. For example, a table set to __TRILIUM_PH_10__ is 600 pixels wide.
To resize columns on mobile, use the bar described in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Resizing with touch__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

Since v0.107.0, the header rows of a table stay visible at the top of the note while you scroll through the rest of the table, and leave with the end of the table. This also works in read-only notes, on shared pages and in wide tables.

To turn rows into header rows, use __TRILIUM_PH_0__Set as header__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__context menu__TRILIUM_PH_3__, or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Header row__TRILIUM_PH_5__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_6__ button of the formatting toolbar.

To let header rows scroll away with the rest of the table, turn off __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Text Notes__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Features__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Use sticky header rows for tables__TRILIUM_PH_7__. The setting applies to the current device only, and shared pages keep their sticky header rows.

units.source: Since v0.106.0, rows and columns can be reordered with the keyboard:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Up__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_5__+__TRILIUM_PH_6__Down__TRILIUM_PH_7__ move the rows touched by the selection up or down.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Left__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_5__+__TRILIUM_PH_6__Right__TRILIUM_PH_7__ move the columns touched by the selection left or right.
Merged cells are never split by a move. The rows or columns held together by a merged cell travel as one block, and moving toward such a block jumps over it entirely.
When the table has a header row, a header row moved below the header area becomes a regular row, and a regular row moved into the header area becomes a header row. Header columns behave the same way.

Outside of tables, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Left__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_5__+__TRILIUM_PH_6__Right__TRILIUM_PH_7__ keep navigating the note history, and __TRILIUM_PH_8__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_9__+__TRILIUM_PH_10__Up__TRILIUM_PH_11__ and __TRILIUM_PH_12__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_13__+__TRILIUM_PH_14__Down__TRILIUM_PH_15__ keep moving the current paragraph.
Since v0.107.0, the rows of a table can be sorted by the values of one column:

To sort all the rows, place the cursor in any cell of the column to sort by, then select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Sort__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Ascending__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Descending__TRILIUM_PH_5__ from the __TRILIUM_PH_6__context menu__TRILIUM_PH_7__. The same items are in the __TRILIUM_PH_8__ button of the formatting toolbar.
To sort only some of the rows, select their cells in the column to sort by, then sort the same way. Sorting is not available while the selection spans more than one column.
Header rows always stay at the top of the table and are never sorted. A sort can be undone with __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Z__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

units.source: A number can start with a currency symbol, such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__, __TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__. A cell that starts with letters, such as __TRILIUM_PH_5__, is text.
units.context: Tables > Sorting rows > How values are compared

units.source: The decimal separator follows the language of the note: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ is one and a half in English, but one thousand five hundred in German. A comma or period that is not followed by exactly three digits is always read as a decimal separator, so __TRILIUM_PH_1__ is one and a half in either language.

units.source: Rows joined by a merged cell are kept together and move as one block. The block is sorted by the value in its first row. When the block has more than one cell in the sorted column, the other cells do not affect the order, and a message says so: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Some rows were sorted together because merged cells tie them to each other__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
When the selection covers only part of such a block, the whole block is sorted.
To merge two or more cells together, simply select them via drag & drop and press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button from the formatting toolbar.
More options are available by pressing the arrow next to it:
Click on a single cell and select Merge cell up/down/right/left to merge with an adjacent cell.
Select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Merge selected cells__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to merge the selected cells, the same as pressing the button itself.
Select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Split cell vertically__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__horizontally__TRILIUM_PH_3__, to split a cell into multiple cells (can also be used to undo a merge).
Select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Unmerge cells__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to turn each merged cell in the selection back into the single cells it covers, keeping its content in the top-left one.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Merge selected cells__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Unmerge cells__TRILIUM_PH_3__ are available since v0.107.0. Merging and splitting are also available by right-clicking the selected cells, via the __TRILIUM_PH_4__context menu__TRILIUM_PH_5__, where __TRILIUM_PH_6__Unmerge cells__TRILIUM_PH_7__ is in the __TRILIUM_PH_8__Split cell__TRILIUM_PH_9__ submenu.
The table properties can be accessed via the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button and allows for the following adjustments:
Border (not the border of the cells, but the outer rim of the table), which includes the style (single, double), color and width.
The background color, with none set by default.
The width and height of the table in percentage (must end with __TRILIUM_PH_0__) or pixels (must end with __TRILIUM_PH_1__).
Left or right-aligned, case in which the text will flow next to it.
Centered, case in which text will avoid the table, regardless of the table width.
The table will immediately update to reflect the changes, but the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Save__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button must be pressed for the changes to persist.
Similarly to table properties, the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button opens a popup which adjusts the styling of one or more cells (based on the user's selection).
The following options can be adjusted:
The border style, color and width (same as table properties), but applying to the current cell only.
The background color, with none set by default.
The width and height of the cell in percentage (must end with __TRILIUM_PH_0__) or pixels (must end with __TRILIUM_PH_1__).
The padding (the distance of the text compared to the cell's borders).
The alignment of the text, both horizontally (left, centered, right, justified) and vertically (top, middle or bottom).
In a centered or right-aligned cell, each item of a bulleted, numbered or to-do list moves together with its bullet, number or checkbox.
The cell will immediately update to reflect the changes, but the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Save__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button must be pressed for the changes to persist.

The border and background colors of tables and cells adapt to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__theme__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the same way as __TRILIUM_PH_2__text colors__TRILIUM_PH_3__ do. A color picked from the palette, chosen with the color picker or typed in is shown in a lighter or darker shade that suits the current theme, so borders stay visible and text stays readable on the background. The hue stays the same, and the table keeps the color as it was picked.
Colors applied with older versions of Trilium are shown exactly as they were picked, until the note is next edited.
Older browsers that can't adapt colors show them exactly as they were picked.

Header cells are shaded to suit the current theme. To change their background in every table, set the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ variable in a __TRILIUM_PH_1__custom theme__TRILIUM_PH_2__ or in __TRILIUM_PH_3__custom app-wide CSS__TRILIUM_PH_4__, for example __TRILIUM_PH_5__. A background picked for a cell still takes precedence.
Press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button to insert a caption or a text description of the table, which is going to be displayed above the table.
By default, tables come with a gray border that is lighter or darker to suit the current __TRILIUM_PH_0__theme__TRILIUM_PH_1__, so it stays discreet on a dark background.

To change the default border of every table, set the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ variable in a __TRILIUM_PH_1__custom theme__TRILIUM_PH_2__ or in __TRILIUM_PH_3__custom app-wide CSS__TRILIUM_PH_4__, for example __TRILIUM_PH_5__. Set it to __TRILIUM_PH_6__ to hide the borders of all the tables that don't have a border of their own.
To adjust the borders, follow these steps:
In the floating panel, select the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Table properties__TRILIUM_PH_1__ option (__TRILIUM_PH_2__).
Look for the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Border__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section at the top of the newly opened panel.
This will control the outer borders of the table.
Select a style for the border. Generally __TRILIUM_PH_0__Single__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is the desirable option.
Select a color for the border.
Select a width for the border, expressed in pixels.
Select all the cells of the table and then press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Cell properties__TRILIUM_PH_1__ option (__TRILIUM_PH_2__).
This will control the inner borders of the table, at cell level.
Note that it's possible to change the borders individually by selecting one or more cells, case in which it will only change the borders that intersect these cells.
Repeat the same steps as from step (2).

units.source: Since v0.104.1, tables can be indented as a block (the whole table moves, rather than just the content of a cell).
Click the __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1____TRILIUM_PH_2__ button to select the entire table. Otherwise, the indentation applies only to the current cell's content.

Simple tables are exported in GitHub-flavored Markdown format (e.g. a series of __TRILIUM_PH_0__ items). If the table is found to be more complex (it contains HTML elements, has custom sizes or images), the table is converted to a HTML one instead.
Generally formatting loss should be minimal when exported to Markdown due to the fallback to HTML formatting.

Text Snippets are closely related to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Templates__TRILIUM_PH_1__, but instead of defining the content of an entire note, text snippets are pieces of formatted text that can easily be inserted in a text note.

units.source: Once a snippet is created, there are two options to insert it:
From the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_1__, by looking for the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ button.
To look for a specific template, start typing the name of the template (its title).
To look for all the templates, type __TRILIUM_PH_0__.
A newly created snippet doesn't appear? Generally it takes up to a few seconds to refresh the list of templates once you make a change.
If this doesn't happen, __TRILIUM_PH_0__reload the application__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__report the issue__TRILIUM_PH_3__to us.

Whenever a snippet is created, deleted or its title/description are modified, all the open text notes will need to be refreshed. This causes a slight flash for usually under a second, but it can cause some discomfort.
Unlike __TRILIUM_PH_0__Templates__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the snippets cannot be limited to a particular __TRILIUM_PH_2__workspace__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

In Trilium, to-do items aren't limited to a simple "done" or "not done." Tasks can also be marked as __TRILIUM_PH_0__in progress__TRILIUM_PH_1__ ("doing"), __TRILIUM_PH_2__under consideration__TRILIUM_PH_3__ ("maybe"), or __TRILIUM_PH_4__cancelled__TRILIUM_PH_5__ ("won't do"), thus giving a more accurate picture of where things actually stand.

Right-click the checkbox and select the desired state. Alternatively, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_3__+__TRILIUM_PH_4__Enter __TRILIUM_PH_5__ to cycle through the task states. Tapping or left-clicking the checkbox, or pressing __TRILIUM_PH_6__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_7__+__TRILIUM_PH_8__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_9__ in the item, will always toggle between "None" and "Done". On the __TRILIUM_PH_10__Mobile Frontend__TRILIUM_PH_11__, the states are buttons in the row of the __TRILIUM_PH_12__List ›__TRILIUM_PH_13__ button, which shows while the cursor is in the list.
Task states are fully preserved when converting between __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Markdown__TRILIUM_PH_3__ notes, in both directions.

To-do lists are meant for small task lists. For more complicated, day-to-day task tracking consider using a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Kanban Board__TRILIUM_PH_1__ collection instead.
The default note type in Trilium, text notes allow for rich formatting, tables, images, admonitions and a handful of other features.
Most of the interaction with text notes is done via the built-in toolbars. Depending on preference, there are two different layouts:

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Floating toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is hidden by default and only appears when needed. In this mode there are actually two different toolbars:__TRILIUM_PH_2____TRILIUM_PH_3____TRILIUM_PH_4__
A toolbar that appears when text is selected. This provides text-level formatting such as bold, italic, text colors, inline code, etc.__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1____TRILIUM_PH_2____TRILIUM_PH_3__
Here's a list of various features supported by text notes:
Links to blocks of a note

Text notes are usually opened in edit mode. However, they may open in read-only mode if the note is too big or the note is explicitly marked as read-only. For more information, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Read-Only Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

There are numerous keyboard shortcuts to format the text without having to use the mouse. For a reference of all the key combinations, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Keyboard Shortcuts__TRILIUM_PH_1__. In addition, see __TRILIUM_PH_2__Markdown-like formatting__TRILIUM_PH_3__ as an alternative to the keyboard shortcuts.
For readability purposes on wider screens, the width of text notes is limited via a configurable option. See __TRILIUM_PH_0__Content width__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for more information.

Trilium supports creating "code" notes, i.e. notes which contain some sort of formal code - be it programming language (C++, JavaScript), structured data (JSON, XML) or other types of codes (CSS etc.).
This can be useful for a few things:
computer programmers can store code snippets as notes with syntax highlighting
JavaScript code notes can be executed inside Trilium for some extra functionality
we call such JavaScript code notes "scripts" – see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Scripting__TRILIUM_PH_1__
JSON, XML etc. can be used as storage for structured data (typically used in conjunction with scripting)
For shorter snippets of code that can be embedded in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes, see __TRILIUM_PH_2__Code blocks__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
In the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__, right-click a note and select __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert child note__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Insert note after__TRILIUM_PH_5__, then:

To create a code note in a given language, hover __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and select the language. The list shows the languages enabled in the options (see below), and ends with __TRILIUM_PH_2__Configure code notes...__TRILIUM_PH_3__, which opens them.

units.source: To change the selected lines or text, right-click the selection and open __TRILIUM_PH_0__Transform__TRILIUM_PH_1__. Its commands come in three groups:

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Sort ascending__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Sort descending__TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__Shuffle lines__TRILIUM_PH_5__, __TRILIUM_PH_6__Reverse line order__TRILIUM_PH_7__ and __TRILIUM_PH_8__Deduplicate lines__TRILIUM_PH_9__, which keeps the first copy of each line.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Trim leading__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Trim trailing__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Trim both__TRILIUM_PH_5__ remove the whitespace at the start, at the end or at both ends of each line. __TRILIUM_PH_6__Remove blank lines__TRILIUM_PH_7__ also removes the lines that hold only whitespace.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__To uppercase__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__To lowercase__TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__To sentence case__TRILIUM_PH_5__, __TRILIUM_PH_6__To title case__TRILIUM_PH_7__ and __TRILIUM_PH_8__Remove diacritics__TRILIUM_PH_9__.

The commands of the first two groups change every line that the selection touches, even partly. Those of the third group change only the selected text. Each change is undone in one step with __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Z__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
Sorting reads numbers, dates and times by their value, as sorting a table does (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Tables__TRILIUM_PH_1__), and ignores the case of letters and the indentation. Blank lines go last.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__To sentence case__TRILIUM_PH_1__ lowercases the text and capitalizes the first word of each sentence and of each line. __TRILIUM_PH_2__To title case__TRILIUM_PH_3__ capitalizes every word except minor words such as "of" and "the", which stay lowercase unless they start or end a sentence.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Remove diacritics__TRILIUM_PH_1__ turns letters such as __TRILIUM_PH_2__, __TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__ into __TRILIUM_PH_5__, __TRILIUM_PH_6__ and __TRILIUM_PH_7__, and removes the vowel points of Hebrew and Arabic. Letters such as __TRILIUM_PH_8__ and __TRILIUM_PH_9__ stay as they are.

Sorting and the case changes follow the language set in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Language & Region__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Default content language__TRILIUM_PH_5__. In Turkish, for example, an uppercase __TRILIUM_PH_6__ is __TRILIUM_PH_7__.

A code note or a code file shown without its editor, such as in an __TRILIUM_PH_0__Include Note__TRILIUM_PH_1__, on the cards of __TRILIUM_PH_2__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or in a tooltip, uses the same colors and line numbers as the editor does. A printout uses the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Light theme__TRILIUM_PH_5__. A __TRILIUM_PH_6__shared page__TRILIUM_PH_7__ uses the VS Code light or dark theme, following the mode of the page.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Why are there only a few themes whereas the code block themes for text notes have a lot?__TRILIUM_PH_1____TRILIUM_PH_2__The reason is that Code notes use a different technology than the one used in Text notes, and as such there is a more limited selection of themes. If you find a CodeMirror 6 (not 5) theme that you would like to use, let us know and we might consider adding it to the set of default themes. There is no possibility of adding new themes (at least for now), since the themes are defined in JavaScript and not at CSS level.

If you see __TRILIUM_PH_0__ displayed as __TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__ as __TRILIUM_PH_3__ inside a code note, those are __TRILIUM_PH_4__font ligature__TRILIUM_PH_5__: the default monospace font draws certain character pairs as a single symbol. The underlying text is not changed by Trilium (unlike text notes which have __TRILIUM_PH_6__Automatic replacements__TRILIUM_PH_7__), and copying it out gives you back __TRILIUM_PH_8__ and __TRILIUM_PH_9__.
This can be turned off with __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1____TRILIUM_PH_2__→ Appearance → Fonts → Programming ligatures__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

Trilium allows you to save common searches as notes within the note tree. The search results will appear as sub-notes under these "saved search" notes. Here is an example of how it works:

A saved search runs when you open it, and when you expand it in the note tree. A saved search in a tab that is not shown, such as a background tab restored at startup, runs when you switch to that tab. Its results stay until you run the search again with the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button of the search parameters. If the query has an error, it appears as a notification.
In __TRILIUM_PH_0__Safe mode__TRILIUM_PH_1__, and when the request fails, the search does not run on its own. Press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Search now__TRILIUM_PH_3__ to run it.

Once a search is saved, the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search parameters__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is still available underneath the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Title__TRILIUM_PH_3__ in order to be able to change the settings later on but it will appear collapsed by default.

By default, saved searches are stored in the day note. However, you can designate a different note to store saved searches by marking it with the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ label. Additionally, for __TRILIUM_PH_1__workspaces__TRILIUM_PH_2__, you can use the __TRILIUM_PH_3__ label to specify a storage location for saved searches within that workspace.
Relation map is a type of note which visualizes notes and their __TRILIUM_PH_0__relations__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
To create a new note and add it to the map, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Add note__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button at the bottom of the map, then click anywhere on the map to place it there.

While the map waits for the click, a translucent box follows the mouse to show where the note will go. To cancel, press the button again (now labeled __TRILIUM_PH_0__Cancel__TRILIUM_PH_1__) or press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
The note is created as a child of the map, with the default title of a new note. It opens in the note panel (see below) with its title selected, so you can type its name straight away.
An existing note can also be dragged from the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__. It will be placed at the position it's dragged on.
Multiple notes can also be dragged via __TRILIUM_PH_0__Multiple selection__TRILIUM_PH_1__. The notes will be positioned near the dragged position without overlapping.
The dragged note can be a sub-child of the map, or it can be at any arbitrary position.

Notes can also be pasted onto the map. Copy or cut them in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__, then click the map and press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_3__+__TRILIUM_PH_4__V__TRILIUM_PH_5__, or right click an empty part of the map and select __TRILIUM_PH_6__Paste note(s)__TRILIUM_PH_7__.

With __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__V__TRILIUM_PH_3__, the notes are placed under the mouse, or in the middle of the map if the mouse is not over it. From the right click menu, they are placed where the menu was opened.
Copied notes stay where they are in the tree. Cut notes are moved under the map, as if they had been pasted into it in the tree.

Links to notes, such as an __TRILIUM_PH_0__Internal (reference) links__TRILIUM_PH_1__ copied from a text note, can be pasted the same way. If the clipboard holds no link to a note, the notes last copied or cut in the tree are pasted.
The right click menu of an empty part of the map also has __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add note__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which creates a new note where the menu was opened.
To create a relationship, hold the mouse on the dot on the right of a note and then:
Drag it over another note to create a relationship pointing from the first note to the second one.
Drag over the same note to create a self-referencing relationship (represented as a loop).

Once dragged, a popover next to the relationship asks for its name. Type a new name and press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_1__, or pick a relation name already in use from the suggestions. To cancel, press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_3__, close the popover or click elsewhere on the map.
Each note is shown as a card with its icon and title, colored in the note's color the same way as the cards of a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Kanban Board__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Hovering a note highlights its relationships, in the note's color if it has one, and fades the other relationships.
To view or edit a note, click it on the map. This opens the note panel (see below).

To open the note in a new tab instead, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+click it or click it with the middle mouse button. __TRILIUM_PH_2__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_3__+click opens it in a new window. The right click menu offers the same options.
To edit the title of a note, change its color or delete it (either from the map, or delete it completely), right click the note.
To rename or delete a relationship, right click it and select the corresponding option.

On a __TRILIUM_PH_0__read-only__TRILIUM_PH_1__ map, notes cannot be moved and relationships cannot be drawn, renamed or deleted. The right click menu of a note only offers to open it, and a relationship has no right click menu.

To move around the map, drag an empty part of it, and zoom with the mouse wheel or the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and __TRILIUM_PH_1__ buttons at the bottom-right corner. Clicking the zoom percentage goes back to 100%, and __TRILIUM_PH_2__ __TRILIUM_PH_3__Fit to view__TRILIUM_PH_4__ zooms and pans so that all the notes are visible.

Once the map has been clicked, the arrow keys or __TRILIUM_PH_0__W__TRILIUM_PH_1__ __TRILIUM_PH_2__A__TRILIUM_PH_3__ __TRILIUM_PH_4__S__TRILIUM_PH_5__ __TRILIUM_PH_6__D__TRILIUM_PH_7__ pan it, and __TRILIUM_PH_8__+__TRILIUM_PH_9__ and __TRILIUM_PH_10__-__TRILIUM_PH_11__ zoom it. The __TRILIUM_PH_12__?__TRILIUM_PH_13__ button at the top-right corner of the map lists all its keyboard shortcuts.

When a note on the map is clicked, a panel opens to the right of the map and the note is highlighted. If the panel would cover the note, or the note is partly off-screen, the map pans to bring it into view. The panel contains:
The title and icon of the note, both editable.
A __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button to expand the panel over the whole map, and to restore it afterwards.
Buttons to interact with the note:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ Open the note in the current tab, or, through the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ menu, in a new tab, split, window or the quick edit popup.
A __TRILIUM_PH_0__ color picker to change the color of the note.
A __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button to remove the note from the map, which can optionally delete the note as well.
The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of the note, if any.
The note's content, which can be edited directly from the panel.
The color picker and the remove button are not shown if the map is read-only.

Clicking another note on the map switches the panel to it. Similarly, clicking an __TRILIUM_PH_0__Internal (reference) links__TRILIUM_PH_1__ inside the panel switches the panel to that note, as long as it is on the map.
To close the panel, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button at its top-right, click an empty part of the map, or press __TRILIUM_PH_1__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_2__.
On mobile, the note opens as a dialog over the whole screen instead of a panel.

units.source: The mindmap allows for easy jotting down of ideas and storing them in a hierarchical fashion.

Right click the node to bring a contextual menu with options such as creating new nodes, focusing on a particular notes or creating links between them.
Use the buttons at the top-left to change the positioning of the nodes relative to the root node (to the left, to the right, or to both sides).

In the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note buttons__TRILIUM_PH_1__ area, an __TRILIUM_PH_2__image reference__TRILIUM_PH_3__ can be copied by pressing the __TRILIUM_PH_4__ button, to paste the mind map in a text note.

units.source: Since v0.102.0 it's possible to annotate PDFs. To do so, look for the annotation buttons on the right side of the PDF toolbar (__TRILIUM_PH_0__).

The following annotation methods are supported:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Highlight__TRILIUM_PH_1____TRILIUM_PH_2__Allows highlighting text with one of the predefined colors.

Although annotations are stored in the PDF itself, they can be edited. units.source: Trilium uses the built-in media decoding mechanism of the browser (or Electron/Chromium when running on the desktop). Starting with v0.103.0, a message will be displayed instead when a media format is not supported.
To play/pause, simply click anywhere on the media. For video files, the controls at the bottom will hide automatically after playing, simply move the mouse to show them again.
The bottom bar has the following features:
A track bar to seek across the media. Audio files up to 60 MB will display a waveform seekbar, to give a visual overview of the track's structure: silences, pauses, and louder segments.
On the left of the track bar, the current time is indicated.
On the right of the track bar, the remaining time is indicated.
On the left side there are buttons to:
Play mode (applies to all media from the parent note):
Play once — play the media until it ends, then stop.
Loop — replay the media automatically once it ends.
Play next — when the current item ends, continue with the next one in the same parent note until the last item finishes.
Rotate the video by 90 degrees (video only).
Previous media — jumps to the previous media: the nearest media note above the current one in the tree (within the same parent note) in the case of media notes, or the previous media attachment.
Next media — jumps to the next media: the nearest media note below the current one in the tree (within the same parent note) in the case of media notes, or the next media attachment.
Zoom to fill, which will crop the video so that it fills the entire window (video only).
Picture-in-picture, if the browser supports it (video only).

Microsoft Office formats: Word (__TRILIUM_PH_0__), Excel (__TRILIUM_PH_1__) and PowerPoint (__TRILIUM_PH_2__).
The OpenDocument alternatives to the previous formats (Text, Spreadsheet, Presentation), created by editors such as LibreOffice and OpenOffice.
Older Microsoft Office formats (__TRILIUM_PH_0__, __TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__) are not supported.
The document is converted to a simplified representation on the server and rendered as read-only content, similar to a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note.
Text formatting: bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, subscript/superscript, text and highlight colors, fonts and font sizes.
Tables, including merged cells and cell background colors.

To keep links readable regardless of the theme, the default hyperlink color applied automatically by word processors is ignored; links that were deliberately given a custom color by the author keep it.

The preview is read-only. To edit the document, download it or open it in an external application; the content of the note is not affected by the preview. Alternatively copy and paste it into a text note.
The preview is a simplified rendering: complex layouts (columns, text boxes, headers and footers), charts and the precise styling of table borders are not reproduced.
Documents larger than 20 MB are not previewed, to keep the server responsive. The usual download and open actions remain available.
If the document cannot be converted, a notice is displayed instead and the file can still be downloaded or opened externally.

units.source: The following note types are supported by Trilium:
The default note type, which allows for rich text formatting, images, admonitions and right-to-left support.
Uses a mono-space font and can be used to store larger chunks of code or plain text than a text note, and has better syntax highlighting.
Stores the information about a search (the search text, criteria, etc.) for later use. Can be used for quick filtering of a large amount of notes, for example. The search can easily be triggered.
Allows easy creation of notes and relations between them. Can be used for mainly relational data such as a family tree.
Displays the relationships between the notes, whether via relations or their hierarchical structure.
Used in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Scripting__TRILIUM_PH_1__, it displays the HTML content of another note. This allows displaying any kind of content, provided there is a script behind it to generate it.

Displays the children of the note either as a grid, a list, or for a more specialized case: a calendar.              __TRILIUM_PH_0__  __TRILIUM_PH_1__Generally useful for easy reading of short notes.
Displays diagrams such as bar charts, flow charts, state diagrams, etc. Requires a bit of technical knowledge since the diagrams are written in a specialized format.
Allows easy drawing of sketches, diagrams, handwritten content. Uses the same technology behind __TRILIUM_PH_0__excalidraw.com__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Displays the content of an external web page, similar to a browser.
Easy for brainstorming ideas, by placing them in a hierarchical layout.
Displays the children of the note as a geographical map, one use-case would be to plan vacations. It even has basic support for tracks. Notes can also be created from it.
Represents an uploaded file such as PDFs, images, video or audio files.

units.source: The Calendar view will display each child note in a calendar that has a start date and optionally an end date, as an event.
The Calendar view has multiple display modes:
Month view, where the entire month is displayed and all-day events can be inserted. Both time-specific events and all-day events are listed.
Week view, where all the 7 days of the week (or 5 if the weekends are hidden) are displayed in columns. This mode allows entering and displaying time-specific events, not just all-day events.
Day view, which views only a single day. Especially useful for heavy agendas or mobile views.
List view, which displays all the events of a given month in sequence.
Year view, which displays the entire year for quick reference.
Unlike other Collection view types, the Calendar view also allows some kind of interaction, such as moving events around as well as creating new ones.

Right click on an existing note in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and select __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert child note__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Collection__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Calendar__TRILIUM_PH_7__.
First, click the desired day (month & year views) or the desired timeslot (day view).
Alternatively, drag across multiple days (or time slots) to set both the start and end date.

In either cases, a small popup will show with a prompt for a title and the date & time of the event that will be created. The date and time can be changed there the same way as in the popup view of an existing event (see below).

At this point, the event hasn't been created yet to protect against accidental clicks. Add a title optionally and press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Create__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button. If no title is provided, the event will follow the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Default Note Title__TRILIUM_PH_3__ rules.

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__ template field below the date and time shows the note type or template the event's note is made from. To make the event from another one, press the field and select it from the list; the calendar remembers the choice for the next event. Select __TRILIUM_PH_1__More templates…__TRILIUM_PH_2__ to change which templates are listed (see __TRILIUM_PH_3__Event templates__TRILIUM_PH_4__). The date and time entered for the event replace any dates and times the template carries.

To give the event a time before creating it (for example, after clicking a day in the month view), press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add time__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and set the start and end time; the duration is shown to the right of them. To make the event all-day again, press the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ button at the end of the row. Adding or removing a time keeps the dates, so an event can start at a time on one day and end at a time on another (for example, a night shift). Changing the start date or time moves the end by the same amount, keeping the duration. An empty end date means the event ends on the day it starts; setting the end time before the start time moves the end date to the next day.
After creating the event, it will show up on the calendar. To edit the content of the event (including recurrence), click on it to bring it into the popup view.
Creating new notes from the calendar will respect the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ relation if set on the Collection note.
Hovering the mouse over an event will display information about the note.__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__
Left clicking the event will open a dedicated popup to quickly configure the event or edit its note content.
Right click will offer more options including opening the note in a new split or window.
Drag and drop an event on the calendar to move it to another day.
The length of an event can be changed by placing the mouse to the right edge of the event and dragging the mouse around.

On a __TRILIUM_PH_0__read-only__TRILIUM_PH_1__ calendar, events can't be dragged, resized or created, their context menu only offers the places to open them in, and the button to pin the current date is hidden. Switching between the month, week and day views still works, but the choice isn't saved.
