units.source: When Trilium is on mobile, the interaction with the calendar is slightly different:
Clicking on an event displays the popup view, which allows editing the event.
Long-presing an event triggers the contextual menu, including the option to open in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Quick edit__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
To insert a new event, touch and hold the empty space. When successful, the empty space will become colored to indicate the selection.
Before releasing, drag across multiple spaces to create multi-day events.
When released, a prompt will appear to enter the note title.
To move an existing event, touch and hold the event until the empty space near it will become colored.
At this point the event can be dragged across other days on the calendar.
Or the event can be resized by tapping on the small circle to the right end of the event.
To exit out of editing mode, simply tap the empty space anywhere on the calendar.
In the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collection Properties__TRILIUM_PH_1__, it's possible to:
Hide weekends from the week view.
Display week numbers on the calendar.
Hide routine events from the month, year and list views (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Hiding routine events__TRILIUM_PH_1__).
Set the slot duration (the length of each time row in day/week view).
Set the slot label interval (how often time labels appear on the axis in day/week view).

The same settings are also listed under __TRILIUM_PH_0__General__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ __TRILIUM_PH_3__Calendar properties__TRILIUM_PH_4__ dialog (see __TRILIUM_PH_5__Event templates__TRILIUM_PH_6__ for how to open it). units.source: The table view displays information in a grid, where the rows are individual notes and the columns are __TRILIUM_PH_0__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__. In addition, values are editable.
The tabular structure is represented as such:
Each child note is a row in the table.
If child rows also have children, they will be displayed under an expander (nested notes).
Each column is a __TRILIUM_PH_0__promoted attribute__TRILIUM_PH_1__ that is defined on the Collection note.
Actually, both promoted and unpromoted attributes are supported, but it's a requirement to use a label/relation definition.
The promoted attributes are usually defined as inheritable in order to show up in the child notes, but it's not a requirement.
If there are multiple attribute definitions with the same __TRILIUM_PH_0__, only one will be displayed.
If an attribute definition has multiple values, they will all be grouped under a single column, with chips indicating individual values.
There are also a few predefined columns:
The current item number, identified by the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ symbol.
This simply counts the note and is affected by sorting.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Note ID__TRILIUM_PH_1__, representing the unique ID used internally by Trilium

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Created__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Modified__TRILIUM_PH_3__, the date and time the note was created and last modified. These columns are hidden by default and can't be edited; show them from the column context menu and click their header to sort by them.

units.context: Table > Interaction > Creating a new table

units.source: Right click on an existing note in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and select __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert child note__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Collection__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Table__TRILIUM_PH_7__.
units.context: Table > Interaction > Creating a new table

units.source: Each column is a __TRILIUM_PH_0__promoted or unpromoted attribute__TRILIUM_PH_1__ that is defined on the Collection note.
To create a new column, either:
Press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add new column__TRILIUM_PH_1__ at the bottom of the table.
Right click on an existing column and select Add column to the left/right.

Right click on the empty space of the column header and select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Label__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Relation__TRILIUM_PH_3__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_4__New column__TRILIUM_PH_5__ section.
Each row is actually a note that is a child of the Collection note.
To create a new note, either:
Press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add new row__TRILIUM_PH_1__ at the bottom of the table.
Right click on an existing row and select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Insert row above, Insert child note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert row below__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
By default it will try to edit the title of the newly created note.
Alternatively, the note can be created from the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__scripting__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
Right clicking on a column, allows:
Sorting by the selected column and resetting the sort.
Hiding the selected column or adjusting the visibility of every column.
Adding new columns to the left or the right of the column.
Right clicking on the space to the right of the columns, allows:
Adjusting the visibility of every column.
Right clicking on a row, allows:
Opening the corresponding note of the row in a new tab, split, window or quick editing it.
Inserting a new note above or below the selected row. These options are only enabled if the table is not sorted.
Inserting a new child note for the selected row.
Hovering over a row shows an __TRILIUM_PH_0__Open__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button at the end of its title, which opens the note in quick edit. On a touch screen, the button is always visible.
Clicking the title itself renames the note instead (see below). To open the note elsewhere:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+click or middle click the title to open the note in a new tab.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_1__+click the title to open it in a new window.
Right click the row to open the note in a new tab, split or window, or in quick edit.
Simply click on a cell within a row to change its value. The change will not only reflect in the table, but also as an attribute of the corresponding note.
The editing will respect the type of the promoted attribute, by presenting a normal text box, a number selector or a date selector for example.
A boolean column shows a checkbox, which is checked or unchecked with a single click. A note without the label shows an unchecked box.
It also possible to change the title of a note by clicking it.
Simply click on a relation and it will become editable. Enter the text to look for a note and click on it.
To remove a relation, remove the title of the note from the text box and click outside the cell.
It is possible to edit a column by right clicking it and selecting __TRILIUM_PH_0__Edit column…__TRILIUM_PH_1__ This will basically change the label/relation definition at the collection level.

Turn on __TRILIUM_PH_0__Multiple values__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to let each note hold several values in that column. The cell then shows them as chips (see __TRILIUM_PH_2__Multiple values__TRILIUM_PH_3__ in Promoted Attributes). The same toggle is available when adding a column.
If the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Name__TRILIUM_PH_1__ field of a column is changed, this will trigger a batch operation in which the corresponding label/relation will be renamed in all the children.

On a __TRILIUM_PH_0__read-only__TRILIUM_PH_1__ table, the cells can't be edited and the rows can't be dragged. Clicking a note's title opens it in quick edit, so there's no __TRILIUM_PH_2__Open__TRILIUM_PH_3__ button. The __TRILIUM_PH_4__New row__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and __TRILIUM_PH_6__New column__TRILIUM_PH_7__ buttons are hidden, and the context menus offer only what leaves the notes as they are: sorting and hiding columns, and opening the notes. Columns can still be resized and reordered, but the layout isn't saved. The __TRILIUM_PH_8__Table properties__TRILIUM_PH_9__ dialog isn't available.

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Hold cards over a collapsed column for a few seconds:__TRILIUM_PH_1__ The column will expand, allowing you to drop the cards at the desired position (if manual sorting is enabled) or peek at the other cards before deciding whether to drop them.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Collapsing and expanding columns > Collapsing

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Move a card to a collapsed column using the keyboard:__TRILIUM_PH_1__ The column will temporarily expand to reveal the moved card. You can then continue moving the selected cards up or down, or to another column.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Collapsing and expanding columns > Collapsing

units.source: Collapsed columns can still be reordered, and their menus remain available.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Collapsing and expanding columns > Collapsing

units.source: A collapsed column shows its title vertically, read from the bottom up. If any column title on the board contains Chinese, Japanese or Korean characters, the titles of all collapsed columns read from the top down instead, so that those characters stay upright.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Collapsing and expanding columns > Collapsing
Kanban Board > Working with columns > Collapsing and expanding columns > Expanding

units.source: You can restore a collapsed column so that its content is visible again in the following ways:
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Collapsing and expanding columns > Expanding

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Using a mouse:__TRILIUM_PH_1__ Click the collapsed column.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Collapsing and expanding columns > Expanding

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Using touch:__TRILIUM_PH_1__ Tap the collapsed column, and then press the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ button on the side toolbar.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Collapsing and expanding columns > Expanding

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Using the keyboard:__TRILIUM_PH_1__ Move the focus to the collapsed column, and then press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Space__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Collapsing and expanding columns > Expanding
Kanban Board > Working with columns > Collapsing and expanding columns > Keeping a column collapsed

units.source: By default, once a column is expanded, it remains expanded. However, you can configure a column to collapse again after you finish working with it. To activate this behavior, open the column menu and check __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Keep the column collapsed__TRILIUM_PH_2__.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Collapsing and expanding columns > Keeping a column collapsed

units.source: A column configured to remain collapsed will expand like any other collapsed column, but only temporarily, until another column is focused.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Collapsing and expanding columns > Keeping a column collapsed
Kanban Board > Working with columns > Collapsing and expanding columns > Collapsing and expanding all columns

units.source: You can expand or collapse all columns at once by using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ (collapse) and __TRILIUM_PH_1__ (expand) buttons. On the desktop, these buttons are located at the bottom of the screen; on the mobile interface, they are in the header.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Collapsing and expanding columns > Collapsing and expanding all columns
Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column

units.source: By default, the cards in a column are sorted manually by moving them up and down. You can also keep them sorted automatically, using customizable criteria for each column. To customize the sorting options, open the column menu → __TRILIUM_PH_0__Sort__TRILIUM_PH_1__. The following options are available:
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Board's default__TRILIUM_PH_2__: Use the default sorting order (initially manual for new boards).
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Manually__TRILIUM_PH_2__: Sort cards by manually moving them up and down.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column
Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Creation date & time__TRILIUM_PH_2__: Sort cards by the creation date and time of the note represented by each card. If a card was created from an existing note, the date and time will match the original creation date and time of that note, not when the card was added to the board.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column

units.source: Any custom attribute: Any card attribute (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__) can be used as a sorting criterion.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Ascending__TRILIUM_PH_2__: Sort from smallest to largest (A to Z, 0 to 9, or oldest to newest).
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Descending__TRILIUM_PH_2__: Sort in reverse order, from largest to smallest.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column

units.source: The card order you set is preserved after you switch away from manual sorting. When you switch back to manual sorting, the cards will be in the same order in which you arranged them.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column
Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column > How card attributes are sorted

units.source: When cards are sorted by an attribute, they are ordered according to the following rules:

Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column > How card attributes are sorted
Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column > How card attributes are sorted

units.source: Text, Multi-line text, URL, Email, Phone

Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column > How card attributes are sorted

units.source: earliest hour (closest to 0) → latest hour (closest to 24)
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column > How card attributes are sorted
Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column > How card attributes are sorted
Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column > How card attributes are sorted
Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column > How card attributes are sorted

units.source: The order in which the options are declared.       __TRILIUM_PH_0__For example, a select attribute declared with “Low”, “Medium”, and “High” options will be sorted as follows: Low → Medium → High.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column > How card attributes are sorted
Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column > How card attributes are sorted

units.source: Grays → colors. Colors are ordered by their color-wheel __TRILIUM_PH_0__hue__TRILIUM_PH_1__ angle (from 0° to 360°).
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column > How card attributes are sorted

units.source: Relation attributes are ordered according to the title of the target note.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column > How card attributes are sorted

units.source: Cards with attributes that have no value set are always sorted at the end of the column, regardless of whether the sort order is ascending or descending. If an attribute holds more than one value, only the first value is used for sorting.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column > How card attributes are sorted
Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column > Configuring the default sorting options

units.source: Every new column uses the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Board's default__TRILIUM_PH_1__ sorting option, which is initially set to manual sorting on new boards. However, the default can be changed to any other sorting criterion and direction. To configure it, go to __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Board properties__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Default card order__TRILIUM_PH_7__ (under the __TRILIUM_PH_8__General__TRILIUM_PH_9__ section).
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column > Configuring the default sorting options

units.source: Once the default is changed, all columns set to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Board's default__TRILIUM_PH_1__ sorting option will follow the new sorting options.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column > Configuring the default sorting options

units.source: Columns using a sorting option other than __TRILIUM_PH_0__Board's default__TRILIUM_PH_1__ will not be affected by the new default. To override all columns so that they use the default sorting options, use the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Reset sorting options to default for all columns__TRILIUM_PH_3__ command in __TRILIUM_PH_4__Board properties__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column > Configuring the default sorting options

units.source: Using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ attribute on Kanban boards __TRILIUM_PH_1__is no longer recommended__TRILIUM_PH_2__, because it applies to every column and prevents manual sorting. Instead, use __TRILIUM_PH_3__, which is designed exclusively for board collections and can take one of the following values: __TRILIUM_PH_4__, __TRILIUM_PH_5__, or __TRILIUM_PH_6__, for example, __TRILIUM_PH_7__. Using the __TRILIUM_PH_8__ label will switch to descending order.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Sorting cards within a column > Configuring the default sorting options
Kanban Board > Working with columns > Setting a limit

units.source: For each column, you can limit the number of cards it contains (also known as a WIP limit). Once the limit is exceeded, the column displays a visual warning to indicate that it is over its limit.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Setting a limit

units.source: To enable the limit, go to the column menu → __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Set limit__TRILIUM_PH_2__, and then:
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Setting a limit

units.source: Turn on the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Warn for exceeding the column capacity__TRILIUM_PH_1__ toggle.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Setting a limit

units.source: Enter the desired limit in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Maximum number of cards in the column__TRILIUM_PH_1__ text box.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Setting a limit
Kanban Board > Working with columns > Setting a limit

units.source: A column that has reached its limit can still accept new cards. Blocking new cards is not supported and most likely never will be, due to the way Trilium works: cards are regular notes, and the attributes used to group them into columns can be set from anywhere in the app, outside the board control. As a result, enforcing the limit would not be consistent.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Setting a limit
Kanban Board > Working with columns > Archiving a column

units.source: If you want to hide a column from the board without deleting it, you can archive it by opening the column menu → __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Archive column__TRILIUM_PH_2__. Archiving a column does not set the archived flag (see __TRILIUM_PH_3__Archived Notes__TRILIUM_PH_4__) on the notes corresponding to its cards.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Archiving a column

units.source: To show archived columns again, go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Collection options__TRILIUM_PH_2__ and toggle __TRILIUM_PH_3__ __TRILIUM_PH_4__Show archived notes__TRILIUM_PH_5__, or turn on __TRILIUM_PH_6__Show archived cards and columns__TRILIUM_PH_7__ in __TRILIUM_PH_8__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_9__ → __TRILIUM_PH_10__Board properties__TRILIUM_PH_11__ (under the __TRILIUM_PH_12__Included notes__TRILIUM_PH_13__ section). Archived columns will appear faded. To restore one, open its column menu and select __TRILIUM_PH_14__ __TRILIUM_PH_15__Unarchive column__TRILIUM_PH_16__.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Archiving a column
Kanban Board > Working with columns > Deleting a column

units.source: You can delete a column by opening the column menu → __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Delete column__TRILIUM_PH_2__, or by pressing __TRILIUM_PH_3__Delete__TRILIUM_PH_4__ when a column header is focused, and then confirming. This removes the column from the board and unsets the grouping attribute for each note represented by a card in that column. If the column contains cards, the confirmation also offers to delete their notes instead of keeping them.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Deleting a column

units.source: The inbox column is not deleted this way. Its menu entry is __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Remove inbox column__TRILIUM_PH_2__, and __TRILIUM_PH_3__Delete__TRILIUM_PH_4__ on its header hides the inbox without changing any card.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Deleting a column
Kanban Board > Working with columns > The inbox column

units.source: The inbox column is a special column containing cards that are not assigned to another column. It is particularly useful when you switch an existing collection containing child notes to a board collection. The inbox column turns all child notes into cards that you can quickly distribute among the other columns. It can also act as a backlog where you can keep new cards that might eventually become part of the board.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > The inbox column

units.source: The inbox column is hidden by default. To show it, go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Collection options__TRILIUM_PH_2__ and toggle __TRILIUM_PH_3__Show inbox column__TRILIUM_PH_4__. The inbox column is distinguishable by its transparent background. It is always the first column and cannot be moved. It does not support a card limit. Otherwise, it operates like a regular column: its title, icon, and color can be changed; it can be sorted manually or automatically; and it can be collapsed.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > The inbox column

units.source: You can also show the inbox column by applying the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ label (read more about __TRILIUM_PH_1__Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_2__) to the board note.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > The inbox column

units.source: Optionally, the inbox column can also list nested notes from the board collection's subtree. To enable this, open the column menu and check __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Include nested notes__TRILIUM_PH_2__.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > The inbox column
Kanban Board > Working with columns > Changing the width of columns

units.source: There are three predefined widths for board columns: narrow (default), medium, and wide. To change the width, open the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Board properties__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Column width__TRILIUM_PH_5__ (under the __TRILIUM_PH_6__General__TRILIUM_PH_7__ section). This option applies to every column on the board, except in the mobile version.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Changing the width of columns

units.source: The same option is also available through the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ label (read more about __TRILIUM_PH_1__Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_2__) on the board note, which accepts “__TRILIUM_PH_3__”, “__TRILIUM_PH_4__”, or “__TRILIUM_PH_5__” as its value.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Changing the width of columns

units.source: You can also redefine these three widths by using custom app CSS (read more about __TRILIUM_PH_0__Custom app-wide CSS__TRILIUM_PH_1__) and assigning the desired pixel values as follows:
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with columns > Changing the width of columns
Kanban Board > Working with cards > Creating a new card

units.source: To create a new card, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__New card__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button located at the bottom of each column. To create a new card above or below a specific card, right-click or hold that card, and then select __TRILIUM_PH_3__ __TRILIUM_PH_4__Insert new above__TRILIUM_PH_5__ or __TRILIUM_PH_6__ __TRILIUM_PH_7__Insert new below__TRILIUM_PH_8__ from the context menu. Alternatively, press __TRILIUM_PH_9__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_10__ + __TRILIUM_PH_11__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_12__ to create a new card above the focused card, or __TRILIUM_PH_13__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_14__ to create one below it.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Creating a new card

units.source: Next, type the title of the new card, and then press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button or __TRILIUM_PH_1__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_2__ to complete it. Tap or click anywhere outside the text box to dismiss it. You can also select a different icon and card template. To learn more about card templates, see Card templates (learn more about __TRILIUM_PH_3__Templates__TRILIUM_PH_4__).
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Creating a new card

units.source: After the card is created, you can tap or click it, or press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Space__TRILIUM_PH_1__, to edit the note content.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Creating a new card

units.source: When using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__New card__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button, cards are always created at the end of the column. To create the card at the top of the column, right-click or hold the __TRILIUM_PH_3__ button and select __TRILIUM_PH_4__ __TRILIUM_PH_5__Create at top__TRILIUM_PH_6__. When using keyboard shortcuts, focus the column header and press __TRILIUM_PH_7__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_8__ to create a new card at the start of the column, or __TRILIUM_PH_9__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_10__ + __TRILIUM_PH_11__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_12__ to create one at the end.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Creating a new card

units.source: Adding an existing note as a card__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Adding an existing note as a card

units.source: Any note in your knowledge base can be represented as a card on a board. To add an existing note to your board, create a new card but do not enter a title. Instead, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button. Alternatively, use the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ __TRILIUM_PH_2__Add an existing note as a card__TRILIUM_PH_3__ command from the column menu.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Adding an existing note as a card

units.source: In the dialog that opens, search for the note by name, and then press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add to column__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button to insert it. Alternatively, you can drag any note from the tree and drop it at the desired position on the board.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Adding an existing note as a card

units.source: If the target note is already in the board collection's subtree, it will already be listed in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__inbox column__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Adding an existing note as a card

units.source: Notes added to the board are cloned, not duplicated. This means that changes to their titles, content, and attributes on the board are reflected in their original locations as well. See __TRILIUM_PH_0__Cloning Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for more information.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Adding an existing note as a card
Kanban Board > Working with cards > Selecting multiple cards

units.source: When working with a board, you may need to perform operations on multiple cards at once, such as moving them to another column, setting attributes or colors, deleting them, or archiving them.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Selecting multiple cards

units.source: You can select multiple cards in the following ways:
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Selecting multiple cards
Kanban Board > Working with cards > Selecting multiple cards

units.source: To add a card to the selection, hold __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and click the card. Repeat this for other cards until all the desired cards are selected. Clicking a selected card again while holding __TRILIUM_PH_2__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_3__ will deselect it.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Selecting multiple cards

units.source: If the cards you want to select form a continuous sequence within a column, hold __TRILIUM_PH_0__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_1__, click the first card in the sequence, and then click the last card.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Selecting multiple cards
Kanban Board > Working with cards > Selecting multiple cards
Kanban Board > Working with cards > Selecting multiple cards

units.source: To enter selection mode, tap the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button at the top of the screen. A selection toolbar will appear in the header, displaying “0 cards selected”.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Selecting multiple cards

units.source: Tap the cards you want to select. If you tap a selected card again, it will be deselected. To select all cards in a column, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button on the selection toolbar. To clear the selection, press the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ button.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Selecting multiple cards

units.source: Use the side toolbar to apply actions to the selected cards.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Selecting multiple cards
Kanban Board > Working with cards > Selecting multiple cards

units.source: To add the currently focused card to the selection, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ + __TRILIUM_PH_2__Space__TRILIUM_PH_3__. Repeat this for the other cards you want to select. Pressing __TRILIUM_PH_4__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_5__ + __TRILIUM_PH_6__Space__TRILIUM_PH_7__ again on a selected card will deselect it.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Selecting multiple cards

units.source: To select a continuous sequence of cards within a column, hold __TRILIUM_PH_0__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and use the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Up__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Down__TRILIUM_PH_5__ arrow keys to expand or shrink the selection.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Selecting multiple cards

units.source: To select every card in the column the focus is in, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ + __TRILIUM_PH_2__A__TRILIUM_PH_3__. The same action is available from the column menu, as __TRILIUM_PH_4____TRILIUM_PH_5__Select all cards__TRILIUM_PH_6__.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Selecting multiple cards
Kanban Board > Working with cards > Selecting multiple cards
Kanban Board > Working with cards > Moving cards between columns

units.source: To move one or more cards to another column, use one of the following methods:
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Moving cards between columns
Kanban Board > Working with cards > Moving cards between columns > Using touch or a mouse

units.source: Touch and hold the card, or click and hold it with the mouse, and then drag it to the desired column. If the column uses manual sorting, you can also position the card relative to the other cards.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Moving cards between columns > Using touch or a mouse

units.source: To drag a card outside the board, for example to the note tree, another split, or another window, hold __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and then start dragging.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Moving cards between columns > Using touch or a mouse

units.source: If the target column is collapsed, you can drop the card onto its header to move it into that column (at the end if manually sorted), without expanding it. However, if you want to reveal its cards before dropping, hold the card over the column for a few seconds; the column will then expand.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Moving cards between columns > Using touch or a mouse

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__You can quickly drop a card at the start or end of a column.__TRILIUM_PH_1__
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Moving cards between columns > Using touch or a mouse

units.source: Drop the card above the column while the “Drop as the first card” hint is displayed to make it the first card in that column. Alternatively, drop it below the column while the “Drop as the last card” hint is displayed to make it the last card.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Moving cards between columns > Using touch or a mouse
Kanban Board > Working with cards > Moving cards between columns > Using the keyboard

units.source: You can also use keyboard shortcuts to move the selected card or cards between columns:
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Moving cards between columns > Using the keyboard

units.source: To quickly move a card to another column, open the card's context menu and select the destination column. The menu lists the first seven columns; on a wider board, the remaining ones are grouped under __TRILIUM_PH_0__More…__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Moving cards between columns > Using the context menu
Kanban Board > Working with cards > Reordering cards within a column

units.source: Cards within a column can be freely reordered unless the column uses a sorting option other than manual. To reposition a card, drag it as described in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Moving cards between columns__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section and drop it at the desired position.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Reordering cards within a column

units.source: Alternatively, you can use keyboard shortcuts to move the selected card or cards:
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Reordering cards within a column
Kanban Board > Working with cards > Reordering cards within a column
Kanban Board > Working with cards > Reordering cards within a column

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ + __TRILIUM_PH_2__Home__TRILIUM_PH_3__: Move to the top of the column.
units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Reordering cards within a column

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ + __TRILIUM_PH_2__End__TRILIUM_PH_3__: Move to the end of the column.

units.source: If multiple cards are selected, the keyboard shortcuts work only if the selection consists of a continuous sequence of cards.

Kanban Board > Working with cards > Editing a card

units.source: Every card on a board is a regular note. To edit the note associated with a card, click or tap the card, or press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Space__TRILIUM_PH_1__ when the card is selected. The note will open in a Quick Edit dialog, where you can modify it. You can also open the note in a new tab, split, or window by using the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ __TRILIUM_PH_3__Open note__TRILIUM_PH_4__ submenu in the card's context menu. Kanban Board > Working with cards > Working with custom card attributes

units.source: By default, the face of a card displays a minimal set of information: the title, icon, and color. In some cases, this may not provide enough useful information at a glance. You can extend the card to display extra information, called card attributes, such as a due date, priority, completion status, or any other information you need. Card attributes use the same principles as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Working with custom card attributes > Creating a new attribute

units.source: Enter a name for the attribute. This is the internal name used by Trilium, so do not use spaces or special characters.

Attributes that only the cards define are listed after the board's own.

units.source: On a board, cards are grouped into columns. The column to which a card belongs is determined by the value of the __TRILIUM_PH_0__grouping attribute__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which is a regular attribute of the card's note.

units.context: Kanban Board > Working with cards > Grouping cards

units.source: Under the hood, the Status attribute is declared on the board collection note with the name __TRILIUM_PH_0__. It is a select-type attribute that is inheritable and promoted. Each select option becomes a column, and each new column created on the board extends the list of options.

units.source: A board marked as __TRILIUM_PH_0__read-only__TRILIUM_PH_1__ only shows its cards. The context menus of a card or a column keep only the entries that change nothing, such as opening the note or __TRILIUM_PH_2____TRILIUM_PH_3__Copy reference__TRILIUM_PH_4__, and the board's own menu doesn't open. The cards can still be grouped by another attribute, but the choice isn't saved, and no new grouping attribute can be created.

Drawing shapes > Drawing a shape on the map > Finishing and cancelling

units.source: To give up on a shape while drawing it, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Escape__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or press the tool's button again. Whatever has been drawn so far is discarded.
units.context: Drawing shapes > Drawing a shape on the map > Finishing and cancelling

units.context: Drawing shapes > Drawing a shape on the map > Finishing and cancelling

units.source: Clicking a shape opens the standard panel which allows changing the title, the content and with buttons to open the note or remove it.
When clicking, a marker takes priority over the shape.
Right-clicking a shape opens a contextual menu similar to the one for markers, which allows opening the corresponding note or removing the shape.
Typing in the map's search bar finds shapes by their title, as it does markers. Selecting one brings the whole shape into view.

units.context: Drawing shapes > How shapes are represented

units.source: Shapes are represented quite similarly to markers, which means each shape is a note. The information about the same is stored using a __TRILIUM_PH_0__label__TRILIUM_PH_1__ called __TRILIUM_PH_2__.
units.context: Drawing shapes > How shapes are represented

units.source: An image map is a geo map drawn over an image of your own instead of a world map, such as a floor plan, a fantasy map for a tabletop game, or a diagram to annotate. Markers and shapes work as they do on a geo map, but their positions are measured on the image instead of in latitude and longitude: in the image's own pixels, or in a coordinate system of your choosing, such as the one a video game uses.

units.context: Image maps > Creating an image map

units.source: Upload the image as a note of its own, for example by dragging the file into the note tree. PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF images are supported; SVG images are not.
units.context: Image maps > Creating an image map

units.source: Create a geo map, or open an existing one.
units.context: Image maps > Creating an image map

units.source: Open the __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Geo map properties__TRILIUM_PH_2__ dialog from the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_4__ or from the settings menu of the __TRILIUM_PH_5__Collection Properties__TRILIUM_PH_6__.
units.context: Image maps > Creating an image map

units.source: Under __TRILIUM_PH_0__Background__TRILIUM_PH_1__, set __TRILIUM_PH_2__Type__TRILIUM_PH_3__ to __TRILIUM_PH_4__Custom image__TRILIUM_PH_5__, then choose the image note in __TRILIUM_PH_6__Image note__TRILIUM_PH_7__. The list only offers image notes in a format the map can draw (PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF), and shows all of them before anything is typed.
units.context: Image maps > Creating an image map

units.source: The map then shows the image instead of the world map and opens with the whole image in view. To go back to a world map, set __TRILIUM_PH_0__Type__TRILIUM_PH_1__ back to __TRILIUM_PH_2__Vector & Raster__TRILIUM_PH_3__. The image is switched off rather than removed: its relation is renamed to __TRILIUM_PH_4__, so setting __TRILIUM_PH_5__Type__TRILIUM_PH_6__ to __TRILIUM_PH_7__Custom image__TRILIUM_PH_8__ again brings back the same image, with its coordinates. An image that the geo map inherits from a parent note or a template can only be switched off on the note that holds it.
units.context: Image maps > Creating an image map

units.source: The image note is stored in a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__relation__TRILIUM_PH_2__ of the geo map, which can also be added by hand.
units.context: Image maps > Creating an image map

units.source: Images are resized when they are uploaded, so by default the image of a map is at most 2000 pixels on its longer side, which can be too coarse for a detailed map. To keep an image at a higher resolution, do one of the following before uploading it:

In __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Media__TRILIUM_PH_3__, raise __TRILIUM_PH_4__Max image dimensions__TRILIUM_PH_5__ or turn off __TRILIUM_PH_6__Automatically compress images__TRILIUM_PH_7__.
Upload it through the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Import__TRILIUM_PH_1__ dialog with __TRILIUM_PH_2__Compress images__TRILIUM_PH_3__ unchecked.
An image that was already uploaded keeps its size; upload it again after changing the settings.

The image is drawn as a single picture by the graphics card, which limits how large it can be. Images up to 4096 pixels on their longer side are safe on practically every device, and most computers handle up to 16384 pixels. On a device whose graphics card cannot hold the image, the markers and shapes still appear but the image itself does not. The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Geo map properties__TRILIUM_PH_1__ dialog warns about an image larger than 4096 pixels, and about one that can't be used at all, such as an SVG image.

Adding, moving and removing markers, drawing shapes, the popup view and the contextual menu work as described for the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Geo Map__TRILIUM_PH_1__. The camera stays over the image and can zoom in up to four times past the image's own resolution.
The features that only make sense on a real map are not available on an image map:
Searching the map and searching for places online.
Clicking the places the base map shows.
Opening a location in an external map application.

The look of the marker titles follows the image: if the image is dark, turn on __TRILIUM_PH_0__Dark image__TRILIUM_PH_1__ under __TRILIUM_PH_2__Background__TRILIUM_PH_3__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Geo map properties__TRILIUM_PH_5__ dialog, so that the titles are drawn in a light color. This sets the __TRILIUM_PH_6__ label.
The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Map style__TRILIUM_PH_1__ setting doesn't apply to an image map, so it's hidden from the settings menu of the collection while the map has an image.

units.context: Image maps > Choosing the coordinate system

units.source: By default, positions are measured in pixels of the image at its original size, from its top-left corner, with __TRILIUM_PH_0__ growing to the right and __TRILIUM_PH_1__ growing downwards.
units.context: Image maps > Choosing the coordinate system

units.source: To use coordinates of your own instead, open the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Geo map properties__TRILIUM_PH_1__ dialog, set __TRILIUM_PH_2__Coordinates__TRILIUM_PH_3__ under __TRILIUM_PH_4__Background__TRILIUM_PH_5__ to __TRILIUM_PH_6__Custom__TRILIUM_PH_7__, and enter the coordinates of the image's __TRILIUM_PH_8__Top-left corner__TRILIUM_PH_9__ and __TRILIUM_PH_10__Bottom-right corner__TRILIUM_PH_11__. Switching to __TRILIUM_PH_12__Custom__TRILIUM_PH_13__ starts from the image's size in pixels, so the markers stay where they are until the corners are changed; for that reason, __TRILIUM_PH_14__Custom__TRILIUM_PH_15__ can only be chosen once the image has loaded. All positions are then read and written in those coordinates, including the ones shown in the contextual menu and in the popup view. To go back to pixels, set __TRILIUM_PH_16__Coordinates__TRILIUM_PH_17__ to __TRILIUM_PH_18__Image pixels__TRILIUM_PH_19__. Corners that the geo map inherits from a parent note or a template can only be removed on the note that holds them; entering other corners on this map overrides them.
units.context: Image maps > Choosing the coordinate system

units.source: The corners are stored in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ label of the geo map as __TRILIUM_PH_1__, with a space between the two corners, which can also be set by hand. For example:
units.context: Image maps > Choosing the coordinate system

units.source: A screenshot of a game map that covers __TRILIUM_PH_0__ from -512 to 512 and __TRILIUM_PH_1__ from -512 to 512, with __TRILIUM_PH_2__ growing downwards: __TRILIUM_PH_3__. Coordinates copied from the game can then be pasted directly into __TRILIUM_PH_4__.
units.context: Image maps > Choosing the coordinate system

units.source: A world whose __TRILIUM_PH_0__ grows upwards, with the origin in the middle of the image: __TRILIUM_PH_1__. A top-left __TRILIUM_PH_2__ larger than the bottom-right one is what flips the axis.
units.context: Image maps > Choosing the coordinate system

units.source: A floor plan measured in meters: __TRILIUM_PH_0__.
units.context: Image maps > Choosing the coordinate system

units.source: The two axes don't have to use the same scale. A circle is always measured in the map's own units, so it appears as an ellipse when the units are stretched differently along the two axes.
units.context: Image maps > Choosing the coordinate system

units.source: Corners that share an __TRILIUM_PH_0__ or a __TRILIUM_PH_1__ don't span an area: the dialog doesn't save them, and a label holding them, or a value that cannot be read, is ignored and the pixels of the image are used instead.
units.context: Image maps > Choosing the coordinate system

units.source: Enabling __TRILIUM_PH_0__Show scale__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in the collection properties draws rulers along the edges of the image instead of a distance scale. Round values of the map's coordinates are marked with ticks along all four edges, labeled along the top and left ones, with faint grid lines across the image. The spacing follows the zoom level, and the values follow __TRILIUM_PH_2__ when it is set.
The rulers are drawn on the image itself, so they move out of view along with its edges when zooming in. The grid lines remain visible across the image.

units.context: Image maps > How the positions are stored

units.source: Because positions are stored in different labels from the ones of a geo map, the same note can be placed both on a geo map and on an image map.
units.context: Image maps > How the positions are stored
Image maps > How the positions are stored
Image maps > How the positions are stored

units.source: The position of a marker, as __TRILIUM_PH_0__, for example __TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Image maps > How the positions are stored

units.source: A shape, in the same format as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ (see __TRILIUM_PH_1__Drawing shapes__TRILIUM_PH_2__) but with __TRILIUM_PH_3__ pairs, and a circle's radius in the map's units, for example __TRILIUM_PH_4__.
units.context: Image maps > How the positions are stored

units.source: The positions belong to the coordinate system, not to the image. When replacing the image with a different one, for example a higher-resolution copy, keep __TRILIUM_PH_0__ describing the area the new image covers and every marker stays in place. With __TRILIUM_PH_1__Image pixels__TRILIUM_PH_2__, the positions are pixels, so an image of a different size moves the markers relative to what the image shows; to avoid that, switch __TRILIUM_PH_3__Coordinates__TRILIUM_PH_4__ to __TRILIUM_PH_5__Custom__TRILIUM_PH_6__ before replacing the image, which keeps the size of the old one (__TRILIUM_PH_7__) as the corners.
units.context: Image maps > How the positions are stored

units.source: To draw freely over an image instead of placing notes on it, consider a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Canvas__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Image maps > How the positions are stored

units.source: This note type displays the children notes on a geographical map, based on an attribute. It is also possible to add new notes at a specific location using the built-in interface.
Add markers on the map, which can be customized with icons, colors and text.
Search the notes already on the map, and look up places anywhere in the world.
Turn a place the map already shows into a marker by clicking it.
Draw paths, areas, rectangles and circles onto the map.
Display tracks on the map using __TRILIUM_PH_0__ files.
Show your own location on the map and follow it as you move.
3D view of the map, which displays buildings when using a vector map.
Starting with v0.105.0, the geomap uses MapLibre GL which requires WebGL v1 support. In general, most devices will support it because browsers/Electron can render it in software if needed.

If the map could not be drawn because WebGL could not be initialized, an error message will appear instead of the map (__TRILIUM_PH_0__This map can't be drawn because WebGL isn't available…__TRILIUM_PH_1__).

The button that shows your location is offered only when Trilium is reached over HTTPS, in the desktop application or in the mobile application. Browsers refuse to share the location of a device with a page served over plain HTTP, so on such a server the button does not appear. The desktop application on Linux does not offer it either, because it has no way to find the location of the device there.

At the top-left there is the search bar. It searches the notes already on the map, and it can also search for places online when you ask it to. While you move through the results of a search, a counter with previous (__TRILIUM_PH_0__) and next (__TRILIUM_PH_1__) buttons appears under it.
At the bottom-center there is a central toolbar which provides editing features: adding new markers on the map (__TRILIUM_PH_0__) and importing GPX tracks (__TRILIUM_PH_1__).
At the bottom-right there are the viewport items:
On mobile these are hidden, use pinch to zoom instead.
On desktop, alternatively use the scroll wheel to adjust the zoom.
A __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button that shows your location on the map and follows it (see __TRILIUM_PH_1__Going to your location__TRILIUM_PH_2__ below).
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ Full screen button which focuses the entire map onto the screen, while still allowing for edits.
At the top-center (on desktop, or left-center on mobile and in split views) there are the drawing tools such as paths, areas, rectangles and circles.
When the map is read-only, the toolbar is not shown.

units.context: Geo Map > Creating a new geo map

units.source: Right click on an existing note in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and select __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert child note__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Collection__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Geo Map__TRILIUM_PH_7__.
units.context: Geo Map > Creating a new geo map

units.source: By default the map will be empty and will show the entire world.
units.context: Geo Map > Creating a new geo map

units.source: Click and drag the map in order to move across the map.
Use the mouse wheel, two-finger gesture on a touchpad or the +/- buttons on the bottom-right to adjust the zoom.
The position on the map and the zoom are saved inside the map note and restored when visiting again the note.

A map that has no position saved yet is framed around the markers it contains when you open it, so they are all in view without having to go looking for them. A map that contains no markers shows the whole world instead.

In practice this applies to maps whose markers were added externally, by a script or through __TRILIUM_PH_0__ETAPI (REST API)__TRILIUM_PH_1__. When you add markers yourself you have already moved the map to reach the place you are marking, and that movement saves a position.

units.context: Geo Map > Going to your location

units.source: Press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Show your location__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) button at the bottom-right of the map, beside the zoom buttons. The first time, the browser or the operating system asks whether Trilium may know where the device is. In the desktop application the operating system's location settings decide.
units.context: Geo Map > Going to your location

units.source: The map then moves to where the device is and marks it with a blue dot. A lighter circle around the dot shows how accurate the position is: a phone with GPS gives a dot on the street, while a computer located through its network connection can give a circle that covers a neighbourhood. The map follows the dot as it moves, and the button stays pressed while it does.
units.context: Geo Map > Going to your location

units.source: Dragging the map stops it from following. The dot stays and keeps moving, and pressing the button again brings the map back to it. Pressing the button while the map is following turns the dot off.
units.context: Geo Map > Going to your location

units.source: Click the dot to see its coordinates in the panel a searched place is shown in. From there the position can be kept as a marker (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Keeping a place as a marker__TRILIUM_PH_1__). Clicking the lighter circle around the dot is a click on the map.
units.context: Geo Map > Going to your location

units.source: If the position cannot be found, a message says so and the button keeps waiting for one; press it again to stop. If you refuse the permission, the button is disabled until the map is opened again. To allow it after all, change the permission for Trilium in the browser or in the system's location settings.
units.context: Geo Map > Going to your location

units.source: Your position is not stored in the note, and Trilium does not send it anywhere on its own. Moving the map there does what any other pan or zoom does: the tile provider behind the map's style sees the coordinates of the area now on screen. The map does remember where you left it, as it does after any other movement, so a map you have taken to your location opens there the next time.
units.context: Geo Map > Going to your location

units.source: The search bar at the top-left of the map searches in two places. It always searches the notes that are already on the map. It can also search for places online, but only when you ask it to.
Searching the notes already on the map__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Searching the notes already on the map

units.source: Type in the search bar, and the notes on the map are matched by their title as you type. Accents are ignored, both in what you type and in the titles, so __TRILIUM_PH_0__ finds __TRILIUM_PH_1__Zürich Hauptbahnhof__TRILIUM_PH_2__. Each word is searched for on its own, so __TRILIUM_PH_3__ finds __TRILIUM_PH_4__Paris Hotel__TRILIUM_PH_5__. Notes without a __TRILIUM_PH_6__ attribute are not offered, since there would be nowhere to go. Drawn shapes and GPS tracks are offered, even though they carry no such attribute: selecting one brings the whole shape or route into view.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Searching the notes already on the map

units.source: If more notes match than the list can show, you are offered the ones closest to the area you are viewing.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Searching the notes already on the map
Geo Map > Searching the map > Searching for places online

units.source: Looking up a place sends what you typed to a third-party service. For this reason, it never happens while you type. Instead, the last row of the result list offers the search. That row reads __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search online for "…"__TRILIUM_PH_1__, with the name of the service below it. The search runs only when you press that row or select it with Enter.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Searching for places online

units.source: Trilium uses Nominatim, the place search run by the OpenStreetMap Foundation. It needs no account and no API key. Its name is shown on every row that belongs to it: the row that offers the search, the row that says a search is running, and the row that reports that nothing was found or that the service could not be reached.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Searching for places online

units.source: The search prefers the area you are viewing. Places inside the current view are searched for first and listed above the others. If you search for a shop while looking at your own town, you therefore find the branch in that town, and not one with the same name on another continent. The view is always treated as at least 25 km across, so a search made while zoomed into a single street still covers the town around it.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Searching for places online
Geo Map > Searching the map > Going to a point

units.source: If you type or paste coordinates into the search bar, a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Go to__TRILIUM_PH_1__ row is offered above all the other results. Selecting it moves the map to that exact spot and marks it. You can then keep it as a marker, in the same way you keep a place found by searching.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Going to a point

units.source: Points are untitled by default; the corresponding note opens with the default name selected so it can be easily replaced. If the map has a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Default Note Title__TRILIUM_PH_1__ label, the marker is named by that template instead.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Going to a point
Geo Map > Searching the map > Going to a point

units.source: A plain pair, such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__. This is what Google Maps and OpenStreetMap both give you when you ask for the coordinates of a place, and it is also what the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ attribute holds.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Going to a point

units.source: The __TRILIUM_PH_0__ link that the map itself offers for a place, through the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Open location__TRILIUM_PH_2__ action.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Going to a point

units.source: The address of a place on Google Maps or OpenStreetMap, pasted whole.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Going to a point

units.source: A pair that is not a place on Earth, such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__, is not offered.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Going to a point
Geo Map > Searching the map > Reading the results

units.source: Results are gathered under headings, and each group is ordered by distance from the middle of the map:
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Reading the results

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__On this map__TRILIUM_PH_1__: notes that are already on the map, whatever their distance.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Reading the results

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Nearby__TRILIUM_PH_1__: places found within about 25 km of the view.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Reading the results
Geo Map > Searching the map > Reading the results

units.source: The headings only appear when at least two of the three groups contain something. Every row that has a position shows how far away it is, in kilometres or miles according to your locale. A place found online shows its name on the first line and its address on the second.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Reading the results
Geo Map > Searching the map > Selecting a result

units.source: Selecting a note already on the map moves to its marker and opens the note beside the map, as clicking the marker would.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Selecting a result

units.source: Selecting a place found online moves the map to it and marks it with a temporary pin. The pin has a different color from the map's own markers. The map is fitted to the area that the place covers, so a country fills the view, while a house is shown at street level. Some places have a boundary, such as a country, a county or a park. When the service reports one, that boundary is outlined under the pin.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Selecting a result

units.source: A panel then opens with the place's full address and its coordinates: in the top-right corner on desktop, and at the bottom of the map on mobile, where the top is kept for the search bar and the result counter. Pressing the coordinates copies them to the clipboard.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Selecting a result

units.source: Keeping a place as a marker__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Keeping a place as a marker

units.source: Press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add as marker__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in that panel to keep the place. A child note is created under the map. It takes the name of the place, as well as the icon, which matches the kind of place it is. Its __TRILIUM_PH_2__ attribute is already set. The note opens beside the map, so you can edit it straight away. The temporary pin disappears, because the place is now a marker like any other.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Keeping a place as a marker

units.source: The button is not offered on a map that cannot be edited, where the panel can still be read.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Keeping a place as a marker

units.source: Press the panel's close button, or the Escape key, to send the place away without keeping it. The pin goes with it.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Keeping a place as a marker
Geo Map > Searching the map > Stepping through the results

units.source: Once you select a result, a counter appears under the search bar, with a previous (__TRILIUM_PH_0__) and a next (__TRILIUM_PH_1__) button. These buttons move through everything the search offered, in the order it was listed. You can therefore compare several results without opening the list again. Pressing the counter itself moves the map back to the current result, which is useful after you have moved the map away from it.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > Stepping through the results
Geo Map > Searching the map > The keyboard

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_1__ runs the online search when its row is the one selected, and otherwise moves to the highlighted result. Pressed after a result has been taken, it brings the list back.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > The keyboard

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Escape__TRILIUM_PH_1__ closes the result list, and closes the place panel.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > The keyboard

units.source: Returning to the search bar reopens the list it was showing.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > The keyboard

units.source: The __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button at the end of the bar empties it, which also takes a searched place, its pin and its panel off the map.
units.context: Geo Map > Searching the map > The keyboard

units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map

units.source: To create a marker, first navigate to the desired point on the map. Then press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add marker__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) button at the center-bottom of the map.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a new note using the Add marker button

units.source: Once pressed, the map will enter in the insert mode, as illustrated by the notification. Additionally, a preview of the marker will be shown at the cursor position.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a new note using the Add marker button

units.source: Simply click the point on the map where to place the marker. To cancel, press either the  Escape key or press again the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add marker__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button.
units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a new note using the Add marker button

units.source: Once clicked, the marker will show up on the map and a popup will show to the right with the title already selected to be changed.

units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a new note using the contextual menu

units.context: Geo Map > Adding a marker using the map > Adding a new note using the contextual menu

units.source: Trilium can display GPS tracks on the geo map, in the form of __TRILIUM_PH_0__ files.
Drag & drop a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ file inside the geo map in the note tree.
In order for the file to be recognized as a GPS track, it needs to show up as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_1__File type__TRILIUM_PH_2__ field.
Press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add a GPS track from a GPX file__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) button which will directly prompt for a GPX file and import it as a subnote of the collection.
When going back to the map, the track should now be visible.

The starting point of the track will be displayed as a marker, with the name of the note underneath. The start marker will also respect the icon and the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ of the note. The end marker is displayed with a distinct icon.
If the track file contains multiple tracks, they will all be displayed as well as markers. Trilium will also split a single track that happens to have non-continuous points.
If the GPX contains waypoints, they will also be displayed, including their names.

When the track is clicked, the entire route is brought into view, as well as the right popup will indicate details about the track such as distance, duration and the elevation map. This information is also displayed when clicking the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ note itself.

When clicking on the markers of a track (whether it's the start or stop builtin markers, or custom markers that are part of the track), only that marker is brought into view, as opposed to the entire route.
When a map is __TRILIUM_PH_0__read-only__TRILIUM_PH_1__ all editing features will be disabled such as:
The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add marker__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) button at the bottom of the map.
Editing from the contextual menu (removing locations or adding new items).
Keeping a place as a marker, whether you found it by searching or clicked it on the map. You can still search and click, and you can still look at a place and copy its coordinates.
The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Geo map properties__TRILIUM_PH_1__ dialog; its entry is hidden from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
To set a map as read-only, go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Editable__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Read-only__TRILIUM_PH_5__.

The styling of the map can be adjusted in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collection Properties__TRILIUM_PH_1__, under __TRILIUM_PH_2__Background__TRILIUM_PH_3__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Geo map properties__TRILIUM_PH_5__ dialog, or manually via the __TRILIUM_PH_6__ attribute.
The geo map comes with two different types of styles:
For these styles the map is represented as a grid of images at different zoom levels. This is the traditional way OpenStreetMap used to work.
Currently, the only raster theme is the original OpenStreetMap style.
Vector styles are not represented as images, but as geometrical shapes. This makes the rendering much smoother, especially when zooming and looking at the building edges, for example.
The map can be zoomed in much further.
These come in various styles that are both light (Colorful, Graybeard, Neutrino) and dark (Eclipse, Shadow).
The vector styles come from __TRILIUM_PH_0__VersaTiles__TRILIUM_PH_1__, a free and open-source project providing map tiles based on OpenStreetMap.
The VersaTiles layers also provide 3D building information (see below).
The default theme is Versatiles Colorful (vector).

units.source: The following options can be configured either via the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collection Properties__TRILIUM_PH_1__, by clicking on the settings (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) button. Alternatively, each of these options also have a corresponding __TRILIUM_PH_3__label__TRILIUM_PH_4__ that can be set manually.
Scale, which illustrates the scale of the map in either kilometers or miles in the bottom-left of the map.
The unit is determined by the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Formatting locale__TRILIUM_PH_1__ option in __TRILIUM_PH_2__Language & Region__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

The name of the markers is displayed by default underneath the pin on the map. Since v0.102.0, it is possible to hide these labels which increases the performance and decreases clutter when there are many markers on the map.
v0.105.0 also introduces a feature called __TRILIUM_PH_0__Group nearby markers__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which will cluster multiple markers together at low zoom.
The clusters display the number of items they contain. The color also changes based on the count.
Clicking on a cluster will automatically zoom in so that the individual markers that make up the cluster are now visible.

The same options are also listed under __TRILIUM_PH_0__General__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_2____TRILIUM_PH_3__Geo map properties__TRILIUM_PH_4__ dialog, opened from the __TRILIUM_PH_5__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_6__ or from the settings menu of the __TRILIUM_PH_7__Collection Properties__TRILIUM_PH_8__. Its __TRILIUM_PH_9__Included notes__TRILIUM_PH_10__ section sets whether archived notes are shown and the __TRILIUM_PH_11__Maximum nesting depth__TRILIUM_PH_12__ (see below), and its __TRILIUM_PH_13__Background__TRILIUM_PH_14__ section holds the map style, the URL of a custom tile set when __TRILIUM_PH_15__Type__TRILIUM_PH_16__ is set to __TRILIUM_PH_17__Custom tileset__TRILIUM_PH_18__ (see above), or, with __TRILIUM_PH_19__Type__TRILIUM_PH_20__ set to __TRILIUM_PH_21__Custom image__TRILIUM_PH_22__, draws the map over an image of your own instead, as described in __TRILIUM_PH_23__Image maps__TRILIUM_PH_24__.

The map shows the notes of its whole subtree, not only its children. __TRILIUM_PH_0__Maximum nesting depth__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) limits how deep below the map it looks: __TRILIUM_PH_3__ shows only the children, __TRILIUM_PH_4__ adds their children, and so on. Without a value, every level is shown.
The Presentation view allows the creation of slideshows directly from within Trilium.

Right click on an existing note in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and select __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert child note__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Collection__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Presentation__TRILIUM_PH_7__.

A presentation without slides shows, in place of the slides and the slide sidebar, a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__New slide__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button that creates the first slide and starts editing it. The arrow beside it creates a slide of another type instead, as described below. A read-only presentation shows only a message that it has no slides. Until there is a slide, the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Slide sidebar__TRILIUM_PH_4__ button is disabled and the controls below the slides are not shown.
Each slide is a child note of the collection.

The slides are not shown in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ by default, since the slide sidebar already lists them (see __TRILIUM_PH_2__Hiding the subtree__TRILIUM_PH_3__). To show them, open the collection's __TRILIUM_PH_4__ settings and turn off __TRILIUM_PH_5__Hide child notes in tree__TRILIUM_PH_6__.
The order of the child notes determines the order of the slides.
Unlike traditional presentation software, slides can be laid out both horizontally and vertically (see below for more information).
Direct children will be laid out horizontally and the children of those will be laid out vertically. Children deeper than two levels of nesting are ignored.

A __TRILIUM_PH_0__Kanban Board__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Table__TRILIUM_PH_3__ collection is shown as one slide, working as it does in the note itself, so its children are not laid out as vertical slides. Other collections keep their children as vertical slides.

Slides have a fixed 16:9 shape (1280×720). The preview in the note is a scaled-down copy of what is shown in full-screen, so content that fits in the preview fits when presenting. When the window or the screen has a different shape, the slide is centered with bars around it.
A slide whose content is larger than the slide is zoomed out until it fits, text included. To keep the text large, split the content over several slides.

units.context: Presentation > Interaction and navigation > Slide sidebar

units.source: A sidebar to the left of the slides shows a thumbnail of every slide in the presentation's theme, with vertical slides indented under the slide they belong to. Web view, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Kanban Board__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Table__TRILIUM_PH_3__ slides are shown as an icon.
units.context: Presentation > Interaction and navigation > Slide sidebar

units.source: The slide being shown is outlined, and the sidebar scrolls to keep it in view.
units.context: Presentation > Interaction and navigation > Slide sidebar

units.context: Presentation > Interaction and navigation > Slide sidebar

units.source: To move a slide, drag its thumbnail; a line shows where it goes. Dragged straight up or down, a slide keeps its level:
units.context: Presentation > Interaction and navigation > Slide sidebar

units.source: A top-level slide takes its vertical slides with it, and dragged over another slide's vertical slides it goes after that whole stack.
units.context: Presentation > Interaction and navigation > Slide sidebar

units.source: A vertical slide can go among the vertical slides of any slide. Dropped below a slide that has none, it becomes that slide's first vertical slide, and the line is indented.
units.context: Presentation > Interaction and navigation > Slide sidebar

units.source: To change a slide's level, drag it to the side as well: to the right to make it a vertical slide, to the left to make it a top-level slide. The line's indent shows the level it will have.

units.source: A slide that has vertical slides of its own can't become a vertical slide, and a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Kanban Board__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Table__TRILIUM_PH_3__ slide can't take vertical slides.

units.source: Press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__↑__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_5__+__TRILIUM_PH_6__↓__TRILIUM_PH_7__ to move the slide up or down at its level, past a whole stack of vertical slides. Press __TRILIUM_PH_8__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_9__+__TRILIUM_PH_10__→__TRILIUM_PH_11__ to make it a vertical slide where it stands, and __TRILIUM_PH_12__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_13__+__TRILIUM_PH_14__←__TRILIUM_PH_15__ to make it a top-level slide (the other way around in right-to-left languages). units.source: Double-click a slide made from a text note to edit it directly on the slide, in the presentation's theme. A dashed outline marks the slide being edited, and the formatting toolbar appears next to the selected text. Changes are saved as you type, as in any text note, and a slide that grows past the edge of the slide is zoomed out to fit.
units.context: Presentation > Editing a slide in place

units.source: To finish editing, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_1__, press the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ __TRILIUM_PH_3__Finish editing__TRILIUM_PH_4__ button below the slides or go to another slide. units.source: A __TRILIUM_PH_0__Kanban Board__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Table__TRILIUM_PH_3__ slide is read-only until it is edited, so that a card or a cell can't be changed by accident while presenting, and clicking a card or a row opens nothing. Double-click it to edit it on the slide as in its note, then press the __TRILIUM_PH_4__ __TRILIUM_PH_5__Finish editing__TRILIUM_PH_6__ button or go to another slide to finish. The bar above the collection has no view type switcher on a slide, and shows the __TRILIUM_PH_7__ settings only while the slide is edited.
units.context: Presentation > Editing a slide in place

units.source: Double-click a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Canvas__TRILIUM_PH_1__ slide to draw on it in place. The canvas editor covers the presentation, with the same tools as in the canvas note, and opens on the drawing at the size and place that the slide shows it. The drawing is saved as you go. Press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or the __TRILIUM_PH_4__ __TRILIUM_PH_5__Finish editing__TRILIUM_PH_6__ button to finish.

A __TRILIUM_PH_5__read-only__TRILIUM_PH_6__ presentation can't be edited in place, and neither can a slide whose own note is read-only.
