units.source: Unlike traditional presentation software such as Microsoft PowerPoint, the slides in Trilium can be laid out horizontally or vertically in order to create depth or better organize the slides by topic.
This horizontal/vertical organization affects transitions (especially on the “slide” transition), however it is most noticeable in navigation.

Pressing __TRILIUM_PH_0__←__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__→__TRILIUM_PH_3__ will navigate through slides horizontally, thus skipping vertical notes under the current slide. This is useful to skip entire chapters/related slides.
Pressing __TRILIUM_PH_0__↑__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__↓__TRILIUM_PH_3__ will navigate through the vertical slides at the current level.

Pressing __TRILIUM_PH_0__Space__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_3__ + __TRILIUM_PH_4__Space__TRILIUM_PH_5__ will go to the next/previous slide in order, regardless of the direction. This is generally the key combination to use when presenting.

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Previous slide__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Next slide__TRILIUM_PH_3__ buttons below the slides go in order, as __TRILIUM_PH_4__Space__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and __TRILIUM_PH_6__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_7__+__TRILIUM_PH_8__Space__TRILIUM_PH_9__ do.
All direct children of the collection will be laid out horizontally. If a direct child also has children, those children will be placed as vertical slides.
In the following example, the note structure is as follows:
At collection level, it's possible to adjust:

The theme of the entire presentation to one of the predefined themes by going to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collection Properties__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and looking for the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Theme__TRILIUM_PH_3__ option.
It's currently not possible to create custom themes, although it is planned.
Note that it is note possible to alter the CSS via __TRILIUM_PH_0__Custom app-wide CSS__TRILIUM_PH_1__ because the slides are rendered isolated (in a shadow DOM).

To change the background color of a slide, go to it and use the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Slide background__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button in the toolbar, or set __TRILIUM_PH_3__ on its note to a hex color.
More complex backgrounds can be achieved via gradients. There's no UI for it; it has to be set via __TRILIUM_PH_0__ to a CSS gradient definition such as: __TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Text notes generally respect the formatting (bold, italic, foreground and background colors) and font size. Code blocks and tables also work.

Try using more than just text notes, the presentation uses the same mechanism as __TRILIUM_PH_0__shared notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note List__TRILIUM_PH_3__ so it should be able to display __TRILIUM_PH_4__Mermaid Diagrams__TRILIUM_PH_5__, __TRILIUM_PH_6__Canvas__TRILIUM_PH_7__ and __TRILIUM_PH_8__Mind Map__TRILIUM_PH_9__ in full-screen (without the interactivity).
A __TRILIUM_PH_0__Canvas__TRILIUM_PH_1__ takes on the light or dark style of the theme, or of the slide's own background color.

A __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note fills the width of the slide, highlighted as in the note. With the code theme following the app's, the slide uses the light or the dark code theme to match the presentation's theme. Long code is zoomed out to fit the slide.
For __TRILIUM_PH_0__Mermaid Diagrams__TRILIUM_PH_1__, some of them have a predefined background which can be changed via the frontmatter. For example, for XY-charts:

A __TRILIUM_PH_0__Web View__TRILIUM_PH_1__ slide shows its page across the whole slide, and the page can be scrolled and its links clicked. The keyboard stays with the presentation, so __TRILIUM_PH_2__Space__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and the arrow keys still change slides after clicking the page; to type into the page, open the web view note itself. Only __TRILIUM_PH_4__ and __TRILIUM_PH_5__ addresses are shown. It works the same way as the web view note itself, so outside the desktop application some websites refuse to be shown.
The Presentation view uses __TRILIUM_PH_0__Reveal.js__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to handle the navigation and layout of the slides.
This view presents the child notes in a grid format, allowing for a more visual navigation experience.
For empty notes, the sub-children are also displayed, allowing for quick navigation.
Depending on the type of note:
For __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes, the text can be slightly scrollable via the mouse wheel to reveal more context.
For __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes, syntax highlighting is applied, with line numbers as in the editor.
For __TRILIUM_PH_0__File__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes, a preview is made available for audio, video and PDF notes.
If the note does not have a content, a list of its child notes will be displayed instead.
The grid view is also used by default in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note List__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of every note, making it easy to navigate to children notes.

List view is similar to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Grid View__TRILIUM_PH_1__, but in the list view mode, each note is displayed in a single row with only the title and the icon of the note being visible by the default. By pressing the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ expand button it's possible to view the content of the note, as well as the children of the note (recursively).
In the example above, the "Node.js" note on the left panel contains several child notes. The right panel displays the content of these child notes as a single continuous document.

The dashboard is currently considered beta. This means that it might face some changes in behavior until it is stabilized.
The dashboard is a collection introduced in Trilium v0.104.0. It is similar to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Grid View__TRILIUM_PH_1__ collection, but with some key differences:
The grid layout is not fixed, allowing for tiles of varying widths and heights. The grid has 12 columns and an unlimited number of rows.
Each widget represents a child note of the collection and can be reordered or resized.
The grid will distribute the columns evenly to fill the entire screen.
If the available space is too low (e.g. in a split or in mobile), the columns are collapsed so that all widgets are displayed one under the other.
While the columns are collapsed, the widgets cannot be reordered or resized.
Unlike the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Grid View__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the widgets are not clickable which allows them to be interactive.
The dashboard uses the same rendering mechanism as the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Grid View__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note List__TRILIUM_PH_3__, which means every note can be rendered, such as:
Web pages can be displayed via __TRILIUM_PH_0__Web View__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and refreshed via the context menu.

Interactive widgets through the use of __TRILIUM_PH_0__Render Note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is the highlighted use case of the dashboard. Using the __TRILIUM_PH_2__AI__TRILIUM_PH_3__ chat, these widgets can be easily created as the AI is instructed in how to write them.
There are two ways to add widgets to a dashboard:
Create a child note of any type, the dashboard will automatically pick it up and add it onto the grid.
From the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__, drag an existing note onto the dashboard and it will be placed there. This will __TRILIUM_PH_2__clone__TRILIUM_PH_3__ the note into the collection.

On a __TRILIUM_PH_0__read-only__TRILIUM_PH_1__ dashboard, the widgets can't be moved or resized, notes dragged from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_3__ aren't added, and the menu of a widget no longer offers to remove it.
Collections are a unique type of note that don't have content, but instead display their child notes in various presentation methods.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Calendar__TRILIUM_PH_1__ displays a week, month or year calendar with the notes being shown as events. New events can be added easily by dragging across the calendar.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Table__TRILIUM_PH_1__ displays each note as a row in a table, with __TRILIUM_PH_2__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_3__ being shown as well. This makes it easy to visualize attributes of notes, as well as making them easily editable.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Kanban Board__TRILIUM_PH_1__ displays notes in columns, grouped by the value of a label. Items and columns can easily be created or dragged around to change their status.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Geo Map__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which displays a geographical map in which the notes are represented as pins on the map. New markers can be easily added by pointing on the map. In addition __TRILIUM_PH_2__shapes__TRILIUM_PH_3__ such as paths, rectangles and circles can be added, as well as GPX tracks.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Presentation__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which shows each note as a slide and can be presented full-screen with smooth transitions or exported to PDF for sharing.

Classic collections are read-only mode and compiles the contents of all child notes into one continuous view. This makes it ideal for reading extensive information broken into smaller, manageable segments.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Grid View__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which is the default presentation method for child notes (see __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note List__TRILIUM_PH_3__), where the notes are displayed as tiles with their title and content being visible.

In certain scenarios, understanding the structure of a database is crucial for troubleshooting issues. However, sharing your actual __TRILIUM_PH_0__database__TRILIUM_PH_1__ file with personal notes is not advisable. To address this, Trilium offers a feature to anonymize the database. This feature can be accessed via Menu -> Options -> Advanced tab.

This feature creates a copy of your database with all sensitive data removed. Specifically, it strips out note titles, contents, revisions, history, and some non-system attributes while retaining the overall structure and metadata, such as modification dates. After anonymization, the database undergoes a __TRILIUM_PH_0__vacuuming process__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to ensure no sensitive data remnants remain in the file. The anonymized database is saved in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ directory within the __TRILIUM_PH_3__data directory__TRILIUM_PH_4__, making it safe to share with bug reports.

This will create a copy of your document and remove all sensitive data (currently note titles, contents, revisions, history and some of the options, and non-system attributes) while leaving all structure and metadata (e.g. date of last change). After this is done, the database is __TRILIUM_PH_0__VACUUMed__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to make sure there's no stale sensitive data in the document file. The resulting file is stored in __TRILIUM_PH_2__ directory (placed in the __TRILIUM_PH_3__data directory__TRILIUM_PH_4__). You can safely attach it to a bug report.

units.source: The manifest is a JSON object with an __TRILIUM_PH_0__ map. Each entry key is the CSS/class id you will use (Trilium uses the CSS class when rendering). Value object:

Inheritance refers to the process of having a __TRILIUM_PH_0__label__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or a __TRILIUM_PH_2__relation__TRILIUM_PH_3__ shared across multiple notes, generally in parent-child relations (or anywhere if using templates).

In Trilium, attributes can be automatically inherited by child notes if they have the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ flag set to __TRILIUM_PH_1__. This means the attribute (a key-value pair) is applied to the note and all its descendants.

To make an attribute inheritable, simply use the visual editor for __TRILIUM_PH_0__Labels__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Relations__TRILIUM_PH_3__. Alternatively, the attribute can be manually defined where __TRILIUM_PH_4__ becomes __TRILIUM_PH_5__ when inheritable.
As an example, the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ label can be set to be inheritable, allowing you to hide a whole subtree of notes from searches and other dialogs by applying this label at the top level.

Standard inheritance forces all the notes that are children (and sub-children) of a note to have that particular label or relation. If there is a need to have some notes not inherit one of the labels, then __TRILIUM_PH_0__copying inheritance__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__template inheritance__TRILIUM_PH_3__ needs to be used instead.

Copying inheritance differs from standard inheritance by using a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ prefix in the attribute name. This prefix causes new child notes to automatically receive specific attributes from the parent note. These attributes are independent of the parent and will persist even if the note is moved elsewhere.

If a parent note has the label __TRILIUM_PH_0__, all newly created child notes (one level deep) will inherit the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ label. This can be useful for setting default properties for notes in a specific section.
Due to the way it's designed, copying inheritance cannot be used to cascade infinitely within a hierarchy. For that use case, consider using either standard inheritance or templates.

Promoted attributes are __TRILIUM_PH_0__attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which are displayed prominently in the UI which allow them to be easily viewed and edited.

The promoted attributes are shown underneath the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Title__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of the note, in a collapsible section. For full-height notes such as __TRILIUM_PH_2__Canvas__TRILIUM_PH_3__, the promoted attributes are collapsed by default to make room.
One way of seeing promoted attributes is as a kind of form with several fields. Each field is just regular attribute, the only difference is that they appear on the note itself.

Attributes can be pretty useful since they allow for querying and script automation etc. but they are also inconveniently hidden. This allows you to select few of the important ones and push them to the front of the user.
In order to have promoted attributes, there needs to be a way to define them.
Technically, attributes are only name-value pairs where both name and value are strings.
The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Attribute definition__TRILIUM_PH_1__ specifies how should this value be interpreted:
Is it just string, or is it a date?
Should we allow multiple values or note?
Should we __TRILIUM_PH_0__promote__TRILIUM_PH_1__ the attribute or not?
Attribute definitions have a dedicated type field which will change how the value will be edited in the promoted attributes section.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the default option which allows any type of text to be edited, similar to normal labels that don't have a type associated.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Multi-line text__TRILIUM_PH_1__, similar to a normal text field, but rendered in a bigger text box that also supports writing on multiple lines.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Number__TRILIUM_PH_1__, will display as a number input field with up/down arrows.
Optionally a __TRILIUM_PH_0__precision__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which sets how many decimals the value steps by and is displayed with.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Checkbox__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which renders as a checkbox for a true/false value. In the label definition, this type is written as __TRILIUM_PH_2__.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Select,__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which provides a list of user-defined options when editing.
The list is not fixed, meaning that new options can be easily added from the promoted attribute.
Renaming an option does not change the existing values since the value is stored as text. Consider a __TRILIUM_PH_0__bulk rename__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

The items do not have a custom color or icon. This is intentional as selects are meant to be light-weight. For a more customizable option, consider using __TRILIUM_PH_0__Relations__TRILIUM_PH_1__ instead which use notes as items and those notes can be colorized and also carry an icon.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Date & Time,__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which provides a date & time picker.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__URL,__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which provides a button to open the web address in a new window.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Email__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which provides a button to quickly send an email to that address using your operating system's default app.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Phone__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which provides a button to quickly call that number using your operating system's default app.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Color__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which provides a color picker and a way to remove the value.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Relation__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which points to another note and uses __TRILIUM_PH_2__Relations__TRILIUM_PH_3__ instead of __TRILIUM_PH_4__Labels__TRILIUM_PH_5__.

For label-based attributes, these types are not enforced by the attribute system, meaning that changing the type afterwards does not guarantee that the values in it correspond to the type (e.g. turning a text into a number).
When the definition allows multiple values, each value is shown as a chip and a new one is added in the box after them. Press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ on a chip to remove that value.

For free-form types such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Number__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Date__TRILIUM_PH_5__, press __TRILIUM_PH_6__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_7__ (or leave the field) to add what was typed. The same value can be added more than once, for example two payments of the same amount.

For __TRILIUM_PH_0__Select__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Checkbox__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Relation__TRILIUM_PH_5__ attributes, a value is picked from the list rather than typed, and each one can be picked only once.

units.source: When a new promoted attribute definition is created, it creates a corresponding label prefixed with either __TRILIUM_PH_0__ or __TRILIUM_PH_1__, depending on the definition type:

units.source: It's possible to create promoted attributes out of system attributes, to be able to easily alter them.
Here are a few practical examples:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_1__ already make use of this practice, for example:
Calendars add “Start Date”, “End Date”, “Start Time” and “End Time” as promoted attributes. These map to system attributes such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ which are then interpreted by the calendar view.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Presentation__TRILIUM_PH_1__ adds a “Background” promoted attribute for each of the slide to easily be able to customize.

The Trilium documentation (which is edited in Trilium) uses a promoted attribute to be able to easily edit the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ (see __TRILIUM_PH_1__Sharing__TRILIUM_PH_2__) in order to form clean URLs.
If you always edit a particular system attribute such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__, simply create a promoted attribute for it to make it easier.

units.context: Promoted Attributes > Using system attributes > Inverse relation

units.source: Some relations always occur in pairs - my favorite example is on the family. If you have a note representing husband and note representing wife, then there might be a relation between those two of __TRILIUM_PH_0__. This is bidirectional relationship - meaning that if a relation is pointing from husband to wife then there should be always another relation pointing from wife to husband.
units.context: Promoted Attributes > Using system attributes > Inverse relation

units.source: Another example is with parent-child relationship. Again these always occur in pairs, but in this case it's not exact same relation - the one going from parent to child might be called __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and the other one going from child to parent might be called __TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Promoted Attributes > Using system attributes > Inverse relation

units.source: Relation definition allows you to specify such "inverse relation" - for the relation you just define you specify which is the inverse relation. Note that in the second example we should have two relation definitions - one for __TRILIUM_PH_0__ which defines __TRILIUM_PH_1__ as inverse relation and then second relation definition for __TRILIUM_PH_2__ which defines __TRILIUM_PH_3__ as inverse relation.
units.context: Promoted Attributes > Using system attributes > Inverse relation

units.source: What this does internally is that whenever we save a relation which has defined inverse relation, we check that this inverse relation exists on the relation target note. Similarly, when we delete relation, we also delete inverse relation on the target note.
units.context: Promoted Attributes > Using system attributes > Inverse relation

units.source: The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Table__TRILIUM_PH_1__ collection makes heavy use of promoted attributes to define the columns of the table, since they already carry the type information. When made inheritable, it's also easy to change those fields when the child notes are opened.
In Trilium, attributes are key-value pairs assigned to notes, providing additional metadata or functionality. There are two primary types of attributes:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Labels__TRILIUM_PH_1__ can be used for a variety of purposes, such as storing metadata or configuring the behavior of notes. Labels are also searchable, enhancing note retrieval.
For more information, including predefined labels, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Labels__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Relations__TRILIUM_PH_1__ define connections between notes, similar to links. These can be used for metadata and scripting purposes.
For more information, including a list of predefined relations, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Relations__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
These attributes play a crucial role in organizing, categorizing, and enhancing the functionality of notes.
Conceptually there are two types of attributes (applying to both labels and relations):

__TRILIUM_PH_0__System attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1____TRILIUM_PH_2__As the name suggest, these attributes have a special meaning since they are interpreted by Trilium. For example the __TRILIUM_PH_3__ attribute will change the color of the note as displayed in the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and links, and __TRILIUM_PH_6__ will change the icon of a note.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__User-defined attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1____TRILIUM_PH_2__These are free-form labels or relations that can be used by the user. They can be used purely for categorization purposes (especially if combined with __TRILIUM_PH_3__Search__TRILIUM_PH_4__), or they can be given meaning through the use of __TRILIUM_PH_5__Scripting__TRILIUM_PH_6__.

In practice, Trilium makes no direct distinction of whether an attribute is a system one or a user-defined one. A label or relation is considered a system attribute if it matches one of the built-in names (e.g. like the aforementioned __TRILIUM_PH_0__). Keep this in mind when creating  __TRILIUM_PH_1__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_2__ in order not to accidentally alter a system attribute (unless intended).

units.source: Attributes in Trilium can be "multi-valued", meaning multiple attributes with the same name can co-exist. This can be combined with __TRILIUM_PH_0__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to easily add them.

A template in Trilium serves as a predefined structure for other notes, referred to as instance notes. Assigning a template to a note brings three main effects:

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Attribute Inheritance__TRILIUM_PH_1__: All attributes from the template note are __TRILIUM_PH_2__inherited__TRILIUM_PH_3__ by the instance notes. Even attributes with __TRILIUM_PH_4__ are inherited by the instance notes, although only inheritable attributes are further inherited by the children of the instance notes.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Content Duplication__TRILIUM_PH_1__: The content of the template note is copied to the instance note, provided the instance note is empty at the time of template assignment.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Child Note Duplication__TRILIUM_PH_1__: All child notes of the template are deep-duplicated to the instance note.
A typical example would be a "Book" template note, which might include:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__: Such as publication year, author, etc. (see __TRILIUM_PH_2__promoted attributes__TRILIUM_PH_3__).
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Outline__TRILIUM_PH_1__: An outline for a book review, including sections like themes, conclusion, etc.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Child Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__: Additional notes for highlights, summary, etc.
An instance note is a note related to a template note. This relationship means the instance note's content is initialized from the template, and all attributes from the template are inherited.
To create an instance note through the UI:

For the template to appear in the menu, the template note must have the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ label. Do not confuse this with the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ relation, which links the instance note to the template note. If you use __TRILIUM_PH_2__workspaces__TRILIUM_PH_3__, you can also mark templates with __TRILIUM_PH_4__ to display them only in the workspace.
Templates can also be added or changed after note creation by creating a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ relation pointing to the desired template note.

To specify a template for child notes, you can use a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ relation pointing to the appropriate template note. There is no limit to the depth of the hierarchy — you can use __TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__, and so on.

Changing the template hierarchy after the parent note is created will not retroactively apply to newly created child notes.__TRILIUM_PH_0__For example, if you initially use __TRILIUM_PH_1__ and later switch to __TRILIUM_PH_2__, it will not automatically apply the new template to the grandchild notes. Only the structure present at the time of note creation is considered.

units.context: Templates > Default parent for new notes

units.source: A template can gather the notes created from it in one place, instead of having them land wherever they happen to be created. To do so, add a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ relation to the template note, pointing at the note that should hold the instances, for example a __TRILIUM_PH_1__Person__TRILIUM_PH_2__ template pointing to a __TRILIUM_PH_3__People__TRILIUM_PH_4__ note. The relation can also be set by clicking the template badge next to the note title and selecting __TRILIUM_PH_5__Template properties...__TRILIUM_PH_6__, then picking a note under __TRILIUM_PH_7__Default location of created notes__TRILIUM_PH_8__.
units.context: Templates > Default parent for new notes

units.source: Adding the relation several times places the new note in every target, as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Cloning Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__. The relation can also be inherited (e.g. from a folder holding several templates), in which case a relation owned by the template itself replaces the inherited one. The default parent is only inherited from the template's ancestors in the tree: a template created from another template does not adopt that template's default parent.

units.source: Unlike the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Inbox__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which holds quickly captured notes until they are sorted, the default parent is meant as the instances' permanent location.

units.source: By default, newly created notes are __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes. If a parent note defines a __TRILIUM_PH_2__ pointing to a template of a different type (e.g. a Code note), the behavior depends on how the new note is created:
If no note type is explicitly chosen (e.g. the + button in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__), the template is applied and the new note takes the type and content of the template.
If a note type is explicitly selected (e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert note after__TRILIUM_PH_3__ / __TRILIUM_PH_4__Insert child note__TRILIUM_PH_5__):
If the selected type matches the template's type, the template is applied.
If the selected type differs, the template is disregarded entirely — the new note is an empty note of the selected type.
Selecting a specific template from the creation menu always takes precedence over __TRILIUM_PH_0__.

units.source: A template can also give its instances a default title, using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ label. To set it without editing the label by hand, click the template badge next to the note title and select __TRILIUM_PH_1__Template properties...__TRILIUM_PH_2__, which checks the expressions as you type and previews the resulting title. See __TRILIUM_PH_3__Default Note Title__TRILIUM_PH_4__ for details.
units.context: Templates > Default title for new notes

units.source: From a visual perspective, templates can define __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and __TRILIUM_PH_1__ attributes, allowing all instance notes (e.g., books) to display a specific icon and CSS style.

Explore the concept further in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Demo Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__, including examples like the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Relation Map__TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__Task Manager__TRILIUM_PH_5__, and __TRILIUM_PH_6__Day Notes__TRILIUM_PH_7__.

Additionally, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Default Note Title__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for creating title templates. A __TRILIUM_PH_2__ on a template note is passed on to its instances like any other label, so it names the children of each instance rather than the instances themselves; to name the instances, use __TRILIUM_PH_3__.

units.source: As described in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Sharing__TRILIUM_PH_1__, Trilium can act as a public server in which the shared notes are displayed in read-only mode. While this can work in most cases, it's generally not meant for high-traffic websites and since it's running on a Node.js server it can be potentially exploited.
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing

units.source: Another alternative is to generate static HTML files (just like other static site generators such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__MkDocs__TRILIUM_PH_1__). Since the normal HTML ZIP export does not contain any styling or additional functionality, Trilium provides a way to export the same layout and style as the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Sharing__TRILIUM_PH_3__ function into static HTML files.
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing

units.source: Apart from the enhanced security, these HTML files are also easy to deploy on “serverless” deployments such as GitHub Pages or CloudFlare Pages and cache very easily.
units.context: Exporting static HTML for web publishing

This topic of creating share templates is considered advanced and requires JavaScript/EJS knowledge.
The default share template should cover most normal uses.
For full control over the HTML structure of a shared page — beyond what custom CSS, JS, or HTML snippets allow — you can replace the page template entirely using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ relation.
Create a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note with the language __TRILIUM_PH_2__Embedded JavaScript__TRILIUM_PH_3__ (EJS).

For a shared note to apply the newly created template, apply the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ relation pointing to the note created at step (1). Make use of __TRILIUM_PH_1__Attribute Inheritance__TRILIUM_PH_2__ to apply it to multiple shared notes.
There are two important constraints to be aware of:

Because EJS templates execute arbitrary server-side JavaScript, __TRILIUM_PH_0__ only takes effect when backend scripting is enabled. units.source: To use the sharing feature, you must have a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Server Installation__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of Trilium. This is necessary because the notes will be hosted from the server.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Enable Sharing__TRILIUM_PH_1__: To share a note, toggle the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ switch within the note's interface. Once sharing is enabled, an URL will appear, which you can click to access the shared note.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Access the Shared Note__TRILIUM_PH_1__: The link provided will open the note in your browser. If your server is not configured with a public IP, the URL will refer to __TRILIUM_PH_2__.

When you share a note, you actually share the entire subtree of notes beneath it. If the note has child notes, they will also be included in the shared content. For example, sharing the "Formatting" subtree will display a page with basic navigation for exploring all the notes within that subtree.

units.source: You can view a list of all shared notes by clicking on __TRILIUM_PH_0__Advanced__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Shared notes__TRILIUM_PH_3__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Global menu__TRILIUM_PH_5__. This allows you to manage and navigate through all the notes you have made public.

units.source: Shared notes are published on the open internet and can be accessed by anyone with the URL unless the notes are password-protected.
The URL's randomness does not provide security, so it is crucial not to share sensitive information through this feature.

Trilium takes precautions to protect your publicly shared instance from leaking information for non-shared notes, including opening a separate read-only connection to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Database__TRILIUM_PH_1__. Depending on your threat model, it might make more sense to use __TRILIUM_PH_2__Exporting static HTML for web publishing__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and use battle-tested web servers such as Nginx or Apache to serve static content.

To protect shared notes with a username and password, you can use the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ attribute. Add this label to the note with the format __TRILIUM_PH_1__. To protect an entire subtree, make sure the label is __TRILIUM_PH_2__inheritable__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

A common pattern in note-taking is that a lot of notes will be centered around a certain date - e.g. you have some tasks which needs to be done on a certain date, you have meeting minutes from a certain date, you have your thoughts etc. and it all revolves around a date on which they occurred. For this reason, it makes sense to create a certain "day workspace" which will centralize all those notes relevant for a certain date.
For this, Trilium provides a concept of "day note". Trilium semi-automatically generates a single note for each day. Under this note you can save all those relevant notes.
Select an existing day note, and the menubar contains a calendar widget. Select any day to create a note for that day.

This pattern works well also because of __TRILIUM_PH_0__Cloning Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ functionality - note can appear in multiple places in the note tree, so besides appearing under day note, it can also be categorized into other notes.

You can see the structure of day notes appearing under "Journal" note - there's a note for the whole year 2025, under it, you have "03 - March" which then contains "09 - Monday". This is our "day note" which contains some text in its content and also has some child notes (some of them are from __TRILIUM_PH_0__Task manager__TRILIUM_PH_1__).

You can also notice how this day note has __TRILIUM_PH_0__promoted attribute__TRILIUM_PH_1__ "weight" where you can track your daily weight. This data is then used in __TRILIUM_PH_2__Weight tracker__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
When a day note is opened, a collapsible section will appear underneath the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Title__TRILIUM_PH_1__ showing the notes edited on that day.

ETAPI is Trilium's public/external REST API. It is available since Trilium v0.50.
As an alternative to calling the API directly, there are client libraries to simplify this
__TRILIUM_PH_0__trilium-py__TRILIUM_PH_1__, you can use Python to communicate with Trilium.

All operations with the REST API have to be authenticated using a token. You can get this token either from __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__ETAPI__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or programmatically using the __TRILIUM_PH_4__ REST call (see the __TRILIUM_PH_5__spec__TRILIUM_PH_6__). With __TRILIUM_PH_7__multi-factor authentication__TRILIUM_PH_8__ enabled, __TRILIUM_PH_9__ also needs the one-time password or a recovery code in __TRILIUM_PH_10__.

A token stays valid until it is deleted in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__ETAPI__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or through __TRILIUM_PH_4__. Changing the password does not revoke it, including a token obtained through __TRILIUM_PH_5__, so a script keeps working after a password change.

When a new note is created, its name is by default "new note". In some cases, it can be desirable to have a different or even a dynamic default note title.

For this use case, Trilium (since v0.52) supports __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__label__TRILIUM_PH_2__. You can create such a label for a given note, assign it a value, and this value will be used as a default title when creating child notes. As with other labels, you can make it inheritable to apply recursively, and you can even place it on the root note to have it applied globally everywhere.
As an example use case, imagine you collect books you've read in a given year like this:
Now, to the parent note "2022 Books" you can assign label __TRILIUM_PH_0__.

And all children of "2022 Books" will be created with initial title "[Author name]: [Book title], [Publication year]". There's no artificial intelligence here, the idea is to just prompt you to manually fill in the pieces of information into the note title by yourself.

units.source: The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Bulk Actions__TRILIUM_PH_1__ dialog makes it easy to apply changes to multiple notes at once, ranging from simple actions such as adding or removing a label to being executing custom scripts.
The first step is to select the notes in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__. It's possible to apply bulk actions to:
A single note (and potentially its child notes) simply by clicking on it (with a left click or a right click).
Multiple notes. See __TRILIUM_PH_0__Multiple selection__TRILIUM_PH_1__ on how to do so.
Right click in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and select __TRILIUM_PH_2__Advanced__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Apply bulk actions__TRILIUM_PH_5__.

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Selected notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section at the top of the dialog lists the notes the actions apply to. When many notes are selected, only the first few are shown; click __TRILIUM_PH_2__+N more__TRILIUM_PH_3__ to show the rest.
To leave a note out without changing the selection in the note tree, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button on its entry. The last remaining note cannot be removed.

By default, only the selected notes will be affected. To also include all the descendants of the notes, turn on __TRILIUM_PH_0__Include descendants of the selected notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__. The number of affected notes, shown below that option, updates to reflect the change.

To add an action, click __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add action__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) at the bottom of the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Chosen actions__TRILIUM_PH_4__ section and pick one from the menu. Hovering over an entry shows a short description of what it does; a detailed description of each is available in the next section.
Each chosen action appears as an entry in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Chosen actions__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section, with its own configuration.
To remove an action, simply press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button to the right of it.
It is possible to apply multiple actions of the same type, such as adding multiple types.
The fields for a label or relation name suggest the names already used in the database as you type, marking the ones Trilium itself attaches a meaning to.
The value field of __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add label__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Update label value__TRILIUM_PH_3__ suggests the values the named label already has in the database.

When all the actions are defined, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Apply to N notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button to trigger all of them at once. The button names the number of notes that will be affected, and stays disabled until at least one action is added.
If an action is missing a field it needs, such as the name of the label to rename, the dialog does not run and points out the empty field instead.
For convenience, the last bulk action configuration is saved for further use and will be restored when entering the dialog again.

These actions operate the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Labels__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of a note. Except for __TRILIUM_PH_2__Add label__TRILIUM_PH_3__, they only affect labels set directly on the note; inherited labels are left unchanged.

For each note, it creates a __TRILIUM_PH_0__label__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of the given name. Keep the __TRILIUM_PH_2__New value__TRILIUM_PH_3__ field empty to create a label without a value, or complete it to assign a value.

The label is added even if the note already has one of the same name, so the note ends up with both. To change the value of an existing label instead, use __TRILIUM_PH_0__Update label value__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

For each note, if it has a __TRILIUM_PH_0__label__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of the given name, it will change its value to the specified one. Leave __TRILIUM_PH_2__New value__TRILIUM_PH_3__ field empty to create a label without a value.
Notes without the label will not be affected.
For each note, if it has a __TRILIUM_PH_0__label__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of the given name, it will be renamed/replaced with a label of the new name. The value of the label (if present) will be kept intact.
Notes without the label will not be affected.
For each note, if it has a label of a given name, it will be deleted (regardless of whether it has a value or not).
Notes without the label will not be affected.

These actions operate the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Relations__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of a note. Except for __TRILIUM_PH_2__Add relation__TRILIUM_PH_3__, they only affect relations set directly on the note; inherited relations are left unchanged.
For each note, it will create a relation pointing to the given note.
The relation is added even if the note already has one of the same name.
For each note, it will modify a relation to point to the newly given note.
Notes without this relation will not be affected.
For each note, if it has a relation of the given name, it will be renamed/replaced with a relation of the new name. The target note of the relation will be kept intact.
Notes without this relation will not be affected.

units.source: The CKEditor is the WYSIWYG (standing for What You See Is What You Get) editor behind __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes.

CKEditor by itself is a commercial product, but the core is open-source. As described in __TRILIUM_PH_0__its documentation__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the editor supports quite a large number of features. Do note that not all the features are enabled in Trilium.

CKEditor ships some plugins as premium (slash commands, templates, AI integration). Initially Trilium (since v0.96.0) shipped some of them like slash commands as part of a license grant from CKEditor to the Trilium Notes developers.
In v0.105.0 we've decided to replace those premium plugins with our own open-source implementations. This also means that we can better tailor those plugins to the Trilium app.
The CKEditor ecosystem is quite extensible, in the sense that custom plugins can be written to extend the functionality of the editor beyond its original scope.
Trilium makes use of such features:
The math feature is added by a version of __TRILIUM_PH_0__isaul32/ckeditor5-math: Math feature for CKEditor 5.__TRILIUM_PH_1__ modified by us to fit our needs.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__mlewand/ckeditor5-keyboard-marker: Plugin adds support for the keyboard input element (__TRILIUM_PH_1__) to CKEditor 5.__TRILIUM_PH_2__
A modified version of __TRILIUM_PH_0__ThomasAitken/ckeditor5-footnotes: Footnotes plugin for CKEditor5__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to allow footnotes.
Apart from that, Trilium also has its own set of specific plugins such as:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Include Note__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which also shows drawing canvases and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Mermaid diagrams__TRILIUM_PH_3__ in place.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Admonitions__TRILIUM_PH_1__, we ended up creating our own plugin but __TRILIUM_PH_2__aarkue/ckeditor5-admonition__TRILIUM_PH_3__ was a good inspiration (including the toolbar icon).
One core aspect of Trilium that allows it to have support for multiple __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Types__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is the fact that it makes use of various off-the-shelf or reusable libraries.
This page showcases some of the technologies used, for a better understanding of how Trilium works but also to credit the developers of that particular technology.

CKEditor is the editor behind __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes, as well as integrated in various facets of the application such as the attribute editor in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Status bar__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or the chat box in the __TRILIUM_PH_4__AI__TRILIUM_PH_5__ sidebar or notes.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Excalidraw__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is the technology behind the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Canvas__TRILIUM_PH_3__ notes. The source code of the library is available on __TRILIUM_PH_4__GitHub__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
We are using an unmodified version of it, so it shares the same __TRILIUM_PH_0__issues__TRILIUM_PH_1__ as the original.

Trilium v0.105.0 introduces __TRILIUM_PH_0__MapLibre GL JS__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Geo Map__TRILIUM_PH_3__ collection, which brings improved performance by using graphical acceleration (WebGL). Trilium ships its own track parsing logic as well as most of the UI such as the right panel.
MindElixir is the library we are using for __TRILIUM_PH_0__Mind Map__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note types. The main library is available on __TRILIUM_PH_2__GitHub as mind-elixir-core__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
Trilium ships its own UI which covers the toolbars, the contextual menu, the zoom buttons and the right panel that shows when clicking a node.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__FullCalendar__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is the technology behind the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Calendar__TRILIUM_PH_3__ collection, providing the various views (day, week, month, year) and the event management. Trilium also ships its own UI in the form of the popup that appears when editing, as well as the header that appears in the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Collection Properties__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
Whereas some applications use file names to uniquely identify notes, Trilium uses the concept of Note ID.
Generally, the Note ID is a 12-character long alphanumeric sequence (including both lower and upper case letter) that is randomly generated for each new note.
How does the import/export affect the note IDs__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Note ID > How does the import/export affect the note IDs

units.source: When notes are exported, their note ID is kept in the metadata of the export. However when they are imported back in, a new note ID is generated for all the notes. This also includes other entities that are part of the import/export process such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Attachments__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Note ID > How does the import/export affect the note IDs

units.source: Since the Note ID is a fixed-width randomly generated number, due to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__pigeonhole principle__TRILIUM_PH_1__, there is a possibility that a newly created note will have the same ID as an existing note.

Since the note ID is alphanumeric and the length is 12 we have __TRILIUM_PH_0__ unique IDs. However since we are generating them randomly, we can use a collision calculator such as the one for __TRILIUM_PH_1__Nano ID__TRILIUM_PH_2__ to determine that we'd need to create 1000 notes per hour every hour for 9 centuries in order to have at least 1% probability of a note collision.

As such, Trilium does not take any explicit action against potential note collisions, similar to other software that makes uses of unique hashes such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Git__TRILIUM_PH_1__. If one would theoretically occur, what would most likely happen is that the existing note will be replaced by the new one.

units.source: For easy extensibility, a lot of features in Trilium make use of actual notes to store information as opposed to having them stored in a separate location in the database. This allows some functions such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Relations__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or even __TRILIUM_PH_4__Search__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and __TRILIUM_PH_6__Links__TRILIUM_PH_7__ to be able to operate on them.
As the name suggests, these notes are hidden to the user by default to prevent cluttering the note tree and to prevent them from being accidentally deleted.

The hidden notes are stored in the user's __TRILIUM_PH_0__Database__TRILIUM_PH_1__ just like normal notes, but they have a unique __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note ID__TRILIUM_PH_3__ which allows them to be distinguished from the normal ones.

Nightly releases are versions built every day, containing the latest improvements and bugfixes, directly from the main development branch. These versions are generally useful in preparation for a release, to ensure that there are no significant bugs that need to be addressed first, or they can be used to confirm whether a particular bug is fixed or feature is well implemented.

Despite being on a development branch, generally the main branch is pretty stable since PRs are tested before they are merged. If you notice any issues, feel free to report them either via a ticket or via the Matrix.

The read-only database is an alternative to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Sharing__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes. Although the share functionality works pretty well to publish pages to the Internet in a wiki, blog-like format it does not offer the full functionality behind Trilium (such as the advanced __TRILIUM_PH_2__Search__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or the interactivity behind __TRILIUM_PH_4__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_5__ or the various __TRILIUM_PH_6__Note Types__TRILIUM_PH_7__).
When the database is in read-only mode, the Trilium application can be used as normal, but editing is disabled and changes are made in-memory only.
All notes are read-only, without the possibility of editing them.
Features that would normally alter the database such as the list of recent notes are disabled.
Some features might “slip through” and still end up creating a note, for example.
However, the database is still read-only, so all modifications will be reset if the server is restarted.
Whenever this occurs, __TRILIUM_PH_0__ will be shown in the logs.

units.source: Optical Character Recognition is the process in which the text from images or PDFs is extracted.
Since v0.103.0, Trilium has built-in support for OCR. The extracted text can be:
Integrated with __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search__TRILIUM_PH_1__, to quickly find the image or file based on snippets of text.
Integrated with the __TRILIUM_PH_0__AI__TRILIUM_PH_1__ feature, which allows the agent to access the content of a non-text note.
Manually accessed for other purposes (e.g. copying into a note or sending it somewhere else).
OCR in Trilium supports the following formats:
Both __TRILIUM_PH_0__individual image notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__attachments in text files__TRILIUM_PH_3__ are supported.
Note that this feature works best for computer-rendered text rather than handwriting.
PDFs with text information (e.g. a PDF created by a browser or a word processing application), in which the text is extracted.
Scanned PDFs, and other PDFs whose text cannot be selected (such as documents whose text was converted to outlines), in which the text is extracted through an OCR process.
Mixed PDFs, containing both text and images with text content.
Note that OCR extraction is limited to 50 pages per PDF, pages containing text information (not as an image) are not subject to this limitation.

Text extraction for scanned PDFs using OCR was introduced in v0.106.0. If a scanned PDF was already processed by an earlier version, reprocess it individually via __TRILIUM_PH_0__Process OCR__TRILIUM_PH_1__; batch processing only handles files that haven't been OCR'd yet.

units.source: OCR needs to be aware of the language of the content in order for it to work correctly. The reason is that each language has its own data which needs to be downloaded, and accents or other symbols will not be supported by the default language.

To configure the languages that are supported by the OCR, simply go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Language & Region__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and adjust the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Content languages__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
When there are no content languages defined, the user interface __TRILIUM_PH_0__Language__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is used instead.
After making this change, the automatic processing or manual reprocessing will take into consideration the new languages.

To enforce the detection in a particular language for a given note, use the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__attribute__TRILIUM_PH_2__, similar to __TRILIUM_PH_3__text content language__TRILIUM_PH_4__. For __TRILIUM_PH_5__Attachments__TRILIUM_PH_6__, it's not possible to manually adjust the language.

The trained data for each language is not packaged with Trilium, as that would require a significant amount of space that might not be otherwise needed. As such, when the trained data will be downloaded automatically via __TRILIUM_PH_0__Tesseract.js__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
The downloaded trained data is located in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Data directory__TRILIUM_PH_1__, in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ directory.

units.source: Some cloud providers offer a subscription, which has a fixed monthly fee instead of pay-per-use (unlike the API keys).

In a nutshell, subscription-based providers work by either reusing your existing CLI tools (e.g. Claude Code, GitHub Copilot and OpenAI Codex via ACP) whereas some require installing the ACP server manually (e.g. Google Antigravity). Because they require something to be installed on your device, these providers are not available on Mobile (Android or iOS) or standalone mode.
See also the dedicated __TRILIUM_PH_0__Privacy__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section to better understand what data is being sent to a cloud provider.

The Flatpak version of Trilium (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Installing from Flathub__TRILIUM_PH_1__) runs in a sandbox that hides the programs installed on your computer, so on its own it cannot find Claude Code, the GitHub Copilot CLI, the Codex CLI or Google's Antigravity ACP server. Trilium can start them outside the sandbox once you allow it to:
Install the CLI on your computer and sign in to it, as described below for each provider.
Allow Trilium to start programs outside its sandbox by running this in a terminal:
Restart Trilium, then go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__AI / LLM__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and add the provider.

Trilium then looks the CLI up in your computer's __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and in your login shell's, and starts it there through __TRILIUM_PH_1__. Until the permission is granted, adding one of these providers fails with a message that repeats these steps.

This permission lets Trilium run any program on your computer outside the sandbox, which is the same access an installation outside Flatpak has. To take it back, run __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and restart Trilium.
The environment variables that point Trilium at a CLI (such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__) name a file inside the sandbox, so with the Flatpak, leave them unset and let Trilium find the CLI on your computer.

First, Claude Code needs to be installed on the machine that runs Trilium. So for a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Desktop Installation__TRILIUM_PH_1__, Claude needs to be installed locally and for a __TRILIUM_PH_2__Server Installation__TRILIUM_PH_3__ accessed via a browser, Claude needs to be installed on the server.
Claude Code must already be authenticated. To do so, run __TRILIUM_PH_0__ in a terminal once, type __TRILIUM_PH_1__ and follow the instructions.
Go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__AI / LLM__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and add the Claude Code provider.
How Trilium identifies your Claude Code binary
By looking for a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ environment variable pointing to the Claude binary. This allows overriding the path if needed.
By looking for __TRILIUM_PH_0__ in your PATH, generally works in most circumstances.

By asking your login shell for its __TRILIUM_PH_0__ which lets a desktop install find a CLI installed through __TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__, __TRILIUM_PH_3__ or Homebrew, since a GUI-launched app doesn't inherit your terminal's environment.
After your provider is set up, you'll benefit from the same features as an API key (note tools, web search, extended thinking, image/PDF attachments, streaming).

Trilium intentionally uses your Claude Code binary in order not to have to package a ~250 MB client with it, but this comes at a cost: there is a small risk for a version incompatibility, if the version installed locally doesn't match the one expected by Trilium. Generally it's best to keep both Claude Code and Trilium updated to the latest version.

This subscription-based provider is still in beta. It is safe to use (won't use additional funds and respects the terms of use), but you might experience small issues. Consider __TRILIUM_PH_0__Reporting issues__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
GitHub Copilot gives access to the models of your GitHub Copilot subscription (Pro, Pro+, Business or Enterprise), without an API key. Usage counts against your Copilot plan.

Install the GitHub Copilot CLI on the machine that runs Trilium, for example with __TRILIUM_PH_0__. As with Claude Code, for a __TRILIUM_PH_1__Server Installation__TRILIUM_PH_2__ it needs to be installed on the server.
Sign in by running __TRILIUM_PH_0__ in a terminal once. If you already use GitHub Copilot in another editor on the same machine, that login is reused.
Go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__AI / LLM__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and add the GitHub Copilot provider.
How Trilium identifies your Copilot CLI binary
By looking for a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ environment variable pointing to the Copilot binary.
By looking for __TRILIUM_PH_0__ in your PATH.
By asking your login shell for its __TRILIUM_PH_0__, the same as for Claude Code.
