Local or self-hosted providers are a free alternative which respects your privacy but requires specific hardware.
Trilium directly supports the following local providers:
Generally Ollama runs in the background so it should be directly usable in Trilium as long as the models are downloaded (e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_0__).

The OpenAI-compatible server is __TRILIUM_PH_0__disabled__TRILIUM_PH_1__ by default in LM Studio installations. First download your desired models through the graphical interface, then go to __TRILIUM_PH_2__Settings__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Developer__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and toggle __TRILIUM_PH_6__Developer mode__TRILIUM_PH_7__. On the left there will be a new __TRILIUM_PH_8__Developer__TRILIUM_PH_9__ tab, with a toggle to start it up.
Even for local providers that are not directly supported by Trilium, you can still use a custom endpoint (see below).

When dealing with self-hosted LLM models, depending on the training and the size of the model, the quality of the output may vary. Before __TRILIUM_PH_0__reporting issues__TRILIUM_PH_1__ regarding the quality of the output (e.g. hallucinating tool calls), consider benchmarking the response against a cloud provider (Claude Sonnet is recommended).

If your desired hosted (e.g. Groq, Mistral, Together) or local LLM provider is not listed in Trilium, you can use the dedicated __TRILIUM_PH_0__OpenAI-compatible__TRILIUM_PH_1__ provider from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Custom endpoint__TRILIUM_PH_3__ section.
This allows you to set the base URL to an OpenAI-compatible API, with an optional API key if required by the service.

Enter the base URL exactly as the service documents it, including its version path, such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ or __TRILIUM_PH_1__. Only a bare host such as __TRILIUM_PH_2__ is completed with __TRILIUM_PH_3__.

The endpoint can run on the same machine as Trilium, elsewhere on your local network or on a Tailscale tailnet. Trilium refuses link-local addresses (__TRILIUM_PH_0__) and cloud metadata endpoints, which no model server is served on.
For custom endpoints, the pricing of the models is not known so the cost of a conversation will not be displayed; this is especially relevant for hosted providers.

Trilium sends nothing to an AI provider until you send a message. Enabling the integration, adding a provider or opening a chat transmits nothing on its own, the one exception is that listing a provider's models sends your API key to that provider, so the list can be fetched.
Once you send a message or run the __TRILIUM_PH_0__In-editor AI assistant__TRILIUM_PH_1__, what leaves your machine depends on the provider you chose and on which context options are enabled.
The provider's servers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek). OpenRouter passes each message on to the lab that runs the chosen model, according to the privacy settings of your OpenRouter account.
The provider's servers, via Claude Code running locally
Nothing leaves the machine running the model
Wherever it was pointed, which may be your own hardware or a hosted service
This is the reason the provider list is grouped this way, and why Trilium pre-selects nothing: the choice of where your note content is sent is made explicitly by you, before anything is sent.

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__In-editor AI assistant__TRILIUM_PH_1__ has a model selection of its own, so it may be answered by a different provider than the one in the chat. The row at the bottom of the assistant's menu always names the one being used.
The conversation itself: your messages and the assistant's replies, including earlier turns
Trilium's system prompt describing how to format answers and use tools.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__The current note, only when note context is enabled.__TRILIUM_PH_1__
In the sidebar chat this is the file icon at the bottom; the dedicated chat note type never sends a current note.
What travels is a metadata block: the note's ID, title, type, creation and modification dates, its parent IDs, the titles of up to 20 children, up to 20 attributes, and a preview of the content.
Notes above a size threshold send a size hint instead of the text, and the model must call a tool to read further.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Any note the model asks for, when note access is enabled.__TRILIUM_PH_1__
Tools let the model search your tree and read notes, attributes and attachments beyond the current one.

It decides what to fetch, and each call waits for you to allow it, unless the chat's permission mode lets reads or every call run on their own, or you allowed that tool for the chat. The reachable scope is your whole tree, except for notes you exclude (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Excluding notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ below).
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Attachments and mentions__TRILIUM_PH_1__, when you add them: images, PDFs and text files are sent to the provider, and an __TRILIUM_PH_2__ mention makes that note fetchable.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Your search query__TRILIUM_PH_1__, when web search is enabled, the model's search terms reach the provider's own search infrastructure, or the search provider chosen in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Tools__TRILIUM_PH_3__ menu (Brave Search, Tavily, Exa, Serper, Perplexity or your SearXNG instance).

__TRILIUM_PH_0__The pages the model reads__TRILIUM_PH_1__, when web search goes through a search provider or a DeepSeek model's built-in search: Trilium fetches each page the model asks for from the site itself, so the site sees a request from the machine running Trilium. The page's text is then sent to the model's provider.

A run of the __TRILIUM_PH_0__In-editor AI assistant__TRILIUM_PH_1__ sends a different set than a chat message. For quick actions, it sends it the moment you pick an action, there is no send button to reconsider at. For the free-form __TRILIUM_PH_2__Ask AI__TRILIUM_PH_3__, there is a dedicated send button and model selector.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__The passage you selected__TRILIUM_PH_1__, or the paragraph the cursor is in when you pick a quick action without selecting anything. Opened from the menu of the drag handle, the assistant sends the whole blocks that the handle shades instead.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Up to 1500 characters of the note on each side of that passage__TRILIUM_PH_1__, as plain text. The assistant is told this is context only and must not be rewritten, but it is sent regardless of whether you selected it: a run on a single sentence still transmits the paragraphs around it.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Where the note sits__TRILIUM_PH_1__: its title and the titles of its parents, as a breadcrumb.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Trilium's writing-assistant instructions__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which describe the formatting it may produce.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Earlier turns of the same exchange__TRILIUM_PH_1__, once you follow up on a response.
No note metadata block is sent, web search is never enabled, and the assistant has no note tools so it can read nothing beyond the text listed above.

While your __TRILIUM_PH_0__protected session__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is locked, protected notes send neither title nor content. __TRILIUM_PH_2__While it is unlocked they are treated like any other note,__TRILIUM_PH_3__ a note the model reads through a tool is sent to the provider in full. If you keep sensitive material in protected notes, be aware that unlocking them removes that boundary for the duration of the session.

The same applies to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__In-editor AI assistant__TRILIUM_PH_1__: it works on whatever is open in the editor, so running it inside an unlocked protected note sends that note's text like any other.

Add the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__label__TRILIUM_PH_2__ to a note to hide it from the AI chat and the __TRILIUM_PH_3__MCP server__TRILIUM_PH_4__. The label covers only that note: the notes below it stay visible unless you make the label __TRILIUM_PH_5__inheritable__TRILIUM_PH_6__, and a child can opt back in with __TRILIUM_PH_7__.

A note created from a template inherits all of the template's labels (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Templates__TRILIUM_PH_1__), so adding __TRILIUM_PH_2__ to a template hides every note that uses it, not just the template.
The note tools report it as not found: it is left out of search results, child lists and subtrees, and relations that point to it are not shown.
The model cannot read, edit, move, clone or rename it, create notes under it, or remove the label. It also cannot delete a note that has an excluded note below it.
Its metadata is not sent as the current note, even when note context is enabled.
A visible child does not show it as a parent, and the model cannot move the child out of it.
Unlike a protected note, an excluded note stays hidden while your protected session is unlocked. The exclusion applies to the note tools only. It is not encryption, and it does not cover:
Files you attach to a message yourself.
The __TRILIUM_PH_0__In-editor AI assistant__TRILIUM_PH_1__ when you run it inside the note.
Text from the note that appears in other notes, such as a link with the note's title.

What a search query can test. Search never returns an excluded note, but a query can still match a visible note through an excluded one: by its title in the note path, through a relation (__TRILIUM_PH_0__), a parent or child (__TRILIUM_PH_1__), or a label the visible note inherits from it. A model that guesses can learn whether an excluded note contains a given word.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Which provider__TRILIUM_PH_1__: the single decision that determines whether anything leaves your machine at all.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Note access__TRILIUM_PH_1__: turn it off in the __TRILIUM_PH_2____TRILIUM_PH_3__Tools__TRILIUM_PH_4__ menu at the bottom of the chat, and the model can read nothing beyond what you type.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__The current note:__TRILIUM_PH_1__ the file icon in the sidebar chat.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Notes the AI cannot reach:__TRILIUM_PH_1__ the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ label, see __TRILIUM_PH_3__Excluding notes__TRILIUM_PH_4__ above.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Which tool calls ask first:__TRILIUM_PH_1__ the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Permissions__TRILIUM_PH_3__ submenu of the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Tools__TRILIUM_PH_5__ menu. __TRILIUM_PH_6__Always ask__TRILIUM_PH_7__ has every call wait for you, reads included. A new chat starts in the mode you picked last, so a chat after one set to __TRILIUM_PH_8__Don't ask__TRILIUM_PH_9__ asks about nothing either. Until you pick a mode, chats start in __TRILIUM_PH_10__Ask before changes__TRILIUM_PH_11__, where the AI reads and searches your notes without asking.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__The editor assistant__TRILIUM_PH_1__: it has no per-run toggles. What you control is whether you run it, what you select before you do and which model answers.
With note access and note context both off, the provider receives only the words you typed.

Adding an Ollama or LM Studio provider keeps every message on the machine running the model, and Trilium marks their models as free because no metered API is involved. The trade-off is quality and hardware: a small local model may fail at tool calls that a cloud model handles, so a local setup that misbehaves is worth benchmarking against a cloud provider before reporting it as a bug.
Trilium itself collects no telemetry from the AI integration.

Your API key is stored in your database, sent only to the provider it belongs to, and is write-only through the options API so that a malevolent __TRILIUM_PH_0__Scripting__TRILIUM_PH_1__ cannot access it. If you have backend or SQL console access enabled, a malevolent script __TRILIUM_PH_2__could potentially exfiltrate your API keys__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

The built-in MCP server is off by default. When enabled, every request must carry an ETAPI token, which grants the same full read and write access to your notes as the REST API; treat one like a password. On desktop it is reachable only from __TRILIUM_PH_0__ unless you turn on __TRILIUM_PH_1__Network Access__TRILIUM_PH_2__.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Model Context Protocol__TRILIUM_PH_1__ allows external chat applications such as Claude Code to have access to the Trilium database.

v0.103.0 comes with a built-in MCP server that is not active by default. To activate it, go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → AI/LLM and toggle the __TRILIUM_PH_2__MCP server__TRILIUM_PH_3__ option.

Once the MCP is active, simply add the MCP server to your AI assistant. The URL to use is displayed in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Endpoint__TRILIUM_PH_1__ __TRILIUM_PH_2__URL__TRILIUM_PH_3__ information underneath the MCP toggle.
Only the HTTP transport is supported, the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ method is not supported. If that is a blocker, consider using a third-party alternative listed below.

The tools exposed to the MCP are the same tools that are supported by the internal chat (see the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note access__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section). Notes with the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ label are hidden from both, see __TRILIUM_PH_3__Privacy__TRILIUM_PH_4__.

units.context: MCP > Built-in MCP > Approving tool calls

units.source: Trilium does not ask for approval of the calls an external assistant makes; that is left to the assistant's own permission settings. To help it decide, each tool tells the assistant whether it only reads your notes, only adds to them (creating a note, cloning it or appending to it), or can overwrite or remove something (editing, renaming, moving or deleting). An assistant that supports these hints can then run reads on their own and ask before changes, the way __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ask before changes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ does in Trilium's chat.
units.context: MCP > Built-in MCP > Approving tool calls

units.source: To protect your notes from unauthorized access, the MCP server requires authentication. Generally MCP servers need to support OAuth for authentication, but Trilium uses a simpler mechanism using Bearer tokens.

To configure authentication, first create an __TRILIUM_PH_0__ETAPI (REST API)__TRILIUM_PH_1__ token by going to __TRILIUM_PH_2__Options__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__ETAPI__TRILIUM_PH_5__. Then follow the instructions in __TRILIUM_PH_6__Options__TRILIUM_PH_7__ → __TRILIUM_PH_8__AI / LLM__TRILIUM_PH_9__, by looking at the __TRILIUM_PH_10__How to connect an assistant__TRILIUM_PH_11__ section under MCP.
The following are alternatives to Trilium's built-in MCP feature. Since Trilium's AI implementation is still experimental, its tooling might not be as mature as external tools.
These solutions are third-party and thus not endorsed or supported directly by the Trilium Notes team. Please address questions and issues on their corresponding repository instead.

Trilium can connect to a large language model and use it as an assistant that works directly on your notes: ask questions about the note you're reading, have it draft or restructure content, or get it to write scripts and widgets for you.

The integration is off by default and does nothing until you enable it and configure a provider; Trilium ships no model of its own. The provider you pick decides how your notes travel: a cloud API billed per use, a subscription you already pay for, or a model running on your own hardware, in which case nothing leaves the machine. See __TRILIUM_PH_0__Providers__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for what each involves, and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Privacy__TRILIUM_PH_3__ for exactly what gets sent.
Once enabled, the assistant is available as:
As a dedicated note type, it can read and modify notes through tools, which you can switch off per conversation if you would rather it only saw what you type.
A panel in the right sidebar, which acts similarly to the dedicated note type but it also has optional access to the current note.

An __TRILIUM_PH_0__In-editor AI assistant__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which comes with builtin actions that operate over selected text (such as proof-reading, summarizing), as well as __TRILIUM_PH_2__Custom AI quick actions__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
Chat-based interface with live streaming of the messages.
Provides the AI context with the note currently being looked at.
Tools to alter note content, create new notes, etc.
Statistics regarding context window use and pricing per message.
Attachments for multi-modal chat (images, text files, PDFs).
Optional MCP to allow external chat tools (e.g. Claude Code) to operate on notes within Trilium.

Easily create a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Render Note__TRILIUM_PH_1__, e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_2__Create for me a render note which allows me to play tic-tac-toe. Make sure to use Preact instead of the legacy jQuery.__TRILIUM_PH_3__
Create widgets for a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Dashboard__TRILIUM_PH_1__, such as a calculator, a stopwatch, a pomodoro timer.
Claude Sonnet is known to produce very good frontend or backend scripts with little guidance, as the AI has been instructed in how to produce them.
Trilium supports four different types of providers:
Pay-per use with an API key which is billed separately from any subscription you might already have.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ OpenRouter, which reaches the models of most labs with one key
Reuses an existing subscription instead of paying per use.
For other providers that are not directly supported by Trilium, either local or hosted (e.g. Groq, Mistral, Together).
For more information about each provider, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Providers__TRILIUM_PH_1__. See the dedicated __TRILIUM_PH_2__Privacy__TRILIUM_PH_3__ to better understand what data is sent to providers.

To enable the AI integration, simply go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__AI / LLM__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and press the toggle in the top-right of the dialog and configure a provider.
There are two different chat interfaces:

units.context: AI > Creating a new chat > The sidebar interface
AI > Creating a new chat > The dedicated note type

units.source: The dedicated chat note is similar to the sidebar interface, but it makes longer conversations more comfortable to read.
units.context: AI > Creating a new chat > The dedicated note type

units.source: Unlike the sidebar, the AI will not be aware of the current note it's in.
units.context: AI > Creating a new chat > The dedicated note type
AI > Creating a new chat > Templates

units.source: Chat notes can be set as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Templates__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to make them easily reusable. The entire conversation history is kept, allowing a basic form of specialization for the LLM with the existing chat acting like a system prompt.
units.context: AI > Creating a new chat > Templates
AI > Creating a new chat > Model selection

units.source: When a provider is configured in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the next step is to select the models that will be available for the chat.
units.context: AI > Creating a new chat > Model selection

units.source: The models are retrieved dynamically from the provider, only when the model selection list is visible. To alter the list of models, simply press the Edit button in the model selection box.
units.context: AI > Creating a new chat > Model selection

units.source: Pricing information is displayed for known models. The pricing information (price per million tokens) is embedded in the application (using a subset of LiteLLM's data) and is updated with new versions of Trilium. Local providers are considered free, whereas custom endpoint providers don't offer any pricing information.
units.context: AI > Creating a new chat > Model selection

units.source: The AI can optionally search the web to find more information about a specific topic.

Where the search comes from is chosen in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Web search__TRILIUM_PH_1__ submenu of the __TRILIUM_PH_2____TRILIUM_PH_3__Tools__TRILIUM_PH_4__ menu next to the model selector at the bottom of the chat, whose row shows the source in use:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Disabled__TRILIUM_PH_1__ turns web search off for this chat.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Use the model's built-in search__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the default, lets the model search with its provider's own search. Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini and DeepSeek models have one, as do Claude Code, Google Antigravity and OpenAI Codex. OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio and custom endpoints don't, so this choice is disabled for their models. DeepSeek's search is billed per search on your DeepSeek account and works only with DeepSeek's own endpoint, not with a custom base URL.

A search provider (Brave Search, Tavily, Exa, Serper, Perplexity or SearXNG) searches through that service instead, whichever model is answering. Search providers are added in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search Providers__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section of the AI settings, which __TRILIUM_PH_2__Manage search providers__TRILIUM_PH_3__ at the bottom of the submenu opens. The browser version can't use Brave Search, Exa or Perplexity, whose services refuse requests made from a web page, so they're shown disabled there.
To use SearXNG, enable its JSON output by adding __TRILIUM_PH_0__ to the search formats in the instance's __TRILIUM_PH_1__. SearXNG turns JSON off by default, and without it every search fails.

SearXNG doesn't use API keys, so leave the API key empty. Fill it in only if your instance sits behind a proxy that requires a token; Trilium sends it as a bearer token in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ header.

Whether web search is on is kept per chat; the search source is shared by all chats. A choice the current model can't use stays in the menu, disabled; hover the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ icon next to it to see why. Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Google Antigravity and OpenAI Codex run their own tools, so they can't use a search provider.
In the chat, a search run through a search provider shows that provider's logo at the start of its line instead of the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ magnifier; hover the logo to see the provider's name.

With a search provider, the model can also read the pages it finds, or a link you give it, as text: Trilium fetches the page itself and hands the model up to its first 20,000 characters. Addresses on your own machine or network are refused. In the browser version most sites don't allow being read this way, so reading a page there usually fails.

Some models reason before they answer. While the model is thinking, its reasoning is shown in full under a spinner; once it is done, it folds into a collapsible __TRILIUM_PH_0__Thought process__TRILIUM_PH_1__ line above the reply.
How much a model thinks is set per chat, in one of two ways depending on the model:
Most models have an __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Extended thinking__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button, next to the __TRILIUM_PH_3____TRILIUM_PH_4__Tools__TRILIUM_PH_5__ button.

Models that offer several levels of reasoning (DeepSeek V4, OpenRouter models that reason, OpenAI Codex, Antigravity) have a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ reasoning effort dropdown next to the model selector instead. __TRILIUM_PH_1__None__TRILIUM_PH_2__, where offered, turns thinking off; higher levels give better answers to hard questions, but take longer and cost more.

The effort dropdown only appears once Trilium knows the model's levels. For a DeepSeek provider set up with an earlier version of Trilium, edit the provider in the model selection box and press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Save__TRILIUM_PH_1__ once.
Tools allow the agentic AI to understand and operate on notes directly within your Trilium instance.

This feature is on by default. To turn it off, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Tools__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button next to the model selector at the bottom of the chat and switch off __TRILIUM_PH_3__Note access__TRILIUM_PH_4__. The __TRILIUM_PH_5__Tools__TRILIUM_PH_6__ button is highlighted while note access or web search is on.
Here are a few tools that Trilium provides for the LLM:
Get the metadata or content of a note.
There are multiple mechanism for the LLM to edit a note: completely by re-writing it, find/replace of a text sequence or append.
When re-writing a note, the LLM can also change its type (for example from a text note to a code note) or the language of a code note, rewriting the content to match.
Whenever the AI makes a change, a __TRILIUM_PH_0__revision__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is saved to be able to revert any unwanted changes.
Asked for a drawing, the LLM can create an SVG image note, or turn an existing note into one. It can write only SVG images, not other formats such as PNG.
Get the full list of attributes, or a specific attribute.

Set the value of an attribute, or add another value next to the existing ones (such as a second __TRILIUM_PH_0__). When setting a value replaces an existing one, the AI is told which value it replaced.

An attribute that runs code, such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__, __TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__, is saved with a __TRILIUM_PH_3__ prefix (for example __TRILIUM_PH_4__), the same way a safe import disables it (see __TRILIUM_PH_5__Active content__TRILIUM_PH_6__). If the note already had that attribute enabled and the AI sets rather than adds the value, the AI removes the enabled one, so none of it runs until you enable the new value. The AI tells you which note it is on; review the code, then enable it with the toggle next to the active content badge beside the note's title or, for a __TRILIUM_PH_7__Render Note__TRILIUM_PH_8__, the __TRILIUM_PH_9__Enable render note__TRILIUM_PH_10__ button in the note.
Get the direct children of a note.
Get the entire subtree of a note.
Move or clone a note somewhere else.
Get the content of an attachment.

Each tool the AI uses appears in the chat as a single line naming the tool and the note or query it worked on; a renamed note shows its previous title struck through, a deleted note its title struck through, a moved note where it was moved from and to, an attribute the AI read, set, added or deleted as a pill (struck through once deleted), an attachment by its title, note and size, and a web page the AI read as a link. A line folds open only when there is something to read inline: the notes a search found, the pages a web search found, the icons an icon search found, the type, attributes or start of the content of a note the AI read, all the attributes of a note, the text of an attachment or of a web page, the User Guide pages the AI looked up or its table of contents (both open in the help panel), the children or the whole subtree of a note, what the AI wrote into a note it created, rewrote or added to, the changes of an edit, or the reason a tool failed. A search names on its line the part of the tree it is confined to, if any, and also shows how many notes it found and how many of the matches the AI asked for; each note it lists opens with a click. To see exactly what the AI sent to a tool and what it got back, hover the line and press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button next to it; on touch screens the button is always shown.

When the reply stops moving for a couple of seconds while the AI is still at work, for example while it reads what a tool returned, a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Still working…__TRILIUM_PH_1__ line appears under it until the next part of the reply arrives.

units.context: AI > Features > Note access (tools) > Approving tool calls

units.source: Before the AI runs a tool, the chat asks whether to allow it. The tool's line is marked with a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ icon and has __TRILIUM_PH_1__Allow__TRILIUM_PH_2__ and __TRILIUM_PH_3__Deny__TRILIUM_PH_4__ buttons below it. When the call would write to a note, the line opens on the text it would write or the changes of an edit. The reply waits until you answer.
units.context: AI > Features > Note access (tools) > Approving tool calls

units.source: To let the call run, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Allow__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: AI > Features > Note access (tools) > Approving tool calls

units.source: To stop asking about a tool for the rest of the chat, open the menu next to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Allow__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and choose to always allow that tool for this chat. The call runs, and so do the other calls of that tool still waiting and every later one in this chat. Other tools keep asking, and a new chat asks again.
units.context: AI > Features > Note access (tools) > Approving tool calls

units.source: To refuse it, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Deny__TRILIUM_PH_1__. The AI is told that you declined, and its reply carries on without the call, which is marked __TRILIUM_PH_2__denied__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: AI > Features > Note access (tools) > Approving tool calls

units.source: Stopping the reply denies every call that is still waiting.
units.context: AI > Features > Note access (tools) > Approving tool calls

units.source: To make a chat ask about a tool again, open the __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Tools__TRILIUM_PH_2__ menu at the bottom of the chat and, under __TRILIUM_PH_3__Allowed in this chat__TRILIUM_PH_4__, press the tool. The submenu is shown once the chat has allowed a tool.
units.context: AI > Features > Note access (tools) > Approving tool calls

units.source: Which calls ask depends on the chat's permission mode, chosen in the __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Tools__TRILIUM_PH_2__ menu under __TRILIUM_PH_3__Permissions__TRILIUM_PH_4__:
units.context: AI > Features > Note access (tools) > Approving tool calls

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Always ask__TRILIUM_PH_1__: every call asks, including the ones that only read (searching notes, or reading a note or an attachment).
units.context: AI > Features > Note access (tools) > Approving tool calls

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ask before changes__TRILIUM_PH_1__: the calls that only read run on their own, and the ones that change your notes (creating, editing, renaming, moving or deleting a note, and setting, adding or deleting an attribute) ask.
units.context: AI > Features > Note access (tools) > Approving tool calls

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Don't ask__TRILIUM_PH_1__: every call runs without asking, changes included.
units.context: AI > Features > Note access (tools) > Approving tool calls

units.source: A new chat starts in the mode you picked last, in any chat, or in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ask before changes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ until you pick one. Picking __TRILIUM_PH_2__Don't ask__TRILIUM_PH_3__ therefore carries over to the next chat too.
units.context: AI > Features > Note access (tools) > Approving tool calls

units.source: A tool allowed for the chat runs without asking in every mode. So does looking something up in what ships with Trilium (its User Guide, the skill sheets that teach the AI Trilium's search syntax and note types, and the icons), since it reads none of your notes. Searching the web and reading a web page never ask either: turning on web search in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Tools__TRILIUM_PH_1__ menu is what allows them, whether the model searches on its own or through a search provider.
units.context: AI > Features > Note access (tools) > Approving tool calls

units.source: The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Subscription-based providers__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Google Antigravity and OpenAI Codex) ask like any other provider.
units.context: AI > Features > Note access (tools) > Approving tool calls

units.source: Most changes you allow can be undone: a deleted note can be restored, and an edit reverted from its revision. Setting an attribute is harder to undo, since attributes have no history.
units.context: AI > Features > Note access (tools) > Approving tool calls

units.source: Gemini can't use its built-in search while note access is on. While it is, the built-in search choice in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Tools__TRILIUM_PH_1__ menu is disabled and says why; a search provider works with note access on.
units.context: AI > Features > Note access (tools) > Approving tool calls

units.source: Since Trilium v0.140.0, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Attachments__TRILIUM_PH_1__ allow for multi-modal chat:
Raster image (sent as vision input, except for SVGs) with the following supported formats: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP.
PDFs, sent natively to the provider (supported by Anthropic, OpenAI and Google).

Not every model reads every kind of attachment: DeepSeek reads no PDFs, and images only with its vision models; OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot and Google Antigravity read images but no PDFs. For such a model:
The attach button offers only the kinds the model reads, and a pasted or dropped file it can't read is not attached.
After switching to such a model, an attachment it can't read is marked with a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ warning, and the message can't be sent until the attachment is removed or another model is selected.
An attachment sent in an earlier message reaches the model as its name only, such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__, so it can tell you it doesn't see the content.
Press the dedicated __TRILIUM_PH_0__Attach__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button (paperclip icon) underneath the text box.
Paste an image directly from clipboard using Ctrl+V.
Once one or more attachments are uploaded, they will appear directly above the text box:
Images have a small thumbnail for easy identifications.
Every attachment can be deleted by pressing their corresponding X button.

Clicking an image or a PDF, either its chip above the text box or where it appears in a sent message, opens it in a viewer: an image can be zoomed and panned there, a PDF read page by page. The button next to the viewer's close button opens the original file in a new browser tab. __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__-clicking instead opens an image in a new browser tab, and a PDF as an attachment in a new Trilium tab.
When an attachment is present, the LLM is instructed to consider the attachment with priority, even if it has access to the current note.
Currently Trilium doesn't pre-process the attachments (e.g. via __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text Extraction (OCR)__TRILIUM_PH_1__) before sending them to the LLM provider.

Mentions are a way to insert references to notes other than the current note, using the same mechanism as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Internal (reference) links__TRILIUM_PH_1__. To refer to another note, simply type @ followed by the name of the note to reference.
This feature is mostly helpful when note tools are enabled, otherwise the LLM will have no way to access the given note.
Skills in Trilium are specialized instruction sets that help the AI be more productive by understanding how Trilium.
These skills are not loaded by default to avoid an increased consumption of tokens, but the AI can load them on-demand if __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note tools__TRILIUM_PH_1__ are enabled.
Search syntax: understands the full syntax of __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Backend scripting: to be able to write proper __TRILIUM_PH_0__Backend scripts__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Frontend scripting: to be able to write proper __TRILIUM_PH_0__front-end scripts__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (basic scripts, widgets, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Render Note__TRILIUM_PH_3__).
Dashboards: to build a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Dashboard__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and its widgets, including interactive ones made with a __TRILIUM_PH_2__Render Note__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

Starting with version v0.102.0, AI/LLM integration has been removed from the Trilium Notes core.
While a significant amount of effort went into developing this feature, maintaining and supporting it long-term proved to be unsustainable.

When upgrading to v0.102.0, your Chat notes will be preserved, but instead of the dedicated chat window they will be turned to a normal __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note, revealing the underlying JSON of the conversation.
Given the recent advancements of the AI scene, we decided to give the LLM integration another try. v0.103.0 introduces a completely new chat system.

One of the key changes that lead to the reimplementation is that now we are using a library (__TRILIUM_PH_0__Vercel AI__TRILIUM_PH_1__) to manage the inner mechanism and the differences between LLM providers instead of having to implement it on our own.

Meeting transcription is a new feature and is still in beta. It has not been tested on every operating system, audio setup and meeting application, so it might fail to capture the audio, miss part of a meeting or behave differently from what this page describes. Before relying on it for an important meeting, try it on a short call first.

If something does not work, please __TRILIUM_PH_0__report the issue__TRILIUM_PH_1__, mentioning your operating system and the meeting application you used. The __TRILIUM_PH_2__Keep recordings for troubleshooting__TRILIUM_PH_3__ option described below keeps what is needed to reproduce a problem.

Meeting transcription turns a meeting into text while it happens: Trilium listens to your microphone and to what the other participants say through your speakers, and writes down who said what in a new note. Recognition runs entirely on your device, so no audio leaves it (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Privacy__TRILIUM_PH_1__ below).
Meeting transcription is available only in the desktop application. It is not available when Trilium is accessed through a browser, nor in the mobile application.

Meeting transcription is off by default. To turn it on, go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Transcription__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and turn on __TRILIUM_PH_4__Meeting transcription__TRILIUM_PH_5__. This adds the __TRILIUM_PH_6__ __TRILIUM_PH_7__Transcribe meeting__TRILIUM_PH_8__ button to the __TRILIUM_PH_9__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_10__, marked with a __TRILIUM_PH_11__Beta__TRILIUM_PH_12__ badge.

The speech recognition models are not part of Trilium. The first time you transcribe a meeting, Trilium asks to download them; see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Downloaded resources__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for the sizes and how to manage them. Each device downloads its own copy.
Press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Transcribe meeting__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button in the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_4__.
If the models are not downloaded yet, confirm the download and wait for it to finish.

Trilium creates a text note titled with the current date and time (for example __TRILIUM_PH_0__Meeting 2026-10-15 14:30__TRILIUM_PH_1__) in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note Inbox__TRILIUM_PH_3__, opens it and starts transcribing. While it transcribes, the button turns into a __TRILIUM_PH_4__ __TRILIUM_PH_5__Stop transcribing__TRILIUM_PH_6__ button and shows the time elapsed. Beside it, a reminder asks you to let everyone in the meeting know that it is being transcribed and to ask for their consent; it closes by itself after 10 seconds, or when you click it.
To end the transcription, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Stop transcribing__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button. Trilium finishes transcribing what was already said before it stops.

Only one meeting can be transcribed at a time. The note itself is an ordinary text note: you can take notes in it during the meeting, rename it or move it anywhere in the tree. It carries the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ label.

Trilium tells you when your microphone or the meeting's audio is not being transcribed. It shows a message saying which one and why, the time on the button turns red and the button's tooltip says that some audio is not being transcribed:

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Not captured__TRILIUM_PH_1__: the transcription started without that audio, for example because there is no microphone or because Trilium was not allowed to record the screen and its audio. Connect the microphone or allow the recording, then stop the transcription and start it again.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__No audio__TRILIUM_PH_1__: nothing has arrived from it for 10 seconds, as when its capture hangs. Stop the transcription and start it again; what was transcribed until then is kept.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Only silence__TRILIUM_PH_1__: it has delivered nothing but silence, for 15 seconds from your microphone or for a minute from the meeting. A microphone muted in your system's settings, or with a mute button of its own, does this. A meeting nobody speaks in for a minute does it too, so this message can be ignored when the others are just quiet.
Each message shows once. __TRILIUM_PH_0__No audio__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Only silence__TRILIUM_PH_3__ clear by themselves once sound arrives again.

If the transcription stops on its own, for example because the audio could no longer be captured, Trilium shows a message and keeps everything transcribed until then. Closing Trilium during a meeting waits for the transcription to finish first.

The transcript is stored as an __TRILIUM_PH_0__attachment__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of the meeting note and is shown in a collapsible __TRILIUM_PH_2__Transcript__TRILIUM_PH_3__ section above the note's content. It updates as the meeting goes on, one paragraph per speaker turn, each with the time it started. While the meeting is being transcribed, the header of the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Transcript__TRILIUM_PH_5__ section shows the level of your microphone (__TRILIUM_PH_6__Me__TRILIUM_PH_7__) and of the meeting's audio (__TRILIUM_PH_8__Others__TRILIUM_PH_9__), so you can tell that both are being heard, even while the section is collapsed; a source that is not being transcribed is marked __TRILIUM_PH_10__Not captured__TRILIUM_PH_11__, __TRILIUM_PH_12__No audio__TRILIUM_PH_13__ or __TRILIUM_PH_14__Only silence__TRILIUM_PH_15__. While someone is talking, __TRILIUM_PH_16__Speaking…__TRILIUM_PH_17__ shows under their name until their words are transcribed. If you are reading the end of the transcript, it scrolls to follow new text.
The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Transcript__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section is expanded each time the note is opened. To collapse it, click its header; it stays collapsed only until the note is opened again.

The transcript is also listed among the note's attachments, under __TRILIUM_PH_0__Generated by Trilium__TRILIUM_PH_1__. Opening it from there shows the same view of the transcript. Deleting the attachment deletes the transcript, and the section disappears from the note.
What you say into your microphone is labeled __TRILIUM_PH_0__Me__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

What the other participants say is labeled __TRILIUM_PH_0__Speaker 1__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Speaker 2__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and so on, while __TRILIUM_PH_4__Identify speakers__TRILIUM_PH_5__ is on; otherwise it is labeled __TRILIUM_PH_6__Others__TRILIUM_PH_7__.

To name a speaker, click their name, type the new name and press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_1__. The name changes on every turn of that speaker. Press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_3__ to cancel, or clear the name to restore the default one.

To show the transcript with or without hesitations such as "uh", "um" and stuttered words, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Hide filler words__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button above it, which shows as pressed while they are hidden. While they are shown, they are grayed out, so you can see what hiding them would remove. This affects only what is shown; the stored transcript keeps every word.

To copy the transcript as plain text, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Copy transcript__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button above it. Each turn is copied with the speaker's name and the time it started, as shown, so the copy leaves out filler words while they are hidden.

If the meeting note is __TRILIUM_PH_0__protected__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and the protected session is locked during the meeting, the transcript cannot be saved. Trilium keeps it in memory and saves it once you enter the protected session again, as long as Trilium stays open.
The settings are in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Transcription__TRILIUM_PH_3__, and are shown once __TRILIUM_PH_4__Meeting transcription__TRILIUM_PH_5__ is on.

The speech recognition model. Both are versions of NVIDIA's Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 model and recognize 25 European languages and work out which one is spoken. __TRILIUM_PH_0__Standard__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is a smaller download and runs well on most computers. __TRILIUM_PH_2__High accuracy__TRILIUM_PH_3__ makes fewer mistakes, but is a larger download and needs about 1.6 GB more memory while transcribing. A model is downloaded the first time you transcribe with it.

Tells the other participants apart and labels each of them separately, using the TitaNet model. Voices are compared only during the meeting: nothing about a voice is stored, and no one is recognized from one meeting to the next. Turn it off if it mixes up voices. The change applies from the next meeting.

Keeps the audio of the meeting, the settings used and the transcript as it was produced, so that a problem can be reported and reproduced. It takes about 230 MB per hour of meeting and is never deleted automatically. The folder where they are kept is shown below the option.

Before turning on __TRILIUM_PH_0__Keep recordings for troubleshooting__TRILIUM_PH_1__, ask everyone in the meeting to agree to being recorded. In several countries and US states, recording a conversation without everyone's consent is a criminal offense. The audio is stored unencrypted, even for protected notes. While the option is on, the tooltip of the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Transcribe meeting__TRILIUM_PH_3__ button says so, and the reminder shown when the transcription starts mentions that the audio is kept.
The sizes and licenses of the models are listed in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Downloaded resources__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Meeting transcription does not use any online service:
The audio is recognized on your device by the open-source sherpa-onnx engine. Trilium does not send the audio or the transcript to any online service, and no account or API key is needed.
An Internet connection is needed only to download the models, from Hugging Face and from the sherpa-onnx project on GitHub. Once they are downloaded, meeting transcription works offline.
Speaker identification compares voices only during the meeting. Nothing about a voice is stored.
The audio is not kept, unless __TRILIUM_PH_0__Keep recordings for troubleshooting__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is on. Those recordings stay in a folder on your device and are never synchronized.

The transcript itself is an attachment of the meeting note, so it is handled like the rest of your notes. If you use __TRILIUM_PH_0__Synchronization__TRILIUM_PH_1__, it is synchronized to your sync server and your other devices. To keep it encrypted, transcribe into a __TRILIUM_PH_2__protected__TRILIUM_PH_3__ note: the transcript of a protected note is protected too.

Meeting transcription needs a speech recognition engine that does not load on every computer, for example on Linux distributions older than Ubuntu 22.04 or Debian 12. Where it does not load, the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Transcribe meeting__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button does not appear, the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Transcription__TRILIUM_PH_3__ options say so, and the log records why.

The transcript is made from the audio played by your device. A participant whose voice does not come out of your speakers or headphones, for example someone in the same room, is transcribed only as far as your microphone picks them up, and is labeled __TRILIUM_PH_0__Me__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Speaker identification works best with a few clearly distinct voices. Similar voices, many participants or poor call quality can lead to speakers being merged or split.
Accuracy is lower for languages other than English, and the model can switch to the wrong language for short passages.
Transcribing uses a noticeable amount of processor time and memory, especially with the __TRILIUM_PH_0__High accuracy__TRILIUM_PH_1__ model.

These are run with the current app and note context. These can be run either manually or automatically on start-up.

This allows rendering custom content inside a note, using either HTML or Preact JSX.

units.source: The __TRILIUM_PH_0__ library is deprecated and will be removed in a future version.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ was removed in v0.106.0. See __TRILIUM_PH_1__v0.106.0: Removal of cheerio__TRILIUM_PH_2__ for the full migration guide.
Cheerio is only used for the scripting API while the server internally uses __TRILIUM_PH_0__ for HTML parsing. Removing __TRILIUM_PH_1__ reduces bundle size and maintenance overhead.
jQuery 4 removes legacy browser support (such as IE11 support), but it also removes some APIs that are considered deprecated such as:
Use native equivalents like __TRILIUM_PH_0__, __TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__, and __TRILIUM_PH_3__ instead.
This may affect custom scripts if they (or the custom jQuery libraries used) depend on the deprecated APIs.
Note that Trilium polyfills __TRILIUM_PH_0__, __TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__ because they were required by one of our dependencies (the autocomplete).
For more information, consult __TRILIUM_PH_0__the official blog post__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Starting with v0.104.0, some features in Trilium are intentionally disabled in order to reduce the attack surface:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Backend scripts__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which can run processes on the server, access the file system or bypass security measures.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__SQL Console__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which can be used to exfiltrate important data such as the document secret or cause irreparable damage to the database.
To activate any of them, there are three variants:
For the desktop app, go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Security__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and toggle the desired option.

This will prompt a system dialog confirming the change. Note that scripts could potentially call this confirmation dialog as well, make sure to accept it only if enabling any of these features is required.
The settings page will be available for the server-side as well, but the options need to be manually toggled using the other mechanisms described here.
This works by setting a separate configuration file in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Data directory__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
In __TRILIUM_PH_0__config.ini__TRILIUM_PH_1__, set the corresponding option under the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ group.

Trilium supports creating __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes, i.e. notes which allow you to store some programming code and highlight it. Special case is JavaScript code notes which can also be executed inside Trilium which can in conjunction with __TRILIUM_PH_2__Script API__TRILIUM_PH_3__ provide extra functionality.
To go further I must explain basic architecture of Trilium - in its essence it is a classic web application - it has these two main components:
frontend running in the browser (using HTML, CSS, JavaScript) - this is mainly used to interact with the user, display notes etc.
backend running JavaScript code in node.js runtime - this is responsible for e.g. storing notes, encrypting them etc.

So we have frontend and backend, each with their own set of responsibilities, but their common feature is that they both run JavaScript code. Add to this the fact, that we're able to create JavaScript __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and we're onto something.

Saving the note to the database is backend's responsibility, so we immediately pass control to the backend and ask it to create a note. Once this is done, we show the newly created note so that the user can set the task title and maybe some attributes.

So we have a script which will add the button to the toolbar. But how can we execute it? One possibility is to click on the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Execute script__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button. The problem with this is that this UI change is time bound by Trilium runtime so when we restart Trilium, button won't be there.
We need to execute it every time Trilium starts up, but we probably don't want to have to manually click on play button on every start up.

The solution is to give the note the __TRILIUM_PH_0__label__TRILIUM_PH_1__ __TRILIUM_PH_2__ - this is one of the "system" labels which Trilium understands. As you might guess, this will cause all such labeled script notes to be executed once Trilium frontend starts up.
(__TRILIUM_PH_0__ does not work for __TRILIUM_PH_1__Mobile frontend__TRILIUM_PH_2__ - if you want to have scripts running there, give the script __TRILIUM_PH_3__ label).
Runnable code notes (frontend or backend) and saved SQL consoles can optionally have a dedicated __TRILIUM_PH_0__ execute button alongside a description.
To do so, apply the following __TRILIUM_PH_0__labels__TRILIUM_PH_1__:
A __TRILIUM_PH_0__ with the value of the label being displayed as the label of the button.
An optional __TRILIUM_PH_0__ which adds explanatory text beside it.
Starting with Trilium v0.104.0, frontend scripts, backend scripts and render notes benefit from an autocomplete system.

The autocomplete opens automatically while typing a name or after a __TRILIUM_PH_0__.__TRILIUM_PH_1__, or manually by pressing __TRILIUM_PH_2__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_3__+__TRILIUM_PH_4__Space__TRILIUM_PH_5__. Its list looks and works like the __TRILIUM_PH_6__/__TRILIUM_PH_7__ list of a text note: each entry has an icon for its kind (function, property, class…), __TRILIUM_PH_8__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_9__ or __TRILIUM_PH_10__Tab__TRILIUM_PH_11__ inserts the highlighted one and __TRILIUM_PH_12__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_13__ closes it.
In addition to that, the editor will also display syntax errors and warnings such as unreachable code.
If you notice a false positive in regards with the errors/warnings reported or an incorrect or missing API, feel free to __TRILIUM_PH_0__open a issue__TRILIUM_PH_1__ with a code sample.
You can see more scripting with explanation in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Advanced Showcases__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

Trilium Notes does not collect/send any data from the user's installation, i.e. no analytics, no telemetry etc. The data flows only between user controlled / installed applications, without any intermediary.

Trilium periodically queries URL __TRILIUM_PH_0__https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/releases__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to see if there's a new stable version released. (check only, there's no automatic download and/or installation).
Trilium will download spelling dictionaries automatically as needed based on language settings

units.source: This article is a description of the original author of Trilium (zadam) in regards with his own knowledge base.

This page contains description of some of the patterns I use to organize information in my knowledge base. This is meant to give some inspiration of how one might create and structure their knowledge base in general and also specifically in Trilium Notes. It also gives some background and justification for some of the design decisions.

units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns

units.source: Just to be clear, meta patterns are "patterns of patterns", i.e. patterns appearing in other patterns.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns
Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Hierarchical organization of information

units.source: Basic meta pattern is that I sort notes (units of information) into a hierarchy - I have some "top level" notes which represent coarse grained organization, these then split into sub-notes defining finer grained organization and so on. I consider this hierarchical (tree) organization very efficient for organization of large amounts of information. A lot of note taking software (such as Evernote) are frustratingly limited in this regard which limits scalability of the software to large amounts of notes.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Hierarchical organization of information
Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Hierarchical organization of information > Scalability

units.source: It's important to frame the following (meta) patterns with some idea of how large amount of data are we talking about.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Hierarchical organization of information > Scalability

units.source: My rule of thumb for estimation of size of personal knowledge base is that you can reasonably produce around 10 notes a day, which is 3650 in a year. I plan to use my knowledge base long term (with or without Trilium Notes), probably decades so you can easily get to number 100 000 or even more. Right now, my personal knowledge base has around 10 000 notes.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Hierarchical organization of information > Scalability

units.source: 100 000 is a number to which most note taking software doesn't scale well (in both performance and UI). Yet I don't think it's really very much considering a lifetime of knowledge.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Hierarchical organization of information > Scalability
Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Hierarchical organization of information > Lazy hierarchy

units.source: My approach to creating the hierarchy is being lazy - I don't create the structure first and then fill it with notes, instead I create single note for some specific topic and start using this one note. Once the content starts to grow, and I see how __TRILIUM_PH_0__some__TRILIUM_PH_1__ parts could be split out, I move them out into separate sub notes. As an example I have a book review for __TRILIUM_PH_2__The Fellowship of the Ring__TRILIUM_PH_3__:
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Hierarchical organization of information > Lazy hierarchy
Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Hierarchical organization of information > Lazy hierarchy
Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Hierarchical organization of information > Lazy hierarchy

units.source: The note contains basic book info (author, publisher etc.), book highlights with the comments and then overall review. Now it turns out there's far too many book highlights and overall review is also rather long, so I want to change the structure to the following:
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Hierarchical organization of information > Lazy hierarchy
Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Hierarchical organization of information > Lazy hierarchy

units.source: The Fellowship of the Ring       __TRILIUM_PH_0__(still contains basic info)__TRILIUM_PH_1__
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Hierarchical organization of information > Lazy hierarchy
Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Hierarchical organization of information > Lazy hierarchy
Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Hierarchical organization of information > Lazy hierarchy

units.source: If I used standard text file stored in a filesystem I would soon run into an annoying problem that in order to split out the Highlights and Review into sub-notes I would also have to convert __TRILIUM_PH_0__The Fellowship of the Ring__TRILIUM_PH_1__ from text file into directory and split out all sections of the note into sub-notes. Instead, Trilium treats all notes as equal - both leaf notes and inner notes can have both text content which allows me to sub-structure only content which needs it.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Hierarchical organization of information > Lazy hierarchy

units.source: Sorting notes into multiple places in the hierarchy__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Sorting notes into multiple places in the hierarchy

units.source: While organizing the notes into the hierarchy, you very quickly run into a dilemma - your note seem to belong to two places in the hierarchy equally. As an example - you want to make a note about __TRILIUM_PH_0__bash__TRILIUM_PH_1__ - does it belong to "OS / Linux" or "Programming / Scripting languages"? This is actually a false dichotomy forced down by the limits of the basic tree hierarchy - the answer is __TRILIUM_PH_2__of course it belongs to both__TRILIUM_PH_3__. This is the reason why Trilium doesn't use standard tree structure (which requires every note to have exactly one parent), but an extension which allows every note to have several parents, thus effectively allowing it to appear in multiple places in the hierarchy. For lack of better term I call this "cloning". The main problem with this term is that it suggests that each clone must have an original, but here all clones are completely equal - effectively there's no original.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Sorting notes into multiple places in the hierarchy

units.source: In tech lingo, it might be better to describe it as a __TRILIUM_PH_0__hard link__TRILIUM_PH_1__ with an important difference that it is possible to hard link (clone) a directory (inner note).
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Sorting notes into multiple places in the hierarchy
Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Protected notes

units.source: I have Trilium Notes opened non-stop. Sometimes I forget to lock my computer when going to the bathroom. Sometimes I let a friend or family member to use my computer for a minute without supervision. They might click on (running) Trilium and inadvertently see a note I really don't want anybody to see (personal diary, credentials). To cover this, Trilium has a concept of "__TRILIUM_PH_0__protected notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__" - protected note is encrypted and on top of that requires the user to enter the password every 5 minutes which guarantees that such note can be in a readable state only for small amount of time. Working with ordinary (not protected) notes don't require password so you're not bothered by extra security when it's not needed.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Protected notes
Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Archiving notes

units.source: Notes can lose relevancy with time - let's say I switch jobs - all the notes specific to the former employer immediately lose most of its import. This doesn't mean I want to delete these notes though - typically I just want them to somehow deprioritize - in Trilium I would do that by assigning an __TRILIUM_PH_0__inherited__TRILIUM_PH_1__ __TRILIUM_PH_2__label__TRILIUM_PH_3__ __TRILIUM_PH_4__ to the company root note. The main effect of this label is that all the notes from this sub-tree are filtered out from search results (fast search via note autocomplete is my main __TRILIUM_PH_5__navigation approach__TRILIUM_PH_6__). Apart from this, I also typically move such outdated notes to some less prominent place in the hierarchy.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Archiving notes

units.source: I use archivation also for notes which are not very relevant from their creation - an example might be automatically imported reddit comments.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Archiving notes

units.source: Sometimes there's no clear __TRILIUM_PH_0__category__TRILIUM_PH_1__ split between relevant and non-relevant notes, in that case I just create "__TRILIUM_PH_2__OLD__TRILIUM_PH_3__" note with __TRILIUM_PH_4__ label and move all irrelevant notes there. So my credentials note might look something like this:
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Archiving notes
Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Archiving notes
Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Archiving notes

units.source: OLD       __TRILIUM_PH_0__(contains a bunch of notes with credentials for services I don't use anymore)__TRILIUM_PH_1__
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Archiving notes
Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Archiving notes
Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Archiving notes
Patterns of personal knowledge > Meta patterns > Archiving notes
Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Day note

units.source: Every day has its note which contains or references everything related to the given day. Structure looks like this:
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Day note
Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Day note
Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Day note
Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Day note
Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Day note
Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Day note

units.source: Day note serves as a workspace and note inbox at the same time - it's the default location to create a note when I don't have time to think about proper placement. At the end of the day I typically review my day note and clone the notes into suitable locations in the hierarchy.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Day note

units.source: Trilium has this pattern partly built-in - Trilium understands and can create this Year / Month / Day structure semi-automatically (on API call). There's also global keyboard shortcut __TRILIUM_PH_0__ which will create new note in the day note.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Day note

units.source: What notes do I keep under this day note?
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Day note

units.source: TODO list for given day (this can be automated - see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Task Manager__TRILIUM_PH_1__)
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Day note
Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Day note

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__clones__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of notes I created during this day (which kind of represents what I've been working on).
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Day note

units.source: I often clone notes (or sub-trees) of e.g. projects I'm working on at given day so they are at hand
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Day note

units.source: I have some __TRILIUM_PH_0__scripts__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which allow me to track certain daily metrics (like weight). These are saved into one daily "data note" (actually JSON __TRILIUM_PH_2__code note__TRILIUM_PH_3__).
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Day note

units.source: I have other scripts which then help me to visualize these data (see a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Weight Tracker__TRILIUM_PH_1__ example)
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Day note

units.source: I have a script which automatically imports all my comments from reddit into the day note.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Day note

units.source: People are sometimes wondering why. The answer is that I usually put some effort and thought into a comment and that's why I feel it's worth preserving, especially if it can be done automatically.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Day note

units.source: For most notes, this day note placement is __TRILIUM_PH_0__secondary__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and their primary location is somewhere else (e.g. for a book review I've been working on it's __TRILIUM_PH_2__Book / Reviews__TRILIUM_PH_3__, not the day note). So for this pattern to work, ability to __TRILIUM_PH_4__clone__TRILIUM_PH_5__ notes into multiple places is pretty fundamental.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Day note
Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Projects

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Project__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is pretty self-explanatory, for me specifically it also means being long term (years) - an example of a project might be Trilium Notes or university studies. Given their longevity, projects can be large and deep, but their structure is very domain specific, and I don't see any common patterns. What's pretty clear is they are often widely interconnected with other parts of the knowledge base - e.g. university credentials are cloned from "Credentials / University" top level notes and Trilium related blog posts are in "Blog / [Name of the blog] / Trilium".
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Projects

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Epics__TRILIUM_PH_1__ are the same thing as projects, but differ in scope - they are typically several months long and as such are usually placed into a year note (e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_2__2018 / Epics__TRILIUM_PH_3__). Epics are often of work nature (also cloned into work note) and personal (e.g. currently I have large epic for moving to a different city).
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Projects

units.source: I don't have a term for short term projects (typically several days long), but continuing the scrum analogy I might call them __TRILIUM_PH_0__story__TRILIUM_PH_1__. These are often placed directly into day notes and manually moved from one day to another (or place into a month note, e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_2__2018 / 11 - November__TRILIUM_PH_3__).
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Projects
Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Credentials

units.source: I keep all my credentials in the knowledge base, they are sorted into categories - work related, project related, personal per country etc. These notes are of course __TRILIUM_PH_0__protected__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and are often cloned into other places (e.g. project credentials are cloned into the project itself). This is a pretty important advantage compared to traditional tools like KeePass - all the relevant information is centralized into one place without compromising security.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Credentials
Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > People profiles

units.source: This might seem creepy to some, but I keep a profile on most people. It contains pretty standard things like date of birth, contacts, address, but also current and previous employments, their hobbies and worldviews and sometimes even important (IM/mail/meatspace) conversations. Just about everything I find notable. It helps to refresh some basic info before meeting people, especially if you haven't been in touch in a while. It gets pretty awkward to ask for the tenth time where do they work for example, because you keep forgetting it.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > People profiles

units.source: Naturally I have a lot of (extended) family members, friends, acquaintances etc. so I need some way to sort them. My main method is to sort them by social circle (work, high school, sports club etc.), sometimes also by their town of residence. Family __TRILIUM_PH_0__circle__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is still too large so the further organization is by __TRILIUM_PH_2__clan__TRILIUM_PH_3__ (as in "Smiths"). Some people are members of several such circles, so they are just cloned into multiple places.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > People profiles

units.source: For family specifically it's pretty useful to create a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Relation Map__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to visualize relationships:
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > People profiles
Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Books

units.source: Of course, I keep standard "To read" list. I also keep a record on the books I've read - typically one book has one subtree where the root has some basic info like author, page count, publication date, date started, date finished (in the form of __TRILIUM_PH_0__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__). I also write a (private) review and keep list of highlights from Kindle, optionally with some commentary, these are usually stored in sub notes (unless they are pretty short).
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Books

units.source: To keep the list of books manageable, I sort them per year (of reading them), this also gives me some basic overview of "reading performance" for given year. I plan to create a __TRILIUM_PH_0__script__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which would show some timeline chart visualizing book attributes __TRILIUM_PH_2__ - __TRILIUM_PH_3__ to have nicer view of my reading sprints and trends.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Books

units.source: Some specific authors also have their own note which contains cloned book reviews, links to interviews and other related resources.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Books

units.source: I have similar system for movies and TV shows, but not as sophisticated.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Books
Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Personal diary

units.source: This is a place to reflect on events, experiences, new findings etc. This can help you get deeper understanding of your inner self, clarify your thinking and make better decisions as a result.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Personal diary

units.source: I sort personal diary notes directly under __TRILIUM_PH_0__day note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (explained above), but it can be cloned also to e.g. "trip note" (if the diary note is about given trip) or to person's profile (if the person plays a role in the diary note). All my diary notes are __TRILIUM_PH_2__protected__TRILIUM_PH_3__ since they are usually pretty sensitive.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Personal diary
Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Documents

units.source: I keep all my personal documents (ID, passport, education certificates ...) scanned in the knowledge base. They are __TRILIUM_PH_0__synchronized__TRILIUM_PH_1__ across every PC which provides decent backup and makes them available everywhere.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Documents

units.source: Advantage compared to e.g. keeping them in Dropbox or Google Drive is that they are not stored on some 3rd party server and they can be encrypted (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Protected Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__).
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Documents
Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Inventory

units.source: Inventory contains documents and other relevant importation for my important belongings - e.g. for car you can keep the registration card, maintenance record, related costs etc. I also keep inventory for some items personally important to me - mainly computers, phones, cameras and similar electronics. This can be practical at times but also provides sentimental value.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Inventory
Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Topic knowledge base

units.source: This where I store hard "knowledge" - summarized topics and findings from different domains. Topics can range from traditional sciences - physics, history, economy to philosophy, mental models, apps (notes about specific apps I use) etc. Of course this is very subjective - given what I do, my Physics sub-tree is pretty sparse compared to my Programming subtree.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Topic knowledge base
Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Work knowledge base

units.source: I usually keep top level note for the company I currently work at (past jobs are moved elsewhere). I track basic organization of the company (divisions, business units), who is who (__TRILIUM_PH_0__Relation Map__TRILIUM_PH_1__) are again useful for visualization), projects I work at etc.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Work knowledge base

units.source: There's a number of credentials to various company services I need to use. Companies usually have a bunch of complex processes and tools. I record meeting minutes, link to the company wiki (which is usually difficult to find relevant info). In general there's a lot of company specific information I need to know or need have them at hand in a nice structure I can understand. Often it's just copy pasting and reshuffling of existing information into something more understandable for me.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Work knowledge base

units.source: From my experience, keeping this makes me more productive and even more importantly dramatically reduces frustration and stress.
units.context: Patterns of personal knowledge > Patterns > Work knowledge base

units.source: I could probably go on with more patterns (e.g. study notes, travelling), but I think you get the idea. Whatever is important in your life, it probably makes sense to document and track it.
